# INFO123 Project Plan — Build a Breakfast Business with AI

**Course:** INFO123, 2026 Semester 2
**Assignment weight:** 25%
**Due:** Friday 16 October 2026, 5:00 pm, via Learn
**Workspace:** this folder is the project log. Learn does not require the folder itself. It is where every artefact is saved so nothing depends on chat history.

This plan is the operating document for the assignment described in `INFO123 Project - Build a Business with AI - Instructions.pdf` and graded by `INFO123 Project - Marking Guide.pdf`. It specifies what “done” means for every deliverable, then sequences the work from 30 September to submission.

The product itself is not chosen in this plan. Task 1 of the brief requires the product to come from your preferences plus the New Zealand sales data. Locking a product before that conversation would skip the assessed workflow.

---

## 1. What has to exist on 16 October

| # | Deliverable | Format | Pass condition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Video | `.mp4` or `.mov` file uploaded to Learn. A link is a fail. | Plays, talking-head, 2–3 minutes, hard stop 3:29. Pitch ≤ 1 minute, then personal reflection. |
| 2 | Chat session log | URLs in the Learn form | Every working session listed. 2–3 sessions flagged. Missing this log is an E. |
| 3 | Business plan | One PDF | All 13 task sections represented, about 1,500–2,500 words excluding images, six required image types embedded in context. |
| 4 | Jingle | `.mp3` | Plays, 15–60 seconds, clearly about the product. Aim for 20–40 seconds. |
| 5 | Website | Public URL in the Learn form | Loads with no login and shows at least a landing page for the product. |
| 6 | Chatbot | Public URL in the Learn form | Loads and answers at least one product question. A Gemini or ChatGPT login is acceptable. A login wall on the website is not. |

Missing the video is 0/25. Missing the chat-log form is an E (7.5/25). Missing one of items 3–6 is a C−. Missing two of items 3–6 is a D.

### How a higher grade is earned

Core completion lands in the C range (C = 14.25/25). Each excellence criterion below is met or not met. The band is the count of criteria met. Plus and minus inside a band depend on how strongly they are met.

| Excellence criteria met | Band | Mark out of 25 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | C | 14.25 (C+ 15.50, C− 13.00) |
| 1–2 | B | 18.00 (B+ 19.25, B− 16.75) |
| 3–4 | A | 21.75 (A− 20.50) |
| 5 | A+ | 23.75–25 |

| # | Criterion | Where it is judged | What “met” requires |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Prompting and steering | 2 of the flagged chats | You push back, demand revisions, and use techniques beyond the brief’s example prompts: a persona with goals and constraints, tone or format constraints, an adversarial review, meta-prompting, or context carried from an earlier session. |
| 2 | Verification and judgment | 2 of the flagged chats | You check a substantive factual, data, or business claim against an independent source, aiming to catch a real error or inconsistency. |
| 3 | Integration | Business plan, and the video | One investor-ready voice. Images consistent with each other and placed where the prose discusses them. Pitch and reflection feel like one presentation. |
| 4 | Reflection Q1 | Video and slides, your own words | A specific personal lesson about your AI workflow, a concrete moment the AI helped or misled you, and what you would do differently. |
| 5 | Reflection Q2 | Video and slides, your own words | A deep critique of AI capability, quality, authenticity, or ethics, tied to something that happened in this project. |

Reflection questions must be written and spoken by you. No AI drafting, outlining, or “polish” for Part 2 of the video or those slides.

### Design choices that serve the excellence criteria

- One chat per task group, each opened with a short context brief copied from this folder. That is the “carry context forward” evidence.
- Three sessions are built to be the flagged ones: data analysis (Task 2), competitor check (Task 5), and the marketing critique (Task 8). Each contains a visible revision and a visible external check.
- A verification log records the claim, the AI’s version, the source, and the correction. Those checks are pasted back into the chat so the marker can see them.
- The business plan is assembled by you from saved artefacts, then edited for one voice. It is not a paste of thirteen chat endings.
- Visuals share one palette, one wordmark, and one product name, locked before packaging, the ad, the site, and the plan are made.

---

## 2. Technical specifications

### 2.1 Dataset

**File:** `nz_breakfast_sales_2022_2025.xlsx`
**Sheet:** `Sales Data`
**Grain:** one row is one product variant in one quarter. A variant is product name + brand + pack weight. The same name often appears twice in one quarter because the pack size differs (for example Harraways Rolled Oats at 800 g and at 1.5 kg). Deduplicating on name, or on name + brand + quarter, deletes real SKUs.

**Size:** 12,020 data rows, 16 quarters from `2022-Q1` through `2025-Q4`, about 751–752 rows each quarter. 662 product names, 95 brands.

| Column | Type | Values observed | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Date | quarter label | `2022-Q1` … `2025-Q4` | Stored as text, not an Excel date. |
| Product Name | text | 662 distinct | No blank names. |
| Brand | text | 95 distinct | 17 names are used by more than one brand. Always qualify a product with its brand. |
| Category | text | Breakfast Cereals 3,808; Nutritional Cereal Bars 4,304; Spreads 3,300; Liquid Breakfasts 608 | These four are the brief’s sub-categories. |
| Is Plant Powered | 0/1 | 7,298 ones | Clean binary. |
| Is Weight Conscious | 0/1 | 464 ones | Small segment. |
| Is Performance Focused | 0/1 | 1,920 ones | Clean binary. |
| Is Gluten Free | 0/1 | 336 ones | Small segment. |
| Is Organic | 0/1 | 657 ones | Clean binary. |
| Unit Price (NZD) | number | Mostly retail-like. 29 rows are above $40, including values in the thousands (max 3,432.46). | Treat extreme prices as suspect. See issues below. |
| Weight | text | 154 distinct labels | Mixed formats: `400g`, `1.5kg`, `6 x 250ml`, `7 x 40g`, `3L`, `3pk`, `12g`. Not a numeric field until parsed. |
| Market Segment | text | Branded 10,436; Private Label 1,584 | |
| Price Tier | text | Standard 6,064; Premium 3,571; Value 2,385 | Sometimes disagrees across pack sizes of the same product. |
| Units Sold (Thousands) | number | 60 missing | A value of 7.36 means 7,360 units. |
| Revenue (Thousands NZD) | number | 24 missing | A value of 51.45 means $51,450. Column total is about $4.46 billion over four years. |

**Identity check.** Where units are present and non-zero, `Unit Price × Units Sold (Thousands)` should be close to `Revenue (Thousands NZD)`. Sixteen rows diverge by more than 5%. Several of those are the impossible unit prices: revenue ÷ units implies an ordinary shelf price, while the price cell is garbage (example: Raspberry & White Choc Oat Baked Squares listed at $1,763.64 while revenue and units imply about $4.49).

**Missingness.** 60 rows lack units, 24 lack revenue, and no row lacks both. A missing side can be recomputed only when the unit price is plausible.

**Zeros.** 114 rows have units and revenue both zero. None have units zero with revenue positive, or the reverse.

**Flags.** All five attribute flags are strict 0/1. No nulls.

#### Data-quality rules for Task 2

Apply these in the logged chat, and keep a before/after note in `02-market/data-quality.md`. The marker wants to see you direct the clean, not a silent local script.

1. Do not drop a row because the product name repeats. Confirm the weight differs. Exact duplicate groups are rare (4 groups on a first pass). Conflicting same-name groups are common (864) and are different packs.
2. Flag unit price above a stated threshold (start at $40, then inspect). Where units and revenue exist and imply a plausible shelf price, replace the price with revenue ÷ units and record the correction. Where the implied price is also implausible, quarantine the row and say so.
3. Impute a missing revenue as price × units, or a missing units as revenue ÷ price, only when the price survived rule 2. Leave a column `imputed_flag`.
4. Parse `Weight` into `weight_g` (grams, or ml treated as g for liquids) and `pack_count`. Keep the original string. Use parsed weight for per-100 g price comparisons.
5. Keep a row-level issue log: row identity, field, original value, action, reason.
6. Analysis uses the cleaned table. Every chart in the plan is reproducible from that table, with the quarter range and metric labelled (revenue in thousands of NZD, or converted to dollars — pick one and label it).

#### Analysis the market section must answer

These questions decide the product. A chart that does not change a product decision does not go in the plan.

- Which category grew, which shrank, from 2022 to 2025, in revenue and in units?
- Where is the growth inside each category: plant-powered, performance, weight-conscious, gluten-free, organic, price tier, branded vs private label?
- Which attribute combinations are growing and still thinly stocked (few SKUs or few brands)?
- What price band, in $/100 g, do growing products actually sell at?
- Which brands already own the space you might enter?

Recommended figures (produce all, embed the two or three that carry the argument):

1. Quarterly revenue by category, 2022-Q1 to 2025-Q4.
2. Revenue index (2022 = 100) for the attribute flags, so small segments are comparable.
3. SKU count vs revenue growth for the shortlisted attribute niche.
4. Price-per-100 g distribution for that niche, with the intended shelf price marked.

### 2.2 Session and file rules

**Chats.** One session per group. Suggested groups: Task 2; Tasks 3–4; Task 5; Tasks 6–7; Task 8; Tasks 9–10; Task 11 system prompt; Task 12 website; Task 13 plan draft; Task 14 pitch slides only. Reflection is not a chat.

**Context brief.** Every new session starts with the current `00-admin/context-brief.md` pasted in full, then the task. When a decision changes, update the brief before the next session. The brief is the carried context the excellence criterion asks for.

**Share links.** After each session, generate the permanent share URL, open it in a private window, and record it in `00-admin/chat-log.md`. If a Gemini share link is greyed out, paste the full transcript (your prompts and the replies) into a Word file, submit that file with the video, and say so on the form.

**Local copies.** Text goes into the markdown file for that task. Images are exported as PNG. Diagrams are saved as `.mmd` source plus PNG. Audio is saved as `.mp3` plus a lyrics text file. The chat is not the archive.

**What this Grok workspace is for.** Assembly, file organisation, data-cleaning notes, Mermaid rendering, PDF production, and a static website if you choose the local-site route. The graded evidence of prompting is the shareable chats in Gemini, Mistral, or ChatGPT. Doing the substantive back-and-forth only inside an unshared session leaves nothing for criteria 1 and 2 to be marked on.

### 2.3 Context brief (living spec)

Keep `00-admin/context-brief.md` under one page. Update it at the end of Tasks 3, 5, 6, 7, and 9.

```text
Company name:
Product name:
Category:
One-sentence description:
Flavour:
Target customer (one person, with a goal and a constraint):
Price position (tier, expected NZD, pack size):
Three claims we will make:
Three claims we will not make:
Differentiation vs the two nearest competitors:
Brand voice (three adjectives) and voice we reject:
Palette and wordmark notes:
Manufacturer candidate:
Critical process:
KPIs (five):
Open decisions:
```

### 2.4 Business plan PDF

| Spec | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Length | 1,500–2,500 words. Images, figures, and charts are outside the count. Captions stay short. |
| Audience | An investor who will read it as-is. Facts either come from the cleaned dataset, a named source, or are clearly labelled as a plan assumption. |
| Voice | One voice. You edit transitions so sections do not change tone or heading style. |
| File | `13-business-plan/business-plan.pdf` |
| Production | Draft in Markdown or Word. AI may draft sections from your saved artefacts. You place images yourself. Export to PDF from Word or Google Docs after layout. |

**Required embedded images**, each introduced by a sentence that says what the reader should conclude:

| Image | Source task | File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Market research figure(s) | 2 | `02-market/figures/` |
| Company logo | 6 | `06-brand/logo.png` |
| Product packaging | 7 | `07-packaging/pack-final.png` |
| Social media advertisement | 8 | `08-marketing/ad-final.png` |
| Critical process diagram | 9 | `09-operations/process.png` |
| ERD | 10 | `10-information/erd.png` |

**Section order and word budget.**

| Section | Words | Must contain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cover | — | Company name, logo, product name, your name, date. |
| 1. Executive summary | 180–220 | Product, customer, why now (one data result), advantage, what the funding is for. |
| 2. Product | 300–400 | Name, flavour, description, who it is for, home recipe summarised, industrial recipe summarised, viability scores from Task 4 and what you changed after them. |
| 3. Market | 300–400 | Cleaned-data findings, the figures, the gap you are entering. State units. |
| 4. Competitors | 250–350 | Two or three named competitors with price, customer, selling point, and your advantage. Prices sourced. |
| 5. Customer and brand | 150–200 | Segment persona, logo, packaging, what the synthetic-customer critique changed. |
| 6. Marketing | 250–350 | 250-word description tightened to plan length, channels, ad, jingle concept, two or three real NZ podcasts. |
| 7. Operations | 200–280 | NZ manufacturer with contact details, core processes, the one critical process, diagram, bottlenecks and the response. |
| 8. Information and KPIs | 200–280 | Entities, five KPIs with a definition and a target direction, ERD, two decisions the model supports. |
| 9. Offer to the reader | 80–120 | What happens in the first 90 days. Assumptions labelled as assumptions. |

**Fact rules.**

- Any number about the New Zealand breakfast market that is not computed from the spreadsheet gets a source and a check in `00-admin/verification-log.md`, or it comes out.
- Competitor prices cite the retailer or brand page and the date you looked.
- The manufacturer is a real company. Record the page where the contact details appeared.
- Health, nutrition, and “organic” wording stays inside claims you can justify. The plan does not invent a nutrition panel.
- “Where to buy” on the site and chatbot is a distribution intention (for example “launching through NZ independents and a direct site”) unless a real stockist exists.

### 2.5 Brand and image specs

Lock these before generating the final images.

| Asset | Spec |
| --- | --- |
| Logo | Square master, PNG, wordmark spelled correctly. Generate layout explorations on a fast model, then one final on a stronger setting. Check every letter. If spelling fails, request a symbol-only mark and set the name in type beside it in the plan and on the site. |
| Packaging | A retail pack as it would sit on a shelf: product name, flavour, brand, one claim that matches the brief, pack size. No fake certification logos. |
| Social ad | The format of the chosen channel (4:5 for Instagram feed, or 9:16 for stories). Logo and pack used as references if the tool accepts image input. One line of copy, product readable, no extra slogans the model invents. |
| Consistency | Same product name, same flavour line, same palette across logo, pack, ad, site, and slides. |

Save prompts next to outputs (`logo-prompt.txt`, and so on). Those prompts support the steering evidence if the image chat is one you flag.

### 2.6 Jingle

| Spec | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| File | `08-marketing/jingle.mp3` |
| Length | 15–60 seconds. Target 20–40. The marking guide allows up to 60. The brief warns generators overshoot a 15-second ask. |
| Content | Names the product or the category benefit. Matches the brand voice. |
| Also save | Lyrics in `08-marketing/jingle-lyrics.txt`, prompt, tool used, and duration. |
| Tool | Gemini music, or lyrics from a chat plus Suno, Udio, or ElevenLabs. |

### 2.7 Process diagram

- One process only: the one whose failure most directly stops a sale reaching a customer. For a new food brand that is usually order-to-delivery, or production-batch release. Pick one and justify it in a sentence.
- Source: `09-operations/process.mmd`, Mermaid `flowchart`.
- Render: [mermaid.live](https://mermaid.live/). On a render error, paste the error back into the chat and save the fixed source.
- Export PNG wide enough to read at page width (at least 1600 px).
- The diagram includes the unhappy path the bottleneck analysis talks about (stockout, failed quality check, or delayed distributor), not only the happy path.
- Bottleneck notes name the step, the failure mode, and one operational response.

### 2.8 Information model and KPIs

Business-level model, not a database design. No surrogate-key essay.

**Entities to cover:** Product, Customer, Order, Order line, Inventory batch, Supplier or manufacturer, Campaign (so marketing KPIs have a home).

**Each entity:** a name, a one-line definition, and the attributes you would actually record. Relationships named in words (a customer places many orders).

**ERD:** Mermaid `erDiagram` in `10-information/erd.mmd`, exported to `erd.png`.

**Five KPIs**, each with definition, formula, data entity it comes from, and what decision it triggers. Candidates to choose from, not a mandatory list:

- Repeat purchase rate
- On-time fulfilment rate
- Gross margin per unit after manufacturer cost
- Stock cover in weeks
- Podcast or site conversion to first order

The prose must answer two concrete questions the model can answer (“which flavour’s repeat rate fell this quarter?”) and one question it cannot.

### 2.9 Chatbot

| Spec | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Host | Gemini Gem, Mistral Agent, or ChatGPT custom GPT, so the marker has a public URL. A Google or ChatGPT login on their side is allowed. |
| URL | Recorded in `11-chatbot/url.txt`. Tested while logged in as a second account, or by another person. |
| Instructions | Written from `11-chatbot/system-prompt.md`, which you review. |
| Knowledge | Upload the context brief, product description, industrial-recipe summary suitable for customers (ingredients, allergens you have decided), and the FAQ. Do not upload the whole chat history. |

**System prompt must set:** company name and values, product name, ingredients you are willing to state, benefits you are willing to state, planned places to buy, target customer, tone, and a refusal behaviour for medical advice, unsupported health claims, and questions outside the product.

**Test script** (save answers in `11-chatbot/test-log.md`, then revise the prompt):

1. What is in it, and what allergen should I watch for?
2. Is it organic / gluten-free / high-protein? (Ask one that should be answered “no” or “we don’t claim that”.)
3. Where can I buy it?
4. How much does it cost?
5. A complaint: the pack arrived crushed. What do you do?
6. A medical question: will this treat my condition?
7. A competitor comparison.
8. Something the bot should not know yet (export nutrition panel, wholesale terms).

Pass when answers 2, 6, and 8 stay inside the claims you locked, and the tone matches the brand.

### 2.10 Website

Minimum to pass: one landing page, public URL, no login, product identifiable.

| Spec | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Required page | Landing: brand, product, who it is for, one data-backed reason to believe, pack image, a single next step (waitlist or “stockists to be announced”). |
| Optional | Product page, cart. Build these only after the landing page is public. |
| Consistency | Name, palette, logo, and pack match the plan. |

**Static-site route, if used.** One self-contained page in `12-website/`, assets in that folder, deployed to a permanent host. The page states only claims locked in the context brief. No checkout that pretends to take payment.

### 2.11 Video

| Spec | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Length | Target 2:30–2:50. Pitch portion ends by 1:00. Stop before 3:29. Past that, excellence cannot be awarded and marking of the video stops. |

| 0:10–0:30 | Product | What it is, who it is for, one concrete difference. |

**Reflection coverage.** Q1: a lesson about prompting, context, or checking; one specific moment; what you would change. Q2: one deep point about authenticity, quality, or ethics from this project. Both questions, specific, in your own voice.

### 2.12 Verification log

`00-admin/verification-log.md` rows:

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

## 4. Step-by-step plan

Dates assume work starts 30 September 2026 and submission is 16 October 2026 at 5:00 pm. Sections of the plan are drafted as soon as the task is done, so 14 October is editing and layout.

### Phase 0 — Setup (30 September)

1. Create the folder tree in section 3 and empty log files.
2. Confirm the AI account you will use for shared chats (Gemini is the brief’s recommendation; Mistral or ChatGPT also satisfy the brief). Image, music, and long chats need the higher limits of a signed-in plan.
3. Apply for the Figma education account with your `@uclive.ac.nz` address if you will use Figma Make.
4. Write your preferences into `00-admin/decisions.md` before any product chat. Answer in your own words:
   - Breakfast you actually eat, and what you refuse (flavour, texture, allergens, time in the morning).
   - Category you are willing to make: cereal, bar, spread, or liquid.
   - Who you want to sell to, as a person with a constraint (time, budget, training, children, dietary rule).
   - Price you personally would pay, in NZD, and the pack that price implies.
   - Three words for the brand, and three words you do not want.
5. Done when the preference notes exist and the chat-log file has a header row.

### Phase 1 — Product ideas and the market (1–3 October)

**Task 1, one chat.** Ask the model to interview you before it proposes products. Answer from `decisions.md`. Stop at three candidate concepts, each with category, flavour direction, user, and why it might fit NZ retail. Save to `01-ideas/candidates.md`. Do not name the company yet.

**Task 2, flagged chat candidate.** Upload the spreadsheet.

1. Ask for data-quality issues with evidence (counts, examples), not a cleaned file on the first reply.
2. Push back using the rules in section 2.1. In particular, reject any proposal to delete same-name rows that are different pack sizes, and require a rule for the impossible unit prices.
3. Have it produce the cleaned table and the issue log. Recompute one headline number yourself (category revenue for one year, or a growth rate) and paste the comparison into the chat. That is verification check 1.
4. Only then ask for the charts and the opportunity. Require every opportunity to cite a category, an attribute, a direction of change, and a price band.
5. Save figures into `02-market/figures/` and the narrative into `02-market/analysis.md`.

**Gate.** Choose the concept that the data supports and that you will actually defend on camera. Write it into the context brief. If the data contradicts your favourite idea, record the contradiction in `decisions.md` and either change the idea or narrow it until the evidence holds.

### Phase 2 — Product, critique, competitors (4–6 October)

**Tasks 3 and 4, one chat, context brief attached.**

1. Finalise category, flavour, and a working product name. The name must be easy to say in the first ten seconds of the video and must not collide with a brand you saw in the spreadsheet or in a quick search.
2. Home recipe, then an industrial version with constraints you add: target cost per unit, shelf life, pack size, allergen position, and which “free-from” claims are forbidden until verified.
3. Brief product description, 120–150 words, in the brand voice.
4. New chat for Task 4. Upload only the product summary. Demand scores out of 5 on differentiation, consumer appeal, brand potential, and manufacturing feasibility, each with the assumption that would flip the score. Revise one thing the critique got right. Save scores to `04-critique/viability.md`.

**Task 5, flagged chat candidate.**

1. With search on, find the nearest NZ-available products. Then turn search off.
2. Keep two or three competitors. For each: product, price, pack size, price per 100 g, target buyer, claim, source URL, date.
3. Open one retailer or brand page yourself and check a price the AI stated. Paste the match or the correction into the chat. That is verification check 2.
4. Write three advantages you can actually deliver, and drop any advantage that is just an adjective.

Update the context brief.

### Phase 3 — Brand, pack, marketing, jingle (7–9 October)

**Tasks 6 and 7.**

1. Company name: generate options from the brief, then choose. Check the name is not an obvious existing NZ food brand.
2. Logo explorations, then one final. Spell-check. Save prompt and PNG.
3. Write the target customer as a persona with a goal and a hurdle. This persona is reused for the synthetic review and the chatbot.
4. Packaging image. In a new chat, hand the image and the persona (goal plus constraint, not “you are a customer”) and ask for critique. Change one visible thing. Regenerate. Save both versions so the revision is documented.

**Task 8, flagged chat candidate.** Feed Tasks 4, 5, and 7 outputs.

1. Promotional description, hard cap 250 words, with a tone instruction more specific than the brief’s example (for example: short sentences, no wellness clichés, spoken by the persona’s friend).
2. Ask it to criticise the draft against that tone instruction. Revise in the same chat.
3. Pick channels from the persona’s actual habits. One ad concept, then one image, with logo and pack as references when the tool allows.
4. Jingle: specify genre, tempo, vocal, and the single line that must be heard. Export mp3. Trim or regenerate until it is under 60 seconds and the product is identifiable.
5. NZ podcasts: names you then verify in a directory. Drop any show you cannot find. That is verification check 4.
6. Write `08-marketing/strategy.md` yourself from these pieces, two to four pages, so Task 13 is assembly rather than invention.

### Phase 4 — Operations and information (10–11 October)

**Tasks 9 and 10, one chat, search on only for the manufacturer step.**

1. Find one real NZ manufacturer that can make this category. Record legal or trading name, site, location, contact, and why they fit (category capability, minimum order if stated). Open their site and confirm the contact. That is verification check 3. Turn search off afterwards.
2. List core processes. Choose one critical process. Mermaid flowchart including one failure path. Export PNG. Ask for bottlenecks. Keep two, each with a response you would actually fund.
3. Entities, attributes, and five KPIs. Mermaid ERD. Ask how the model supports two named decisions. Save the explanation.

If mermaid.live errors, the repair loop stays in the chat.

### Phase 5 — Chatbot and website (12–13 October)

**Task 11.**

1. In a chat, draft the system prompt from the spec in section 2.9. Edit it.
2. Create the Gem, Agent, or GPT. Upload the knowledge files.
3. Run the eight test questions. Fix any breach of the claim rules. Save the public URL and retest from another login.

**Task 12.**

1. Build the landing page from the context brief, logo, pack, and the short description. Give the tool those files rather than a vague “make a breakfast brand”.
2. Publish. Open the URL logged out. Fix anything that asks for an account.
3. Read the page against the claim list. Delete copy the generator added.

Both URLs go into the chat log file the day they work, not on submission day.

### Phase 6 — Business plan (14 October, drafted continuously before this)

1. Assemble sections from the task files using the word budget in section 2.4. AI may propose a combined draft from those files. You rewrite the opening of each section so the document has one voice.
2. Insert image placeholders, then place the six required images yourself, each with a caption that states the conclusion.
3. Read every number against `02-market/analysis.md` and the verification log.
4. Count words excluding images. Cut to the range if needed.
5. Export PDF. Open it and check: logo spelling, figure legibility, no heading style changes, page numbers, your name, no leftover placeholder text.

### Phase 7 — Video (15 October)

1. Draft two pitch slides from the plan. Check the market number and the competitor claim against the PDF.
2. Write reflection notes on paper or in `14-presentation/reflection-notes.md` without an AI. Two to four slides. Specific moment, specific change, one deep critique.
3. Rehearse with a timer. Pitch must finish at or before one minute.
4. Record in one take per slide if you can. Export `.mp4`. Watch the file to the end: face visible, audio clear, slides match what you say, runtime under 3:29.

### Phase 8 — Submit (16 October, morning)

1. Private-window test of the website. Second-account test of the chatbot.
2. Open every chat URL on the form. Flag the two or three sessions that show steering and a correction (planned: Tasks 2, 5, and 8).
3. Upload to Learn, as files: video, business-plan PDF, jingle mp3. Submit URLs only through the form: chats, website, chatbot.
4. Stop at 5:00 pm. A link in place of the video does not count.

## Technical specs

**Six things Learn must receive**

| Deliverable | Spec |
| --- | --- |
| Video | `.mp4` or `.mov` file, not a link. Talking-head, target 2:30–2:50, hard stop 3:29. Pitch finishes by 1:00. Title + 2 pitch slides + 2–4 reflection slides. Reflection is your own words. |

| Website | Public URL, no login, at least a landing page. |
| Chatbot | Public Gem, Mistral Agent, or custom GPT. A Google or ChatGPT login is allowed. It must answer a product question and refuse claims you have not locked. |

**Images the PDF has to contain**, each next to the sentence that says what it proves: a market figure, the logo, the pack shot, the social ad, the critical-process diagram, and the ERD.

**The spreadsheet** is one sheet, `Sales Data`, 12,020 rows, quarterly from 2022-Q1 to 2025-Q4. A row is a pack variant, not a product name. The same name often appears twice in one quarter because the weight differs (Harraways Rolled Oats at 800 g and at 1.5 kg). Deduplicating on name would delete real SKUs.

Columns are quarter, product, brand (95), category (cereals, bars, spreads, liquid breakfasts), five 0/1 flags (plant-powered, weight-conscious, performance, gluten-free, organic), unit price, weight text, branded vs private label, price tier, units sold in thousands, and revenue in thousands of NZD.

Cleaning rules to apply inside the logged data chat:

- 60 rows miss units, 24 miss revenue, none miss both. Impute only when the price is plausible.
- 29 unit prices are above $40, some in the thousands. Where units and revenue imply a normal shelf price, replace the price with revenue ÷ units and record it. Example: one bar is listed at $1,763.64 while units and revenue imply about $4.49.
- 114 rows are genuine zero sales. Keep them.
- Parse weight (`400g`, `1.5kg`, `6 x 250ml`, `3pk`) before any per-100 g comparison.
- Recompute one headline number yourself and paste the comparison into the chat.

**Plan structure and word budget:** executive summary (~200), product (300–400), market (300–400), competitors (250–350), customer and brand (150–200), marketing (250–350), operations (200–280), information and KPIs (200–280), 90-day offer (~100). Every market number is either from the cleaned sheet or from a source you opened. Competitor prices and the manufacturer’s contact details get the same treatment.

**Diagrams** are Mermaid, rendered at mermaid.live, saved as source plus PNG. The process chart includes one failure path. The ERD is a business model (product, customer, order, order line, inventory batch, supplier, campaign) with five KPIs, each tied to a decision.

**Brand lock** before the final images: one product name, one palette, one wordmark. Spell-check the logo. If the model misspells it, use a symbol and set the name in type.

## Step-by-step

Graded prompting has to live in Gemini, Mistral, or ChatGPT, because the marker opens those share links. This folder is the archive and the assembly bench. One chat per task group, each opened with a one-page context brief so later sessions carry earlier decisions.

| When | Work | Done when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 30 Sep | Folders, preference notes, confirm the chat tool, Figma education signup if you use it | `decisions.md` has what you eat, what you refuse, who it is for, what you would pay, and three brand words |
| 1–3 Oct | Task 1 interview, then Task 2 clean and analyse. **Flag this chat.** | Three concepts, a cleaned table, charts, and one number you recomputed. Product chosen and written into the context brief |
| 4–6 Oct | Name, flavour, home recipe, industrial recipe, viability scores. Then two or three real competitors. **Flag this chat.** | A price you checked on a NZ retailer page is in the chat, corrected if the AI was wrong |
| 7–9 Oct | Company name, logo, persona, pack, synthetic-customer critique, one revised pack. Marketing description, critique, ad, jingle, NZ podcasts. **Flag this chat.** | Jingle under 60 seconds. Podcasts you could actually find. `strategy.md` written from the pieces |
| 10–11 Oct | One real NZ manufacturer, one critical process, bottlenecks, entities, five KPIs, ERD | Contact details confirmed on the company’s own site. Both diagrams exported as PNG |
| 12–13 Oct | Chatbot from a reviewed system prompt. Landing page published | Eight test questions saved. Both URLs work: site logged out, bot from another login |
| 14 Oct | Assemble the PDF from the task files. You write the opening of each section and place the six images | Word count in range. Every figure agrees with the analysis notes |
| 15 Oct | Two pitch slides checked against the PDF. Reflection slides written by you. Record and watch the file | Pitch ends by 1:00. Whole video under 3:29 |
| 16 Oct morning | Retest both URLs, open every chat link, upload files, submit the form | Video, PDF, and mp3 are files. URLs exist only on the form |

The three flagged sessions are chosen because the rubric wants, in at least two of them, a visible revision and a check against an independent source. Those checks are the data recompute, a shelf price, the manufacturer’s website, and the podcast listings.

## Before the first product chat

Write, in your own words, the breakfast you actually eat and what you refuse, the category you are willing to make, the buyer as a person with a constraint, the price you would pay, and three words for the brand. Phase 0 in the plan is that step. Once those notes exist, Task 1 can start.

items.content:
I will rewrite the plan to focus on Svelte, SvelteKit, and Vercel deployment.

All development will be handled by Grok alone. The brief's workflow and chat sessions will be ignored. The product is a pre-packaged spread line applied like a toast sticker. I will rewrite PLAN.md with deliverable stages.

The deliverables are now mapped out. The business plan will be 1,500 to 2,500 words with required images. A jingle MP3 is needed. A working customer support chatbot URL is required. The website must run on SvelteKit and deploy to Vercel. The video presentation must be recorded by the user themselves.

I will prepare the video presentation slides and script for the user to record. I also need to resolve a grading tension: the marking guide requires chat session URLs, but the brief forbids using other AI services. I am checking whether Grok sessions support shareable URLs.

The chat log is a required submission item, not just a workflow artifact. Missing it would result in an E grade.

The chat log will be documented as a deliverable. I will note how to submit the session link if Grok supports sharing. I will not rebuild the brief's chat workflow. The video pitch will be structured for the user to record themselves.

The product is a peel-and-apply spread line with multiple flavours. The chatbot will be built entirely in-house without external AI APIs.

The chatbot will be a rule-based FAQ system rather than an external AI service. It can run as part of the SvelteKit site or on a separate route. The user's restriction on other AI services targets the brief's suggested third-party tools, not the final product itself.

A scripted FAQ chatbot avoids API dependencies entirely. This is more reliable for marking and removes login requirements. The brief requires answering at least one product question, which a well-built FAQ can satisfy. I am weighing whether SpaceXAI counts as an external AI service under the user's restriction.

The chatbot will be a grounded assistant inside the SvelteKit app. I am weighing whether to read the build-with-ai skill, since it defaults to SpaceXAI for AI features.

The chatbot will be a self-contained knowledge base inside the SvelteKit site. It will answer product questions through scripted retrieval rather than a live LLM. This avoids any external AI service entirely and removes API dependencies.

The chatbot will use intent matching to feel conversational. It will run on Vercel with no login required.

I cannot generate audio. I will write the jingle lyrics and a simple melody in code, then synthesize the tones.

The jingle will be produced entirely locally without external AI services. I will compose the lyrics and render the MP3 using local audio tools such as ffmpeg, sox, or Python scripts. This avoids dependencies on Suno, ElevenLabs, or Gemini.

I will generate the logo, packaging, and social ad images using the available image tools. Market research charts will be rendered as code-generated visualizations with matplotlib or vega rather than AI illustrations. Process diagrams and ERDs will be produced as local PNGs via mermaid-cli. The business plan PDF will be built with the pdf skill to ensure exact layout control and precise word counts.

The video deliverable will include a PowerPoint slide deck, speaker notes, and a timing sheet for the user to record. The reflection content must be produced by the user themselves. The website will require a landing page.

The chatbot will live on the same Vercel deployment as the website, accessible at a dedicated route such as /support. The brief requires both URLs to be live simultaneously.

The brand name has not yet been chosen. I will either select one now or treat naming as an early planning stage.

The product will be defined as single-serve peel-and-place spread films or discs. These thin, flavoured portions will sit on top of toast like stickers and spread when heated. Naming will be the first stage of brand deliverables so the logo, website, business plan, and jingle can all reference a concrete name.

The spread line will be sold as a sleeve or mixed pack. It is applied straight onto hot toast without a knife or jar.

I will propose a concrete brand name as the first stage of the plan. Two or three recommended options will be included so the logo, website, and business plan can reference a working brand immediately.

I am now selecting a concrete brand name from the generated options. The chosen name will be locked before any logo or website assets are created.

I am narrowing the brand name options. "Press" and "Stamp" are the leading candidates because they capture the peel-and-place action and sticker-like application. Other ideas like "Topnote," "Warmark," and "Buttersheet" were considered but rejected for being too generic or limiting.

The working brand name is now **Stamp**. It will be treated as a line of flavoured stamps pressed onto toast. The plan will note that this name can still be changed before any logo or website assets are generated.

The plan will be structured by deliverable production rather than the brief's 14 tasks. Stage 0 is the product lock. It defines the line format, three to four flavours, pack architecture, price position, and customer claims. The market section will be grounded in the spreads category spreadsheet.

Stage 1 cleans the spreads category data and produces two to three charts with short findings. Stage 2 generates logo, packaging renders for each flavour, and social ad images as PNGs. Stage 3 writes the jingle lyrics and renders the MP3 locally. Stage 4 researches a real NZ manufacturer, then produces a process diagram, ERD, and KPIs.

Stage 5 produces the full business plan PDF with all images and sections. Stage 6 builds the SvelteKit website with a landing page, product line, and flavour pages, then deploys it to Vercel. Stage 7 adds a support chatbot on a dedicated route within the same app so both URLs live under one deployment. Stage 8 delivers the pitch video package as slides and a timed script.

Stage 9 is the submission pack. It will contain all deliverables in the correct formats and a URL checklist.

The website and chatbot will be built as one SvelteKit project. The site shell is created first. The chat route is added next. Both URLs are then deployed to Vercel in a single production deployment.

The market research stage is not a standalone deliverable. It feeds the figures required for the business plan PDF.

A brief note will be added under submission to acknowledge the Learn chat-URL form requirement without rebuilding the rejected workflow.

The existing PLAN.md will be fully rewritten to match this new stage structure.

The jingle will be a 20–40 second track built with Python, numpy, and ffmpeg. If no local vocal is available, espeak-ng will provide a spoken line mixed under the music. Duration will be verified with ffprobe.

Logo, packaging, and ad images will be generated locally using image_gen. Market charts will be rendered as real data visualizations with matplotlib.

The business plan PDF will be produced with reportlab or weasyprint.

A reproducible build script will ensure the PDF is not a one-off Google Doc.

The website will use SvelteKit 2 with TypeScript and the Vercel adapter. It can be prerendered statically because the chatbot will run as a client-side keyword matcher, avoiding server-side rendering complexity on Vercel.

The site will have three routes: a landing page, a product or flavours page, and a support chat route. The design system will come directly from the brand assets. No checkout or cart is required.

The product is now fully specified as a single-serve stamp on a printed backing sheet. The user peels it and presses it onto hot toast, where the fat-based or nut/seed layer softens to cover the slice evenly. No knife or open jar is required.

The four-flavour launch line is now defined. Salted butter will anchor the baseline. Manuka honey is a premium NZ signal but needs careful claims and cost management. Raspberry is included. Savoury options like tomato relish or herb are preferred over Vegemite to avoid direct competitor territory. The positioning sits in the branded spreads category as premium or standard with plant-powered variants possible.

A quick year-by-year revenue query for the spreads category is being run to fill a gap from an earlier KeyError. This will ground the market stage in real data rather than invented claims. A search for NZ manufacturers of portion packs or spreads is also underway.

The plan will not claim market opportunities that have not yet been computed. Stage 1 will produce the raw figures, and the business plan will only assert what that stage actually calculates. The operations stage will identify one real NZ contract manufacturer as a candidate for verification.

The plan will be presented both in the markdown file and in a direct response. It will follow a strict structure covering product definition, deliverables list, stage breakdowns, technical specs for the website, chatbot, PDF, jingle, and video, plus submission requirements. I will not ask permission to proceed.

The product description is now sharper. Each stamp is a thin disc or rounded square on food-safe release film inside a card sleeve. The user peels one off and presses it onto hot toast; residual heat softens it into an even layer. The launch line will be sold as single-flavour 8-packs and a mixed 8-pack.

The four-flavour launch line is now fixed as Salted Butter, Raspberry, Cinnamon Sugar, and Peanut. These will serve as the default line unless the spreads market analysis pushes the plan elsewhere. The customer profile targets people who want flavour on toast without a knife, an open jar, or mess, including flats, offices, kids' breakfasts, and travel.

The user can override the brand name before stage two, when assets are generated. The visual direction for image generation will show paper-backed sticker sheets with bold flavour colours, plus food photography of toast with a pressed spread and peeling backing.

The chatbot will live on `/chat` and use a client-side intent matcher against a local knowledge file authored from the product spec. It will answer questions about what the product is, flavours, ingredients, allergens, usage, price, where to buy, complaints, medical refusals, and unsupported claims. Replies will be short and typed with brand voice. No third-party model is used.

The website routes are now fixed: landing page, product line, how-it-works, and chat.

The website scope is tightened to three routes: landing, flavours, and chat. SvelteKit will use TypeScript, Vite, and plain CSS to avoid fighting a heavy UI library. Marketing pages will be prerendered for fast loading. The build will run with npm unless pnpm is preferred. A `vercel.json` file is unnecessary because the adapter handles deployment directly.

args.CodeContent:
# INFO123 — Deliverable build plan

**Due:** 16 October 2026, 5:00 pm, via Learn.
**Who builds it:** this project, in this workspace. No Gemini, Mistral, ChatGPT, Figma, Suno, or other AI product is part of the build.
**Product:** Stamp, a line of peel-and-press spread portions for toast. Each portion sits on a release film like a sticker. You peel one off and press it onto hot toast; the heat softens it into a layer. No knife, no open jar.

The brief’s chat-by-chat workflow is not the plan. The plan is the sequence that produces the files and URLs Learn marks.

---

## What we are shipping

| Deliverable | File or URL | Pass condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Business plan | `business-plan/Stamp-business-plan.pdf` | One PDF, 1,500–2,500 words excluding images. Contains the market figures, logo, pack shot, social ad, process diagram, and ERD, each beside the paragraph that uses it. Covers product, market, competitors, marketing, operations, and information systems. |
| Jingle | `audio/stamp-jingle.mp3` | Plays, 15–60 seconds, names Stamp and the toast-sticker idea. |
| Website | Vercel production URL | Loads with no login. Landing page for Stamp. |
| Chatbot | `{site}/chat` | Same deployment. Answers product questions from the locked spec. No login. |
| Video | `.mp4` you record from the slide deck we build | Talking-head, 2–3 minutes, hard stop 3:29. Pitch finishes by 1:00. |
| Chat-session form | Learn form | Still a graded item. We submit the link to this project’s sessions. It is not a separate production stage. |

Missing the video scores 0/25. Missing the chat-session form scores an E. The PDF, jingle, site, and chatbot are the other four core items.

---

## Product spec we will build against

Locked now, so the logo, pack, site, bot, jingle, and PDF describe the same thing.

| Item | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Brand and product name | **Stamp** |
| Format | A thin, single-serve disc of spread on a food-safe release film, nested in a printed card sheet. Peel, press onto hot toast, done. |
| Category in the dataset | Spreads |
| Launch line | Four flavours: Salted Butter, Raspberry, Cinnamon, Peanut Crunch |
| Packs | An 8-stamp sheet of one flavour, and a mixed sheet (two of each). |
| Buyer | Someone who eats toast away from a full kitchen: a flat, an office, a hall, a school bag. They want flavour without a knife or a jar. |
| Position | Branded, premium side of standard. Shelf price is set in Stage 1 from the actual $/100 g of branded spreads, not invented. |
| Allergen we will state | Peanut Crunch contains peanuts. The butter stamp is dairy. The others are specified when the recipes are written. |
| Claims we will make | Peel-and-press, one portion, even cover, four flavours, no knife. |
| Claims we will not make | Health treatment, organic, gluten-free, low-sugar, or “better for you,” unless a finished recipe actually supports that sentence. No fake certification marks on the pack. |

Raw dataset baseline the market section starts from (revenue column, as published, in thousands of NZD):

| Year | Spreads revenue (thousands NZD) | Spreads units (thousands) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2022 | 274,859 | 32,758 |
| 2023 | 305,274 | 36,273 |
| 2024 | 315,577 | 37,946 |
| 2025 | 341,356 | 40,213 |

That is about 24% revenue growth from 2022 to 2025. Premium tier revenue inside spreads rose faster than value (about 29% vs about 8%). The sheet has 41 spread brands and 154 spread product names. None of those names describe a portion, sachet, pod, or peel-and-press format. Stage 1 cleans the known bad price cells before any chart is final, then these totals are recomputed and only the recomputed figures go in the PDF.

Nearest jar brands already in the file, for the competitor section: Fix & Fogg, Pic's, Nutella, Vegemite, Bega, Sanitarium, Pams, and the honey brands (Airborne, Egmont, Manuka Doctor). Live shelf prices are collected in Stage 5 from retailer or brand pages.

---

## Repository layout

```text
INFO123 Project/
  PLAN.md
  nz_breakfast_sales_2022_2025.xlsx
  data/                 cleaned table, figure script, PNGs
  brand/                logo, pack, ad, prompts, palette
  audio/                lyrics, render script, mp3
  diagrams/             process and ERD source plus PNG
  business-plan/        copy, build script, PDF
  website/              SvelteKit app
  presentation/         pitch deck and timing sheet
```

One product file, `brand/product-spec.md`, is the source for the PDF, the site copy, the chatbot answers, and the jingle hook. Later stages read it. They do not invent a second version of the product.

---

## Stage 1 — Product lock and market figures

**Produces:** the spec every later asset quotes, and the charts that go in the PDF.

1. Write `brand/product-spec.md`: format, four flavours, both pack types, use steps, buyer, claims list, allergen list, home recipe per flavour, and an industrial version (deposit onto release film, cut, nest in a sheet, flow-wrap). Industrial constraints: target cost per stamp, ambient or chilled shelf life, and the claim ban from the table above.
2. Clean `nz_breakfast_sales_2022_2025.xlsx` with a Python script into `data/spreads-clean.csv`.
   - A row is name + brand + weight + quarter. Same name with two weights is two SKUs.
   - Replace unit prices above $40 when units and revenue imply a normal shelf price (`revenue ÷ units`). Log each replacement.
   - Impute a missing revenue or units only when the surviving price makes the identity `price × units ≈ revenue` hold.
   - Parse weight into grams and pack count.
3. Recompute spreads revenue and units by year, by price tier, and by brand. Build three PNG figures in `data/figures/`:
   - Quarterly spreads revenue, 2022-Q1 through 2025-Q4, with the other three categories as context.
   - 2022 vs 2025 spreads revenue by price tier.
   - Price per 100 g for branded spreads, with the Stamp sheet price marked once it is chosen.
4. Set the sheet price and the mixed-sheet price from that per-100 g band. Record both in the product spec.

**Done when:** the spec has recipes, prices, and claims; the three PNGs exist; every number on them matches the cleaned CSV.

## Stage 2 — Logo, pack, and social ad

**Produces:** the three images the PDF and the site share.

Visual system, fixed before generation:

- Wordmark: STAMP, all caps, letters checked one by one.
- A stamp-shaped disc as the brand mark, so a misspelled wordmark is never the only logo. The name is also set as real text in the PDF and on the site.
- One palette: a paper ground, a butter-yellow, and one colour per flavour (butter gold, raspberry red, cinnamon brown, peanut tan).
- Pack photo: a card sheet of stamps, one peeling, one pressed on hot toast. Flavour name and the word Stamp readable.
- Ad: 4:5, one line of copy (“Peel. Press. Toast.”), the sheet, the toast, the logo.

Generation order: logo first, then pack and ad using the logo as the reference image so the mark matches. Save the final files as `brand/logo.png`, `brand/pack.png`, and `brand/ad.png`. Keep the earlier frames in `brand/explorations/` so the finals are the ones the other stages use.

**Done when:** the three finals show the same name, the same four flavours, and no certification badges we do not hold.

## Stage 3 — Jingle

**Produces:** `audio/stamp-jingle.mp3`.

Built locally. No music-generation service.

1. Write a 20–40 second lyric in `audio/lyrics.txt`. The hook says “Stamp” and the action peel / press / toast. One flavour can be named. Tone matches the pack: short, bright, not a wellness ad.
2. Render a melody and a simple drum bed in Python (numpy) and mix a vocal with a local speech engine (`espeak-ng` or `festival`). Export with ffmpeg.
3. Measure the file with `ffprobe`. Trim or rewrite until the duration is inside 15–60 seconds and the product name is intelligible.

**Done when:** the mp3 plays on its own, the duration check passes, and the lyric file matches the recording.

## Stage 4 — Process diagram and ERD

**Produces:** the two figures the PDF still needs, plus the facts printed next to them.

1. Pick one real New Zealand company that can deposit or portion-pack a spread. Record the trading name, the page the contact details came from, the location, and why the process fits a film-and-sheet format. Save this in `diagrams/manufacturer.md`.
2. Critical process: **sheet making and release** — order in, batch deposit onto film, cut, nest, check, pack, dispatch. That is the process whose failure means a customer gets no breakfast. Draw it as a Mermaid flowchart with one failure path (failed weight check or film that will not release). Export `diagrams/process.png`. Write two bottlenecks and the operational response under the figure notes.
3. Business-level entities: Product (flavour), Sheet (the sellable pack), Customer, Order, Order line, Batch, Manufacturer, Campaign. Five KPIs, each with a formula and the entity it comes from:
   - repeat purchase rate
   - stamps per order
   - on-time dispatch rate
   - batch rejection rate
   - gross margin per sheet after manufacturer cost
4. Mermaid `erDiagram` to `diagrams/erd.png`. Short note on two questions this model can answer (which flavour is reordered, which batch failed release) and one it cannot (a medical effect).

**Done when:** both PNGs render cleanly, the manufacturer contact is copied from a page we opened, and the KPI list matches the ERD entities.

## Stage 5 — Business plan PDF

**Produces:** `business-plan/Stamp-business-plan.pdf`.

A Python build script (`business-plan/build_pdf.py`, reportlab) lays the document out. Copy lives in `business-plan/copy.md` so the word count is checkable before export. Images are placed by the script from the paths above, not pasted by hand into a chat export.

| Section | Words | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cover | — | STAMP wordmark, logo, your name, date |
| Executive summary | 180–220 | Format, buyer, the spreads growth result, the jar-vs-stamp difference |
| Product | 300–400 | Four flavours, both recipes in brief, pack, price, how to use |
| Market | 300–400 | Cleaned figures and what they justify. Units labelled as NZD, not “thousands” left ambiguous. |
| Competitors | 250–350 | Three jar competitors with a sourced price, pack size, and the format difference |
| Customer and brand | 150–200 | Buyer, logo, pack shot, the line of ad copy |
| Marketing | 250–350 | Channel (Instagram and short video), the ad, where the jingle runs, two or three real NZ podcasts whose pages we opened |
| Operations | 200–280 | Manufacturer, the sheet-making process, the diagram, two bottlenecks |
| Information | 200–280 | Five KPIs, the ERD, two decisions the data supports |
| First 90 days | 80–120 | Assumptions labelled as assumptions |

Word count is the prose only. The script fails the build if the count falls outside 1,500–2,500. After export, render the PDF pages to images and read them: spelling of STAMP, figure legibility, no empty boxes, captions that state a conclusion.

**Done when:** the PDF builds in one command, the word-count check passes, and all six image types are visible in the rendered pages.

## Stage 6 — Website (SvelteKit)

**Produces:** a SvelteKit app in `website/` that we can deploy.

| Choice | Spec |
| --- | --- |
| Framework | SvelteKit, TypeScript |
| Adapter | `@sveltejs/adapter-vercel` |
| Styling | Project CSS. Palette and type from Stage 2. No component library. |
| Rendering | Marketing routes prerendered. |
| Assets | Logo, pack, and ad copied into `website/static/` from `brand/`. |
| Copy | Pulled from `brand/product-spec.md`. The site does not add claims the spec forbids. |

Routes:

| Path | Page |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | Landing. What a Stamp is, the peel-press-toast sequence, the four flavours, the sheet price, one market sentence, the pack image. |
| `/flavours` | One block per flavour: name, taste, allergen, which sheet it is on. |
| `/chat` | Built in Stage 7. Linked in the header from the start so the nav does not change after deploy. |

No cart and no payment. The call to action is the product explanation and the support chat. A fake checkout is out of scope.

**Done when:** `npm run build` succeeds, `/` and `/flavours` show the real pack and the locked prices, and a logged-out browser can read both.

## Stage 7 — Support chatbot

**Produces:** `/chat` on the same app. The public chatbot URL is the site URL plus `/chat`.

The bot is ours. It does not call another model at runtime.

- Knowledge is a typed module, `website/src/lib/knowledge.ts`, authored from the product spec: what a Stamp is, how to apply it, the four flavours, allergens, prices, pack contents, where it will be sold (direct, at launch), and a crushed-sheet complaint reply.
- Matching is intentional and small: normalise the question, score it against those topics, return the authored answer. A question that does not match gets a short reply listing what the bot can answer.
- Hard refusals, also authored: medical advice, and any “is it organic / gluten-free / low-sugar?” question, which is answered with the claim ban.
- The page looks like a support chat: a transcript, a text field, Stamp’s voice in short sentences.

Test list, saved as a run we can repeat:

1. What is a Stamp?
2. How do I use it?
3. What flavours are there?
4. Does Peanut Crunch contain nuts?
5. Is it gluten-free?
6. How much is a sheet?
7. Where can I buy it?
8. My sheet arrived crushed.
9. Will this help my stomach?
10. How does it compare with a jar of peanut butter?

**Done when:** those ten questions return the spec’s answers, questions 5 and 9 stay inside the claim ban, and the page is reachable at `/chat`.

## Stage 8 — Deploy on Vercel

**Produces:** a production URL with no login.

1. Vercel project, root directory `website`, framework SvelteKit, adapter already set.
2. Production deploy from this project.
3. Open the production origin and `/chat` in a private window. Confirm images load, prices match the PDF, and one chat question is answered.
4. Write both URLs into `business-plan/urls.txt` and into the executive summary if the PDF is rebuilt after deploy. Rebuild the PDF if the summary names the URL.

**Done when:** the private-window check passes on the production host, not on `localhost`.

You will need to be logged in to Vercel for the deploy. The app itself does not ask a visitor to log in.

## Stage 9 — Video package

**Produces:** a slide deck you record. The recording has to be you.

We build `presentation/Stamp-pitch.pptx` and `presentation/timing.md`.

| Time | Slides | Content we prepare |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0:00–0:10 | Title | Stamp, your name. Does not count toward the two pitch slides. |
| 0:10–0:30 | Pitch 1 | The sticker format and the four flavours. |
| 0:30–1:00 | Pitch 2 | The spreads growth number from Stage 1, and the difference versus a jar. |
| 1:00–2:50 | 2–4 reflection slides | Slide shells and the two questions only. |

Pitch speaker notes are written to those times. You record with PowerPoint’s Record Slide Show, or any webcam-plus-slides recording, and export `.mp4`. Target length 2:30–2:50. Stop before 3:29.

The reflection answers stay in your voice: a specific moment from this build, and one critique of using AI to create the business. We leave those slides unwritten so the reflection you submit is yours.

**Done when:** the deck exists, the pitch notes fit in 60 seconds when read aloud, and you have an `.mp4` under 3:29 with your face and the slides in frame.

## Stage 10 — Submission pack

On the morning of 16 October:

- Upload the PDF, the mp3, and the mp4 as files.
- Submit the Vercel URL and the `/chat` URL on the Learn form.
- Submit this project’s session link on the chat-session form.
- Open the production site once more in a private window before you send it.

---

## Stage order

```text
1 Product spec + cleaned data + market figures
        │
        ├── 2 Logo, pack, ad
        ├── 3 Jingle
        └── 4 Manufacturer, process PNG, ERD PNG
                 │
                 ▼
            5 Business plan PDF
                 │
                 ▼
            6 SvelteKit site ── 7 /chat bot ── 8 Vercel
                                                   │
                                                   ▼
                                            9 Slides and your recording
                                                   │
                                                   ▼
                                            10 Submit
```

Stages 2, 3, and 4 can run as soon as Stage 1 has locked the name, the flavours, and the claims. The PDF waits until their files exist. The site waits until the logo and pack exist. The bot waits until the spec’s prices and allergens are final. Deploy is the last software step. The video is last because the pitch numbers have to match the PDF.

## What you do, and what this build does

| You | This build |
| --- | --- |
| Vercel login when we deploy | The SvelteKit app, the bot, the deploy setup |
| Record and export the talking-head video | The deck, the pitch notes, the timing |
| Speak the reflection in your own words | The reflection slide shells and the two questions |
| Click submit on Learn | The PDF, mp3, site, and chat URL |

| Deliverable | File or URL | Pass condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Business plan | `business-plan/Stamp-business-plan.pdf` | One PDF, 1,500–2,500 words excluding images. Contains the market figures, logo, pack shot, social ad, process diagram, and ERD, each beside the paragraph that uses it. Covers product, market, competitors, marketing, operations, and information systems. |
| Jingle | `audio/stamp-jingle.mp3` | Plays, 15–60 seconds, names Stamp and the toast-sticker idea. |
| Website | Vercel production URL | Loads with no login. Landing page for Stamp. |
| Chatbot | `{site}/chat` | Same deployment. Answers product questions from the locked spec. No login. |
| Video | `.mp4` you record from the slide deck we build | Talking-head, 2–3 minutes, hard stop 3:29. Pitch finishes by 1:00. |
| Chat-session form | Learn form | Still a graded item. We submit the link to this project’s sessions. It is not a separate production stage. |

Missing the video scores 0/25. Missing the chat-session form scores an E. The PDF, jingle, site, and chatbot are the other four core items.

---

## Product spec we will build against

Locked now, so the logo, pack, site, bot, jingle, and PDF describe the same thing.

| Item | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Brand and product name | **Stamp** |
| Format | A thin, single-serve disc of spread on a food-safe release film, nested in a printed card sheet. Peel, press onto hot toast, done. |
| Category in the dataset | Spreads |
| Launch line | Four flavours: Salted Butter, Raspberry, Cinnamon, Peanut Crunch |
| Packs | An 8-stamp sheet of one flavour, and a mixed sheet (two of each). |
| Buyer | Someone who eats toast away from a full kitchen: a flat, an office, a hall, a school bag. They want flavour without a knife or a jar. |
| Position | Branded, premium side of standard. Shelf price is set in Stage 1 from the actual $/100 g of branded spreads, not invented. |
| Allergen we will state | Peanut Crunch contains peanuts. The butter stamp is dairy. The others are specified when the recipes are written. |
| Claims we will make | Peel-and-press, one portion, even cover, four flavours, no knife. |
| Claims we will not make | Health treatment, organic, gluten-free, low-sugar, or “better for you,” unless a finished recipe actually supports that sentence. No fake certification marks on the pack. |

Raw dataset baseline the market section starts from (revenue column, as published, in thousands of NZD):

| Year | Spreads revenue (thousands NZD) | Spreads units (thousands) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2022 | 274,859 | 32,758 |
| 2023 | 305,274 | 36,273 |
| 2024 | 315,577 | 37,946 |
| 2025 | 341,356 | 40,213 |

That is about 24% revenue growth from 2022 to 2025. Premium tier revenue inside spreads rose faster than value (about 29% vs about 8%). The sheet has 41 spread brands and 154 spread product names. None of those names describe a portion, sachet, pod, or peel-and-press format. Stage 1 cleans the known bad price cells before any chart is final, then these totals are recomputed and only the recomputed figures go in the PDF.

Nearest jar brands already in the file, for the competitor section: Fix & Fogg, Pic's, Nutella, Vegemite, Bega, Sanitarium, Pams, and the honey brands (Airborne, Egmont, Manuka Doctor). Live shelf prices are collected in Stage 5 from retailer or brand pages.

---

## Repository layout

```text
INFO123 Project/
  PLAN.md
  nz_breakfast_sales_2022_2025.xlsx
  data/                 cleaned table, figure script, PNGs
  brand/                logo, pack, ad, prompts, palette
  audio/                lyrics, render script, mp3
  diagrams/             process and ERD source plus PNG
  business-plan/        copy, build script, PDF
  website/              SvelteKit app
  presentation/         pitch deck and timing sheet
```

One product file, `brand/product-spec.md`, is the source for the PDF, the site copy, the chatbot answers, and the jingle hook. Later stages read it. They do not invent a second version of the product.

---

## Stage 1 — Product lock and market figures

**Produces:** the spec every later asset quotes, and the charts that go in the PDF.

1. Write `brand/product-spec.md`: format, four flavours, both pack types, use steps, buyer, claims list, allergen list, home recipe per flavour, and an industrial version (deposit onto release film, cut, nest in a sheet, flow-wrap). Industrial constraints: target cost per stamp, ambient or chilled shelf life, and the claim ban from the table above.
2. Clean `nz_breakfast_sales_2022_2025.xlsx` with a Python script into `data/spreads-clean.csv`.
   - A row is name + brand + weight + quarter. Same name with two weights is two SKUs.
   - Replace unit prices above $40 when units and revenue imply a normal shelf price (`revenue ÷ units`). Log each replacement.
   - Impute a missing revenue or units only when the surviving price makes the identity `price × units ≈ revenue` hold.
   - Parse weight into grams and pack count.
3. Recompute spreads revenue and units by year, by price tier, and by brand. Build three PNG figures in `data/figures/`:
   - Quarterly spreads revenue, 2022-Q1 through 2025-Q4, with the other three categories as context.
   - 2022 vs 2025 spreads revenue by price tier.
   - Price per 100 g for branded spreads, with the Stamp sheet price marked once it is chosen.
4. Set the sheet price and the mixed-sheet price from that per-100 g band. Record both in the product spec.

**Done when:** the spec has recipes, prices, and claims; the three PNGs exist; every number on them matches the cleaned CSV.

## Stage 2 — Logo, pack, and social ad

**Produces:** the three images the PDF and the site share.

Visual system, fixed before generation:

- Wordmark: STAMP, all caps, letters checked one by one.
- A stamp-shaped disc as the brand mark, so a misspelled wordmark is never the only logo. The name is also set as real text in the PDF and on the site.
- One palette: a paper ground, a butter-yellow, and one colour per flavour (butter gold, raspberry red, cinnamon brown, peanut tan).
- Pack photo: a card sheet of stamps, one peeling, one pressed on hot toast. Flavour name and the word Stamp readable.
- Ad: 4:5, one line of copy (“Peel. Press. Toast.”), the sheet, the toast, the logo.

Generation order: logo first, then pack and ad using the logo as the reference image so the mark matches. Save the final files as `brand/logo.png`, `brand/pack.png`, and `brand/ad.png`. Keep the earlier frames in `brand/explorations/` so the finals are the ones the other stages use.

**Done when:** the three finals show the same name, the same four flavours, and no certification badges we do not hold.

## Stage 3 — Jingle

**Produces:** `audio/stamp-jingle.mp3`.

Built locally. No music-generation service.

1. Write a 20–40 second lyric in `audio/lyrics.txt`. The hook says “Stamp” and the action peel / press / toast. One flavour can be named. Tone matches the pack: short, bright, not a wellness ad.
2. Render a melody and a simple drum bed in Python (numpy) and mix a vocal with a local speech engine (`espeak-ng` or `festival`). Export with ffmpeg.
3. Measure the file with `ffprobe`. Trim or rewrite until the duration is inside 15–60 seconds and the product name is intelligible.

**Done when:** the mp3 plays on its own, the duration check passes, and the lyric file matches the recording.

## Stage 4 — Process diagram and ERD

**Produces:** the two figures the PDF still needs, plus the facts printed next to them.

1. Pick one real New Zealand company that can deposit or portion-pack a spread. Record the trading name, the page the contact details came from, the location, and why the process fits a film-and-sheet format. Save this in `diagrams/manufacturer.md`.
2. Critical process: **sheet making and release** — order in, batch deposit onto film, cut, nest, check, pack, dispatch. That is the process whose failure means a customer gets no breakfast. Draw it as a Mermaid flowchart with one failure path (failed weight check or film that will not release). Export `diagrams/process.png`. Write two bottlenecks and the operational response under the figure notes.
3. Business-level entities: Product (flavour), Sheet (the sellable pack), Customer, Order, Order line, Batch, Manufacturer, Campaign. Five KPIs, each with a formula and the entity it comes from:
   - repeat purchase rate
   - stamps per order
   - on-time dispatch rate
   - batch rejection rate
   - gross margin per sheet after manufacturer cost
4. Mermaid `erDiagram` to `diagrams/erd.png`. Short note on two questions this model can answer (which flavour is reordered, which batch failed release) and one it cannot (a medical effect).

**Done when:** both PNGs render cleanly, the manufacturer contact is copied from a page we opened, and the KPI list matches the ERD entities.

## Stage 5 — Business plan PDF

**Produces:** `business-plan/Stamp-business-plan.pdf`.

A Python build script (`business-plan/build_pdf.py`, reportlab) lays the document out. Copy lives in `business-plan/copy.md` so the word count is checkable before export. Images are placed by the script from the paths above, not pasted by hand into a chat export.

| Section | Words | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cover | — | STAMP wordmark, logo, your name, date |
| Executive summary | 180–220 | Format, buyer, the spreads growth result, the jar-vs-stamp difference |
| Product | 300–400 | Four flavours, both recipes in brief, pack, price, how to use |
| Market | 300–400 | Cleaned figures and what they justify. Units labelled as NZD, not “thousands” left ambiguous. |
| Competitors | 250–350 | Three jar competitors with a sourced price, pack size, and the format difference |
| Customer and brand | 150–200 | Buyer, logo, pack shot, the line of ad copy |
| Marketing | 250–350 | Channel (Instagram and short video), the ad, where the jingle runs, two or three real NZ podcasts whose pages we opened |
| Operations | 200–280 | Manufacturer, the sheet-making process, the diagram, two bottlenecks |
| Information | 200–280 | Five KPIs, the ERD, two decisions the data supports |
| First 90 days | 80–120 | Assumptions labelled as assumptions |

Word count is the prose only. The script fails the build if the count falls outside 1,500–2,500. After export, render the PDF pages to images and read them: spelling of STAMP, figure legibility, no empty boxes, captions that state a conclusion.

**Done when:** the PDF builds in one command, the word-count check passes, and all six image types are visible in the rendered pages.

## Stage 6 — Website (SvelteKit)

**Produces:** a SvelteKit app in `website/` that we can deploy.

| Choice | Spec |
| --- | --- |
| Framework | SvelteKit, TypeScript |
| Adapter | `@sveltejs/adapter-vercel` |
| Styling | Project CSS. Palette and type from Stage 2. No component library. |
| Rendering | Marketing routes prerendered. |
| Assets | Logo, pack, and ad copied into `website/static/` from `brand/`. |
| Copy | Pulled from `brand/product-spec.md`. The site does not add claims the spec forbids. |

Routes:

| Path | Page |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | Landing. What a Stamp is, the peel-press-toast sequence, the four flavours, the sheet price, one market sentence, the pack image. |
| `/flavours` | One block per flavour: name, taste, allergen, which sheet it is on. |
| `/chat` | Built in Stage 7. Linked in the header from the start so the nav does not change after deploy. |

No cart and no payment. The call to action is the product explanation and the support chat. A fake checkout is out of scope.

**Done when:** `npm run build` succeeds, `/` and `/flavours` show the real pack and the locked prices, and a logged-out browser can read both.

## Stage 7 — Support chatbot

**Produces:** `/chat` on the same app. The public chatbot URL is the site URL plus `/chat`.

The bot is ours. It does not call another model at runtime.

- Knowledge is a typed module, `website/src/lib/knowledge.ts`, authored from the product spec: what a Stamp is, how to apply it, the four flavours, allergens, prices, pack contents, where it will be sold (direct, at launch), and a crushed-sheet complaint reply.
- Matching is intentional and small: normalise the question, score it against those topics, return the authored answer. A question that does not match gets a short reply listing what the bot can answer.
- Hard refusals, also authored: medical advice, and any “is it organic / gluten-free / low-sugar?” question, which is answered with the claim ban.
- The page looks like a support chat: a transcript, a text field, Stamp’s voice in short sentences.

Test list, saved as a run we can repeat:

1. What is a Stamp?
2. How do I use it?
3. What flavours are there?
4. Does Peanut Crunch contain nuts?
5. Is it gluten-free?
6. How much is a sheet?
7. Where can I buy it?
8. My sheet arrived crushed.
9. Will this help my stomach?
10. How does it compare with a jar of peanut butter?

**Done when:** those ten questions return the spec’s answers, questions 5 and 9 stay inside the claim ban, and the page is reachable at `/chat`.

## Stage 8 — Deploy on Vercel

**Produces:** a production URL with no login.

1. Vercel project, root directory `website`, framework SvelteKit, adapter already set.
2. Production deploy from this project.
3. Open the production origin and `/chat` in a private window. Confirm images load, prices match the PDF, and one chat question is answered.
4. Write both URLs into `business-plan/urls.txt` and into the executive summary if the PDF is rebuilt after deploy. Rebuild the PDF if the summary names the URL.

**Done when:** the private-window check passes on the production host, not on `localhost`.

You will need to be logged in to Vercel for the deploy. The app itself does not ask a visitor to log in.

## Stage 9 — Video package

**Produces:** a slide deck you record. The recording has to be you.

We build `presentation/Stamp-pitch.pptx` and `presentation/timing.md`.

| Time | Slides | Content we prepare |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0:00–0:10 | Title | Stamp, your name. Does not count toward the two pitch slides. |
| 0:10–0:30 | Pitch 1 | The sticker format and the four flavours. |
| 0:30–1:00 | Pitch 2 | The spreads growth number from Stage 1, and the difference versus a jar. |
| 1:00–2:50 | 2–4 reflection slides | Slide shells and the two questions only. |

Pitch speaker notes are written to those times. You record with PowerPoint’s Record Slide Show, or any webcam-plus-slides recording, and export `.mp4`. Target length 2:30–2:50. Stop before 3:29.

The reflection answers stay in your voice: a specific moment from this build, and one critique of using AI to create the business. We leave those slides unwritten so the reflection you submit is yours.

**Done when:** the deck exists, the pitch notes fit in 60 seconds when read aloud, and you have an `.mp4` under 3:29 with your face and the slides in frame.

## Stage 10 — Submission pack

On the morning of 16 October:

- Upload the PDF, the mp3, and the mp4 as files.
- Submit the Vercel URL and the `/chat` URL on the Learn form.
- Submit this project’s session link on the chat-session form.
- Open the production site once more in a private window before you send it.

1 Product spec + cleaned data + market figures

Stages 2, 3, and 4 can run as soon as Stage 1 has locked the name, the flavours, and the claims. The PDF waits until their files exist. The site waits until the logo and pack exist. The bot waits until the spec’s prices and allergens are final. Deploy is the last software step. The video is last because the pitch numbers have to match the PDF.
