Two overlapping circular arcs from the same family form a closed blob instead of an S, because both bowls are full circles stacked.

The sweep is creating nearly full circles. The terminal caps are landing in the center where the arcs meet, closing the counters into teardrops instead of opening them outward. The upper arc must not complete the right side.

The upper bowl should open toward the lower right. The terminal belongs at the upper right as the hook's end, with the stroke continuing from the lower left into the lower bowl.

The top terminal should sit on the right. The upper bowl opens toward the right. The spine crosses to the right. The lower bowl opens toward the left. The bottom terminal should sit on the left.

Sans-serif S terminals are often horizontal. The bottom terminal may extend right as well. Monoline rounded S terminals are round blobs on the right and left.

The fix is to draw one continuous thick path shaped like an S hook, rather than two separate circles. The upper arc should sweep about 180–200 degrees and stop at the middle-left without curling back up on the right side of the upper bowl, leaving the gap facing right.

The upper arc should run counter-clockwise from the east terminal around the north and west, ending at the south. This leaves the right side of the circle undrawn, so the opening faces southeast and creates a proper S upper bowl.

A 220-degree sweep ends at the lower-left of the circle, not the bottom. A 260-degree sweep from the terminal to the bottom would let the stroke flow into the crossbar.

The upper arc will run from -10° to -250°. That end point sits slightly left of the bottom and still faces right, so the stroke can continue into the lower bowl. The lower bowl will be an 180-degree rotation of the upper arc.

The lower arc's start point is the 180-degree rotation of the upper arc's end. Whether these two points meet depends on whether that rotated point overlaps the upper shape.

Two rotated arcs only join if their endpoints sit at the rotation center. Otherwise they overlap and form an 8. The upper arc must end exactly at the center so the lower arc can begin there.

The endpoint of the upper arc must land exactly at the letter center. The lower arc is a 180-degree rotation of the upper shape, so it also ends at that same center point. With open ends, the two stroke outlines meet there. The stroke thickness creates a line segment perpendicular to the tangent, with length twice the half-width.

The two strokes must form a single continuous ribbon. The tangents align through the 180-degree rotation, and the cross-sections coincide at the letter center. Caps should be omitted at that join so the outlines can be unioned cleanly. The next step is to compute the exact angles so the arc endpoint lands precisely on the center.

The letter center is at (120, 169), but the upper circle center is at (120, 120). The distance between them is only 49, while the radius is 72. That means the center cannot sit on the centerline circle.

The upper center must be moved so it lies exactly one radius away from the letter center. The lower center will be its 180-degree reflection across that point. The outer top of the upper bowl should sit near y=0, and the outer bottom of the lower bowl should sit near the baseline.

With a half-width of 50, the upper center is at (120, 109). The radius becomes 59.5. This places the top of the upper bowl at y=0 and the bottom near y=338.

The stroke width of 100 is larger than the centerline radius of 59.5, leaving only a 9.5-unit inner counter. That is very narrow and resembles a Toundra counter. The total letter width would be about 219, which is narrower than the target 240. To fix this, the upper center can be shifted horizontally so the distance to the letter center remains exactly one radius.

Shifting the upper center left to keep the radius at 70 pushes the outer left edge off the canvas. The next attempt uses a half-width of 50 and a radius of 64.

A half-width of 50 and radius of 64 still pushes the outer left edge off the canvas. A half-width of 52 is impossible because the vertical distance to the letter center exceeds the radius. The only viable solution is a zero horizontal offset, which sets the radius to exactly (169 − half)/2. That yields an outer radius of (169 − half)/2 + half, giving a total width of 169 + half.

A half-width of 55 yields a width of 224, which is close to the target of 240. However, the inner radius becomes only 2, leaving the counter as a hairline that would make the bowl solid and hide its opening. The arc must reach the letter center while spanning the full height, so the two constraints are incompatible.

The circular arc is overconstrained. It cannot satisfy all geometry requirements at once.

A cubic spine is the better approach. It can be sampled and filtered for proper curvature radius. The design will be verified against the stroke width and margin.

A cubic centerline will be sampled and filtered for minimum curvature above 60, stroke width of 100, and full containment within the 240×338 canvas. The design uses one cubic from the terminal to the letter center, with its 180-degree rotation completing the S. The terminal is fixed at (170, 75) and the center at (120, 169); control points B1 and B2 will be tuned. Candidates will be checked for self-intersection before saving.

The two cubic halves will meet with C1 continuity at the letter center. The arrival tangent of the first curve and the departure tangent of its 180-degree rotation are identical, so no sharp corner is created.

The 180-degree rotation automatically preserves C1 continuity, so no extra join logic is needed. Curvature will be computed with the standard cubic formula, rejecting any design whose minimum radius drops below 58 units.

The upper bowl should arch high and left, with the terminal slightly below the crown. In Toundra, letter tops align at the cap line.

The centerline crown is fixed at y=52 and the left extreme at x=52. The terminal is placed at (185, 90) so the stroke reaches x=235, yielding a width near 235. A visual grid will sample control points to find a valid cubic curve.

Offset outlines will be generated and validated by checking for self-intersection via simple polygon segment tests. The ribbon code will only accept designs that pass both the minimum curvature check and the self-intersection test. A reference S from a rounded font was considered but set aside in favor of matching Toundra weight. A single carefully chosen cubic curve is now being tested.

import math
from pathlib import Path

def cubic(p0, p1, p2, p3, n=80):
    pts=[]
    for i in range(n+1):
        t=i/n
        u=1-t
        x=u**3*p0[0]+3*u**2*t*p1[0]+3*u*t**2*p2[0]+t**3*p3[0]
        y=u**3*p0[1]+3*u**2*t*p1[1]+3*u*t**2*p2[1]+t**3*p3[1]
        pts.append((x,y))
    return pts

def derivs(p0,p1,p2,p3,t):
    # B' and B''
    u=1-t
    # first deriv
    dx=3*u*u*(p1[0]-p0[0])+6*u*t*(p2[0]-p1[0])+3*t*t*(p3[0]-p2[0])
    dy=3*u*u*(p1[1]-p0[1])+6*u*t*(p2[1]-p1[1])+3*t*t*(p3[1]-p2[1])
    ddx=6*u*(p2[0]-2*p1[0]+p0[0])+6*t*(p3[0]-2*p2[0]+p1[0])
    ddy=6*u*(p2[1]-2*p1[1]+p0[1])+6*t*(p3[1]-2*p2[1]+p1[1])
    return dx,dy,ddx,ddy

def min_radius(p0,p1,p2,p3,n=200):
    m=1e9
    mt=None
    for i in range(n+1):
        t=i/n
        dx,dy,ddx,ddy=derivs(p0,p1,p2,p3,t)
        sp=dx*dx+dy*dy
        if sp<1e-8:
            return 0,t
        kappa=abs(dx*ddy-dy*ddx)/(sp**1.5)
        rad=1/kappa if kappa>1e-8 else 1e9
        if rad<m:
            m,mt=rad,t
    return m,mt

def ribbon(points, radius):
    normals=[]
    for i,p in enumerate(points):
        if i==0:
            dx,dy=points[1][0]-p[0], points[1][1]-p[1]
        elif i==len(points)-1:
            dx,dy=p[0]-points[i-1][0], p[1]-points[i-1][1]
        else:
            dx=points[i+1][0]-points[i-1][0]
            dy=points[i+1][1]-points[i-1][1]
        mag=(dx*dx+dy*dy)**0.5 or 1
        normals.append((-dy/mag, dx/mag))
    def cap(point, normal, sign):
        nx,ny=normal
        tx,ty=sign*ny, -sign*nx
        steps=[]
        for i in range(16):
            ang=math.pi*i/15
            c,s=math.cos(ang), math.sin(ang)
            steps.append((point[0]+(nx*c+tx*s)*radius, point[1]+(ny*c+ty*s)*radius))
        return steps
    left=[(p[0]+n[0]*radius, p[1]+n[1]*radius) for p,n in zip(points,normals)]
    right=[(p[0]-n[0]*radius, p[1]-n[1]*radius) for p,n in zip(points,normals)]
    outline=left+cap(points[-1], normals[-1], 1)+list(reversed(right))+cap(points[0], normals[0], -1)
    return outline

def seg_intersect(a,b,c,d):
    def cross(p,q,r):
        return (q[0]-p[0])*(r[1]-p[1])-(q[1]-p[1])*(r[0]-p[0])
    d1,d2=cross(c,d,a), cross(c,d,b)
    d3,d4=cross(a,b,c), cross(a,b,d)
    if d1*d2<0 and d3*d4<0:
        return True
    return False

def simple(poly):
    n=len(poly)
    # skip adjacent segments
    for i in range(n):
        a,b=poly[i], poly[(i+1)%n]
        for j in range(i+2, n):
            if i==0 and j==n-1:
                continue
            c,d=poly[j], poly[(j+1)%n]
            if seg_intersect(a,b,c,d):
                return False
    return True

def rot(p,c):
    return (2*c[0]-p[0], 2*c[1]-p[1])

C=(120,169)
half=50

candidates=[
    ("a", (180,96), (150,24), (28,70), C),
    ("b", (176,100), (176,36), (36,80), C),
    ("c", (184,110), (150,28), (24,120), C),
    ("d", (170,88), (120,20), (24,100), C),
    ("e", (188,120), (188,40), (40,90), C),
    ("f", (176,92), (130,18), (18,140), C),
]

items=[]
for label,p0,b1,b2,c in candidates:
    rad,t=min_radius(p0,b1,b2,c)
    pts=cubic(p0,b1,b2,c, n=60)
    # full centerline
    lower=[rot(p,C) for p in reversed(pts[:-1])]
    full=pts+lower
    # drop duplicate center
    outline=ribbon(full, half)
    ok=simple(outline)
    print(f"{label} minR={rad:.1f} at t={t:.2f} simple={ok} bbox x {min(p[0] for p in outline):.0f}-{max(p[0] for p in outline):.0f} y {min(p[1] for p in outline):.0f}-{max(p[1] for p in outline):.0f}")
    items.append((label, outline, rad, ok))

# svg sheet
chunks=[]
for i,(label,outline,rad,ok) in enumerate(items):
    ox=i*300
    d="M "+" L ".join(f"{x+ox:.1f} {y:.1f}" for x,y in outline)+" Z"
    chunks.append(f'<path d="{d}" fill="#00483C"/>')
    chunks.append(f'<text x="{ox+8}" y="390" font-size="28" fill="#00483C" font-family="sans-serif">{label} r{rad:.0f} {"ok" if ok else "X"}</text>')

svg=f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 -20 {300*len(items)} 420"><rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#E24BFF"/>{"".join(chunks)}</svg>'
Path("/tmp/s2.svg").write_text(svg)
print("svg")

def letter_s():
    """Capital S. Two circular bowls joined on a shared tangent, then scaled to the cap height.

    The stroke lands near the 110 stem. The inner radius stays large enough that the
    counters still read as an S after the scale.
    """
    import math

    half = 72.0
    radius = 84.0
    t0 = math.radians(-60)
    t1 = t0 - math.radians(220)

    def xy(r, t):
        return (r * math.cos(t), r * math.sin(t))

    steps = 150
    ts = [t0 + (t1 - t0) * i / steps for i in range(steps + 1)]
    outer = [xy(radius + half, t) for t in ts]
    inner = [xy(radius - half, t) for t in reversed(ts)]

    def semicap(t, bulge):
        mx, my = xy(radius, t)
        nx, ny = math.cos(t), math.sin(t)
        tx, ty = -math.sin(t) * bulge, math.cos(t) * bulge
        pts = []
        for i in range(1, 20):
            ang = math.pi * i / 20
            pts.append(
                (
                    mx + (nx * math.cos(ang) + tx * math.sin(ang)) * half,
                    my + (ny * math.cos(ang) + ty * math.sin(ang)) * half,
                )
            )
        return pts

    # Counterclockwise travel. Cap the terminal only; the join is the shared edge.
    upper = outer + inner + list(reversed(semicap(t0, 1)))
    join = xy(radius, t1)
    lower = [(2 * join[0] - x, 2 * join[1] - y) for x, y in upper]
    all_pts = upper + lower
    minx = min(p[0] for p in all_pts)
    miny = min(p[1] for p in all_pts)
    maxx = max(p[0] for p in all_pts)
    maxy = max(p[1] for p in all_pts)
    scale = CAP / (maxy - miny)

    def path(points):
        coords = " L ".join(
            f"{(x - minx) * scale:.1f} {(y - miny) * scale:.1f}" for x, y in points
        )
        return f"M {coords} Z"

    return (maxx - minx) * scale, "fill", path(upper) + " " + path(lower)

1→"""STAMP wordmark in the Toundra lettering system.

The Toundra wordmark is a custom drawing, not a retail font. These capitals
follow its measured construction: cap height 338, stem 110, counter 20,
semicircular outer arches, round feet. Manrope is the text face and is not
used for the wordmark.

Output is one filled even-odd path, all capitals.
"""
10→
from pathlib import Path

INK = "#00483C"
CAP = 338
STEM = 110
GAP = 20
TRACK = 18

OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "wordmark.svg"
20→

def pill(cx, top, bot, half):
    """Closed vertical capsule. half is the radius (half the width)."""
    return (
        f"M {cx - half:.1f} {top + half:.1f} "
        f"A {half:.1f} {half:.1f} 0 0 1 {cx + half:.1f} {top + half:.1f} "
        f"L {cx + half:.1f} {bot - half:.1f} "
        f"A {half:.1f} {half:.1f} 0 0 1 {cx - half:.1f} {bot - half:.1f} Z"
    )
30→

def letter_s():
    """Capital S. Two circular bowls joined on a shared tangent, then scaled to the cap height.

    The stroke lands near the 110 stem. The inner radius stays large enough that the
    counters still read as an S after the scale.
    """
    import math

40→    half = 72.0
    radius = 84.0
    t0 = math.radians(-60)
    t1 = t0 - math.radians(220)

    def xy(r, t):
        return (r * math.cos(t), r * math.sin(t))

    steps = 150
    ts = [t0 + (t1 - t0) * i / steps for i in range(steps + 1)]
50→    outer = [xy(radius + half, t) for t in ts]
    inner = [xy(radius - half, t) for t in reversed(ts)]

    def semicap(t, bulge):
        mx, my = xy(radius, t)
        nx, ny = math.cos(t), math.sin(t)
        tx, ty = -math.sin(t) * bulge, math.cos(t) * bulge
        pts = []
        for i in range(1, 20):
            ang = math.pi * i / 20
60→            pts.append(
                (
                    mx + (nx * math.cos(ang) + tx * math.sin(ang)) * half,
                    my + (ny * math.cos(ang) + ty * math.sin(ang)) * half,
                )
            )
        return pts

    # Counterclockwise travel. Cap the terminal only; the join is the shared edge.
    upper = outer + inner + list(reversed(semicap(t0, 1)))
70→    join = xy(radius, t1)
    lower = [(2 * join[0] - x, 2 * join[1] - y) for x, y in upper]
    all_pts = upper + lower
    minx = min(p[0] for p in all_pts)
    miny = min(p[1] for p in all_pts)
    maxx = max(p[0] for p in all_pts)
    maxy = max(p[1] for p in all_pts)
    scale = CAP / (maxy - miny)

    def path(points):
80→        coords = " L ".join(
            f"{(x - minx) * scale:.1f} {(y - miny) * scale:.1f}" for x, y in points
        )
        return f"M {coords} Z"

    return (maxx - minx) * scale, "fill", path(upper) + " " + path(lower)


def letter_t():
    # Capital T: a round-ended bar on a round-footed stem.
90→    bar_h = 78
    width = 250
    stem_x = (width - STEM) / 2
    d = (
        f"M {bar_h / 2:.1f} 0 "
        f"H {width - bar_h / 2:.1f} "
        f"A {bar_h / 2:.1f} {bar_h / 2:.1f} 0 0 1 {width - bar_h / 2:.1f} {bar_h:.1f} "
        f"H {stem_x + STEM:.1f} "
        f"V {CAP - STEM / 2:.1f} "
        f"A {STEM / 2:.1f} {STEM / 2:.1f} 0 0 1 {stem_x:.1f} {CAP - STEM / 2:.1f} "
100→        f"V {bar_h:.1f} "
        f"H {bar_h / 2:.1f} "
        f"A {bar_h / 2:.1f} {bar_h / 2:.1f} 0 0 1 {bar_h / 2:.1f} 0 Z"
    )
    return width, "fill", d


def letter_a():
    # Arch, closed pill counter, opening between the feet.
    w = 240
110→    r_top = w / 2
    r_foot = STEM / 2
    notch_top = 214
    d = (
        f"M 0 {r_top:.1f} "
        f"A {r_top:.1f} {r_top:.1f} 0 0 1 {w:.1f} {r_top:.1f} "
        f"L {w:.1f} {CAP - r_foot:.1f} "
        f"A {r_foot:.1f} {r_foot:.1f} 0 0 1 {w - STEM:.1f} {CAP - r_foot:.1f} "
        f"L {w - STEM:.1f} {notch_top + GAP / 2:.1f} "
        f"A {GAP / 2:.1f} {GAP / 2:.1f} 0 0 0 {STEM:.1f} {notch_top + GAP / 2:.1f} "
120→        f"L {STEM:.1f} {CAP - r_foot:.1f} "

1→"""Flat brand applications for Stamp.

The wordmark is the only mark. Fields use the acid purple that replaces
Toundra's lime, with Toundra's forest green as the ink. Supporting type is
Manrope, the text face of that identity.
"""

from pathlib import Path

10→from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

import build_wordmark

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
FONT = ROOT / "fonts"
PURPLE = (226, 75, 255)  # #E24BFF
INK = (0, 72, 60)  # #00483C


20→def font(weight: int, size: int) -> ImageFont.FreeTypeFont:
    return ImageFont.truetype(str(FONT / f"Manrope-{weight}.ttf"), size)


def render_wordmark(width: int) -> Image.Image:
    build_wordmark.main()
    svg = ROOT / "wordmark.svg"
    png = ROOT / "explorations" / "wordmark-ink.png"
    png.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    import subprocess
30→
    subprocess.check_call(
        [
            "magick",
            "-background",
            "none",
            str(svg),
            "-resize",
            f"{width}x",
            f"PNG32:{png}",
40→        ]
    )
    return Image.open(png).convert("RGBA")


def recolor(image: Image.Image, rgb: tuple[int, int, int]) -> Image.Image:
    image = image.convert("RGBA")
    pixels = image.load()
    for y in range(image.height):
        for x in range(image.width):
50→            _, _, _, alpha = pixels[x, y]
            if alpha:
                pixels[x, y] = (*rgb, alpha)
    return image


def paste_center(canvas: Image.Image, sprite: Image.Image, y: int) -> None:
    x = (canvas.width - sprite.width) // 2
    canvas.paste(sprite, (x, y), sprite)

60→
def text_center(draw: ImageDraw.ImageDraw, y: int, text: str, face, fill, canvas_w: int) -> int:
    box = draw.textbbox((0, 0), text, font=face)
    w, h = box[2] - box[0], box[3] - box[1]
    draw.text(((canvas_w - w) / 2, y), text, font=face, fill=fill)
    return h


def lockup(background, ink, width, height, mark_width, path: Path) -> None:
    canvas = Image.new("RGB", (width, height), background)
70→    mark = recolor(render_wordmark(mark_width), ink)
    paste_center(canvas, mark, (height - mark.height) // 2)
    canvas.save(path, quality=95)


def pack() -> None:
    w, h = 1200, 1600
    canvas = Image.new("RGB", (w, h), INK)
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(canvas)
    mark = recolor(render_wordmark(980), PURPLE)
80→    top = 120
    paste_center(canvas, mark, top)
    y = top + mark.height + 48
    meta = font(600, 32)
    meta_h = text_center(draw, y, "80 g    ·    8 stamps    ·    12 months", meta, PURPLE, w)
    bar = 180
    flavour = font(800, 92)
    sub = font(500, 44)
    name_h = draw.textbbox((0, 0), "Salted Butter", font=flavour)[3]
    sub_h = draw.textbbox((0, 0), "salted butter spread", font=sub)[3]
90→    block = name_h + 28 + sub_h
    region_top = y + meta_h + 36
    region_bot = h - bar
    flavour_y = region_top + (region_bot - region_top - block) / 2
    text_center(draw, flavour_y, "Salted Butter", flavour, PURPLE, w)
    text_center(draw, flavour_y + name_h + 28, "salted butter spread", sub, PURPLE, w)
    draw.rectangle((0, h - bar, w, h), fill=PURPLE)
    tag = font(800, 48)
    box = draw.textbbox((0, 0), "Peel. Press. Toast.", font=tag)
    th = box[3] - box[1]
100→    text_center(draw, h - bar + (bar - th) / 2 - 8, "Peel. Press. Toast.", tag, INK, w)
    canvas.save(ROOT / "pack.png")


def ad() -> None:
    w, h = 1080, 1350
    canvas = Image.new("RGB", (w, h), PURPLE)
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(canvas)
    mark = recolor(render_wordmark(940), INK)
    paste_center(canvas, mark, 430)
110→    y = 430 + mark.height + 64
    text_center(draw, y, "Peel. Press. Toast.", font(800, 54), INK, w)
    text_center(draw, h - 120, "Toast spreads", font(600, 28), INK, w)
    canvas.save(ROOT / "ad.png")


def main() -> None:
    lockup(PURPLE, INK, 1800, 1000, 1500, ROOT / "logo.png")
    lockup(INK, PURPLE, 1800, 1000, 1500, ROOT / "explorations" / "wordmark-on-green.png")
    pack()
120→    ad()
    print("wrote logo, pack, ad")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

The S is indeed twisted. The color scheme should be dark purple on light purple, matching the dark green and lime green inspiration.

The terminals curl inward like a spiral. The spine is diagonal. The upper counter opens as a spiral hook. I will rebuild the S with heavy geometric lines. It will use round semicircular terminals and horizontal arms. The openings will be simple notches instead of curls.

The S should be a block built from the same vocabulary: semicircular arches, round feet, and narrow pill-shaped counters. The top arm will be a horizontal bar with a round right end, roughly 78 to 100 units thick. The left and right sides connect downward from the middle bar. The bottom arm will have a round left end. The terminals must point straight right, not inward.

The bottom terminal should point left horizontally. The spine must be flatter and more horizontal than diagonal. Both bowls will stay upright and symmetrical. The top arm will be about 90 units thick to match the heavy stems. I am weighing how to keep the counters open enough to read without looking weak.

The S will be drawn as an explicit outline with round corners, not two spiraling arcs. The body will consist of three horizontal masses connected on alternating sides. The top terminal will be a horizontal stadium pill on the right side. I will build it with SVG arcs using the same quarter and semicircle joins as the other letters.

I am sketching the centerline path for the S. The outline will use mostly straight segments with large round corners instead of spirals. I have begun mapping coordinates, starting from a right terminal at (180, 55) and moving left to (70, 55), then down the left side toward (55, 140).

The S will be 246 by 338 units. The outer silhouette will trace clockwise from the top-left. The top edge will be flat with rounded corners. Only the top arm will carry a semicircular cap. The path will descend along the underside of that arm into the upper counter. The left end of the upper counter will be a small round notch, matching the gap between the A's feet.

The outline now traces the full clockwise path through the upper and lower counters. Arm thickness is set to 98 units and counter gaps to 22. This yields a total height of exactly 338. The vertical bands are mapped from top to bottom.

The upper counter opens on the right side. Its left edge sits at x = 108, just past the 110-unit left stem. The lower counter opens on the left side. Its right edge sits at x = 136, just before the 110-unit right stem.

The upper counter is a horizontal slot. Its left end is round. The right end is flat. The top arm's semicircular cap blocks the counter from reaching the right edge.

The top-left corner will be a large rounded arch, similar to the A's arch. A full semicircle there would make the shape look like an n, so the radius must stay smaller than half the arm height.

The S terminals will be semicircular ends with radius equal to half the arm thickness. A 98-unit arm gives a 49-unit terminal radius. This is smaller than the A's 120-unit arch, so the S will read as a more terminal-like shape.

The outer spine curves will use radii of 80 to 100 so the S reads as round as the other letters. I am now drafting a stadium-style construction with a 250-unit width, 96-unit arms, and 25-unit gaps.

The terminal radius is fixed at 48. The upper counter’s left edge will sit at x = 118, with its round end centered at (118, 108.5). I am now tracing the clockwise outline with explicit points.

The vertical bands are now fixed at y = 96, 121, 217, and 242. The upper counter’s left end is being placed at x = 122 with a radius of 12.5.

The upper counter’s left end will bulge left into the stem. A counterclockwise SVG arc sweep is required for that inward curve.

The upper counter’s left edge is fixed at x = 122.5 so the stem stays roughly 110 units thick. After the notch, the outline runs right along the middle bar to its right edge instead of continuing up to the top arm. The clockwise path now starts from the top-left corner.

The right side of the middle and bottom bars will form one continuous outer edge. The bottom-right corner will be a quarter-round arc. The outline descends from the middle bar down to the corner radius before sweeping into the bottom.

The outer bottom-right corner will use a quarter-circle radius of 80. The left side will stay solid because the upper counter does not open that way.

The bottom-right corner will use a quarter-circle radius of 80. The left side will stay solid because the upper counter does not open that way.

The lower counter opens on the left side. Its right end is the closed end. The clockwise path now runs from the bottom arm up the left edge to the top-left corner.

The lower counter’s right edge is fixed at x = 127.5 so the stem stays roughly 110 units wide. The notch will bulge right, and the clockwise arc from the bottom of the notch to its top must sweep toward positive x.

The lower counter notch will use a clockwise sweep to bulge right. The upper counter notch will use a counterclockwise sweep to bulge left. The top-right terminal cap will bulge right.

The bottom-left terminal cap will use a clockwise sweep to bulge left. The top-left corner will be a quarter-circle arc with radius 48, matching the arm thickness.

The top-left corner will use a counterclockwise quarter-circle arc from (0, 48) to (48, 0). The bottom-right corner will be a quarter-circle arc from (250, 290) to (202, 338).

The bottom-right corner will use a quarter-circle arc with radius 48. The left side of the middle bar will run from the notch up to the top-left corner. The lower counter opens on the left, so the outer path must not block that opening.

The left edge of the middle bar will run only from the top-left corner down to the upper counter. It will not continue below that point, leaving the lower opening empty. The corner at the junction will be slightly rounded so it does not look broken.

The top-right corner at (w, y2) will be rounded with a radius of 36 to 48 so it matches the other letters. The upper counter’s right edge stays open.

A 40-unit radius on the outer shoulder would swallow into the middle bar. The S should follow a heavy grotesque style, with continuous curves where the spine meets each bowl. I will render this geometric version first and adjust corner radii if it looks too blocky.

The 48-unit terminal radius is slightly heavier than the T’s 39, but that suits the S’s 96-unit arms. The user complained the S looks twisted, so a clean geometric outline is the priority. If the shape still feels too blocky, the outer corners can be softened.

The S will be built as a superellipse with two rectangular bites taken out, similar to geometric ultra-bolds. A softer variant with 70-unit outer corner radii is also being considered. The color scheme is shifting from lime and forest green to dark purple on light purple, using analogous tones instead of the previous vivid magenta-purple.

The user wants a dark purple on light purple scheme, analogous to the previous dark green on lime. The previous #E24BFF was a mid-light vivid purple, which does not fit this dark-on-light relationship. Lime #DCFC0C is yellow-green and very bright, so the light purple base should be a much lighter, more saturated purple.

Forest green is a dark teal-green, so the dark purple must be a deep purple rather than a dark green. The light purple base should be a very bright, high-chroma purple such as #E7B6FF or #F3C6FF to match lime’s highlighter-like brightness.

Dark purple candidates are being narrowed to deep purples like #3D0066 and #240033. The lime green’s hue is green-yellow, while the forest green is a dark cyan-green, so the two colors do not share an identical hue.

I will extract the HSL values of the Toundra colors to design a purple pair with matching lightness and saturation. The dark-on-light contrast must stay strong, similar to the 9:1 ratio between lime and forest green. I am now testing specific highlighter purples such as #E8B4FF, #D9A0FF, and #F0C2FF.

The light purple must be highly saturated and bright, not pastel-washed. #E24BFF is too dark for a true light purple, so lighter highlighter purples like #E59BFF and #EEA8FF are now being tested. Dark purple candidates are shifting to visible purple inks such as #4A0066 and #3D0052.

Dark purple candidates are now narrowed to deep purples like #3B0764 and #2E1065. I will compute contrast ratios and create a visual strip to compare the purple pair against the lime/forest relationship. The logo lockup will use dark purple on light purple, while the pack reverse will swap them, following the same dark-on-light structure as Toundra.

The recolor function replaces every non-zero alpha pixel, so the SVG fill color does not affect the PNGs. I will still update the SVG ink to dark purple for correctness. The logo, pack, and ad assets are being mapped to the new light-purple-on-dark-purple palette.

I will update identity.md and PLAN.md. I am designing two S variants: a blocky version with 48-unit corner radii, and a softer one with 70-unit radii for a more rounded spine that sits better with A and T. I will render comparison strips before committing the applications.

A third S variant is being considered: a superellipse with horizontal terminals and a narrower middle bar, to avoid looking like a digital 8-segment display. The SVG path coordinates for the top arm and right edge are being double-checked to ensure the shape renders cleanly.
The S is curling like a spiral, and the ink is still forest green. I’ll redraw S as a straight capital and switch the pair to dark purple on light purple.
Toundra lime lightness is 0.52, not 0.

python3 << 'PY'
def rel_lum(rgb):
    def f(c):
        c=c/255
        return c/12.92 if c<=0.04045 else ((c+0.055)/1.055)**2.4
    r,g,b=rgb
    return 0.2126*f(r)+0.7152*f(g)+0.0722*f(b)
def contrast(a,b):
    L1,L2=rel_lum(a),rel_lum(b)
    lighter,darker=max(L1,L2),min(L1,L2)
    return (lighter+0.05)/(darker+0.05)
def hsl(rgb):
    r,g,b=[c/255 for c in rgb]
    mx,mn=max(r,g,b),min(r,g,b)
    l=(mx+mn)/2
    if mx==mn:
        h=s=0
    else:
        d=mx-mn
        s=d/(2-mx-mn) if l>0.5 else d/(mx+mn)
        if mx==r: h=((g-b)/d)%6
        elif mx==g: h=(b-r)/d+2
        else: h=(r-g)/d+4
        h*=60
    return round(h,1), round(s,3), round(l,3)

# lime L is 0.52 because it's a mid HSL value with huge chroma.
# Match that: purple hue ~280, S~1, L~0.52, and dark purple L~0.14 S high.
def from_hsl(h,s,l):
    c=(1-abs(2*l-1))*s
    x=c*(1-abs((h/60)%2-1))
    m=l-c/2
    if 0<=h<60: rp,gp,bp=c,x,0
    elif h<120: rp,gp,bp=x,c,0
    elif h<180: rp,gp,bp=0,c,x
    elif h<240: rp,gp,bp=0,x,c
    elif h<300: rp,gp,bp=x,0,c
    else: rp,gp,bp=c,0,x
    return tuple(round((v+m)*255) for v in (rp,gp,bp))

cands=[]
for h in (275, 280, 285, 290, 295):
    for l in (0.50, 0.54, 0.58, 0.62):
        light=from_hsl(h,1,l)
        for dh,dl in ((h,0.14),(h,0.16),(h,0.18),(h-8,0.16),(h,0.20)):
            dark=from_hsl(dh%360, 0.85, dl)
            c=contrast(light,dark)
            if 6.5 <= c <= 10:
                cands.append((c, light, dark, hsl(light), hsl(dark)))
# unique-ish print best spread
seen=set()
for c,light,dark,hl,hd in sorted(cands, key=lambda x: abs(x[0]-9.0))[:18]:
    key=(light,dark)
    if key in seen: continue
    seen.add(key)
    print(f"#{light[0]:02X}{light[1]:02X}{light[2]:02X} on #{dark[0]:02X}{dark[1]:02X}{dark[2]:02X}  c={c:.2f} light{hl} dark{hd}")

from pathlib import Path

def letter_s_geom(arm=96, gap=25, w=250, corner=52):
    """Upright geometric S. Terminals are horizontal round caps, counters are straight slots."""
    cap = bw.CAP
    # fit vertical: 3*arm + 2*gap should equal cap. Scale arm/gap if needed.
    raw = 3*arm + 2*gap
    scale = cap / raw
    arm *= scale
    gap *= scale
    r = arm / 2
    rg = gap / 2
    y1 = arm
    y2 = arm + gap
    y3 = y2 + arm
    y4 = y3 + gap
    y5 = cap
    # notch centers: stem about 110
    cx_u = 110 + rg  # upper notch bulges left, leftmost = cx_u - rg = 110
    cx_l = w - 110 - rg  # lower notch bulges right, rightmost = cx_l + rg = w-110
    rc = min(corner, r)  # outer corner radius, cannot exceed arm/2 if we stay in the arm
    # Use rc for the four outer corners. Terminal caps use r (full arm).
    # Top-left and bottom-right use rc. Top-right and bottom-left terminals use r.
    d = (
        f"M {rc:.1f} 0 "
        f"H {w - r:.1f} "
        f"A {r:.1f} {r:.1f} 0 0 1 {w - r:.1f} {y1:.1f} "
        f"H {cx_u:.1f} "
        f"A {rg:.1f} {rg:.1f} 0 0 0 {cx_u:.1f} {y2:.1f} "
        f"H {w - rc:.1f} "
        f"A {rc:.1f} {rc:.1f} 0 0 1 {w:.1f} {y2 + rc:.1f} "
        f"V {y5 - rc:.1f} "
        f"A {rc:.1f} {rc:.1f} 0 0 1 {w - rc:.1f} {y5:.1f} "
        f"H {r:.1f} "
        f"A {r:.1f} {r:.1f} 0 0 1 {r:.1f} {y4:.1f} "
        f"H {cx_l:.1f} "
        f"A {rg:.1f} {rg:.1f} 0 0 0 {cx_l:.1f} {y3:.1f} "
        f"H {rc:.1f} "
        f"A {rc:.1f} {rc:.1f} 0 0 1 0 {y3 - rc:.1f} "
        f"V {rc:.1f} "
        f"A {rc:.1f} {rc:.1f} 0 0 1 {rc:.1f} 0 Z"
    )
    return w, d

# Check arc directions by rendering a few corner sizes and arm weights
variants = [

def measure(path, name):
    im = Image.open(path).convert("RGB")

    bright = a.sum(axis=2) > 400
    # flood background from edges using scipy? do a simple mask: bright pixels connected to border
    h, w = bright.shape
    bg = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)
    # seed border bright
    from collections import deque
    q = deque()
    for x in range(w):
        if bright[0, x]:
            bg[0, x] = True; q.append((0, x))
        if bright[h-1, x] and not bg[h-1, x]:
            bg[h-1, x] = True; q.append((h-1, x))
    for y in range(h):
        if bright[y, 0] and not bg[y, 0]:
            bg[y, 0] = True; q.append((y, 0))
        if bright[y, w-1] and not bg[y, w-1]:
            bg[y, w-1] = True; q.append((y, w-1))
    while q:
        y, x = q.popleft()
        for ny, nx in ((y+1,x),(y-1,x),(y,x+1),(y,x-1)):
            if 0<=ny<h and 0<=nx<w and bright[ny, nx] and not bg[ny, nx]:

    hole = bright & ~bg

I will refine the packaging labels with drawings matching the inspo brand style. Each flavour will get a distinct but consistent colour scheme. I will present the results.

The Toundra style uses uniform strokes, rounded caps, and simple geometric shapes. I will draw a smiling sun, stacked clouds, and pine trees. Each flavour gets its own colour scheme.

Greenhouse icons will use a shared ground line and one ink colour. Tray labels will feature small line icons beside product names. Salted Butter will get a simple food icon like a butter pat or toast slice.

Salted Butter will use a scored butter block with salt crystals. Raspberry will be a clustered circle with a leaf. Stampmite will avoid the Marmite jar and instead show a toast with a dark spread or a grain stalk.

Stampmite will use a geometric barley ear or a peeled disc icon to avoid Marmite trade dress. Peanut will be a simple two-lobe outline. The pack label will either show a row of small icons under the name, or a single scene in the middle, matching the tote and tray layouts.

The pack label will use a meta row, a large empty middle for the line drawing scene, and a bottom bar with Peel. Press. Toast. Each flavour gets a light and dark pair in the same highlighter-to-deep-ink relationship, shifted by hue. Salted Butter will use butter yellow and deep gold-brown.

Salted Butter will use a warm yellow light and a deep amber dark. Raspberry will use a bright pink light and a deep red dark. Stampmite will use a caramel light and a dark brown dark.

Stampmite will keep the original purple as the house colour while packs use distinct flavour schemes. It will use a warm amber highlighter on dark espresso or a malty red-brown pair. Peanut will use tan and golden tones. All flavour palettes must remain clearly distinct from one another.

The colour palettes are now fixed. Salted Butter will use a bright yellow field and a dark chocolate-gold ink. Raspberry will use a pink field and a wine dark. Stampmite will keep the house purple as both light and dark. Peanut will use an orange field and a deep brown ink.

All four packs will follow the dark-field, light-type layout used on the wax bean pouch. Line icons will render in the light colour so they remain readable against the dark background.

I will draw the icons as SVGs and rasterize them with ImageMagick, then recolor them to match each pack’s palette. Each flavour will get a compact centered scene between the meta row and the flavour name, or between the name and the bottom bar. The style uses uniform 8-pixel strokes with round caps and joins, a shared ground line, and no shading or fills.

I will keep the icon style friendly but avoid cartoon overload. Each scene will feature one face only. The Salted Butter icon will show a scored butter block with salt crystals and a toast stamp. The Raspberry icon will use overlapping circle clusters for the berries and a simple leaf. The Stampmite icon will be a geometric stem with alternating grain ovals.

A shared micro icon row for peel, press, and toast will appear on every pack for consistency. The flavour-specific drawing will sit beside it to provide differentiation.

I will verify contrast for readability. The four packs will be presented as a contact sheet and saved individually in the brand explorations folder.

The existing pack.png will remain untouched until the user picks a winner. I will create a new build script to render all four flavour packs and a contact sheet, then hand-draw the icon SVGs with simple paths.

The Peanut icon will be drawn as two overlapping circles forming a stadium outline. The subtitle text for each pack is being verified against the product specs: salted butter spread, raspberry spread, yeast extract spread, and peanut spread.

A test render will run before composing the full packs. The contact sheet will be saved to brand/explorations/flavour-packs.png. All icons will share a 520 by 300 viewBox. Toundra strokes will be thin, around two and a half to three percent of icon height.

"""Flavour pack fronts.

Same layout, same line-icon drawings, a different bright/dark pair per flavour.
The drawings follow the Toundra icon style: one even stroke, round caps, no fill.
"""

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

import build_wordmark

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
FONT = ROOT / "fonts"
OUT = ROOT / "explorations" / "flavours"
STROKE = 14

# Bright field-colour and dark ink, one pair per flavour.
# Same roles as the house purple: light type on a dark pack.
FLAVOURS = [
    {
        "id": "butter",
        "name": "Salted Butter",
        "sub": "salted butter spread",
        "light": (255, 214, 64),
        "dark": (74, 48, 0),
    },
    {
        "id": "raspberry",
        "name": "Raspberry",
        "sub": "raspberry spread",
        "light": (255, 70, 122),
        "dark": (92, 16, 48),
    },
    {
        "id": "stampmite",
        "name": "Stampmite",
        "sub": "yeast extract spread",
        "light": (226, 75, 255),
        "dark": (59, 7, 100),
    },
    {
        "id": "peanut",
        "name": "Peanut",
        "sub": "peanut spread",
        "light": (255, 140, 48),
        "dark": (78, 36, 8),
    },
]


def font(weight: int, size: int) -> ImageFont.FreeTypeFont:
    return ImageFont.truetype(str(FONT / f"Manrope-{weight}.ttf"), size)


def svg_wrap(body: str, w: int = 640, h: int = 360) -> str:
    return (
        f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 {w} {h}" '
        f'fill="none" stroke="#000" stroke-width="{STROKE}" '
        f'stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">{body}</svg>'
    )


def icon_butter() -> str:
    # A scored butter block, three salt crystals, a shared ground line.
    return svg_wrap(
        """
        <line x1="48" y1="300" x2="592" y2="300"/>
        <rect x="176" y="108" width="288" height="168" rx="28"/>
        <line x1="272" y1="108" x2="272" y2="196"/>
        <line x1="368" y1="108" x2="368" y2="196"/>
        <path d="M118 92 l18 -28 l18 28 l-18 28 z"/>
        <path d="M498 78 l14 -22 l14 22 l-14 22 z"/>
        <path d="M536 132 l12 -18 l12 18 l-12 18 z"/>
        """
    )


def icon_raspberry() -> str:
    # Overlapping circles for the drupelets, two simple leaves.
    circles = [
        (320, 168, 36),
        (276, 146, 32),
        (364, 146, 32),
        (258, 196, 30),
        (320, 214, 32),
        (382, 196, 30),
        (292, 112, 26),
        (348, 112, 26),
    ]
    dots = "\n".join(
        f'<circle cx="{cx}" cy="{cy}" r="{r}"/>' for cx, cy, r in circles
    )
    leaves = """
        <path d="M292 96 C250 70 214 78 196 108 C236 112 268 108 292 96"/>
        <path d="M348 96 C390 70 426 78 444 108 C404 112 372 108 348 96"/>
        <line x1="320" y1="86" x2="320" y2="108"/>
    """
    return svg_wrap(dots + leaves + '<line x1="48" y1="300" x2="592" y2="300"/>')


def icon_stampmite() -> str:
    # Two barley ears. Geometric grains, no jar silhouette.
    def ear(cx: int) -> str:
        parts = [f'<line x1="{cx}" y1="48" x2="{cx}" y2="292"/>']
        for i, y in enumerate(range(78, 268, 28)):
            side = -1 if i % 2 == 0 else 1
            grain = 22 - i
            parts.append(
                f'<ellipse cx="{cx + side * 26}" cy="{y}" rx="{grain}" ry="12" '
                f'transform="rotate({side * -38} {cx + side * 26} {y})"/>'
            )
        parts.append(f'<path d="M{cx} 48 l-16 -20 M{cx} 48 l16 -20"/>')
        return "\n".join(parts)

    return svg_wrap(ear(230) + ear(410) + '<line x1="48" y1="300" x2="592" y2="300"/>')


def icon_peanut() -> str:
    # Two shell outlines with a seam. Lobes are plain curves, not a character.
    one = """
        <g transform="translate(210 168)">
          <path d="M0 -108
                   C46 -108 62 -78 54 -46
                   C78 -34 96 0 90 40
                   C84 86 48 112 0 112
                   C-48 112 -84 86 -90 40
                   C-96 0 -78 -34 -54 -46
                   C-62 -78 -46 -108 0 -108 Z"/>
          <path d="M-36 -20 C-10 -8 10 16 34 28"/>
        </g>
    """
    two = """
        <g transform="translate(430 188) scale(0.78)">
          <path d="M0 -108
                   C46 -108 62 -78 54 -46
                   C78 -34 96 0 90 40
                   C84 86 48 112 0 112
                   C-48 112 -84 86 -90 40
                   C-96 0 -78 -34 -54 -46
                   C-62 -78 -46 -108 0 -108 Z"/>
          <path d="M-36 -20 C-10 -8 10 16 34 28"/>
        </g>
    """
    return svg_wrap(one + two + '<line x1="48" y1="300" x2="592" y2="300"/>')


ICONS = {
    "butter": icon_butter,
    "raspberry": icon_raspberry,
    "stampmite": icon_stampmite,
    "peanut": icon_peanut,
}


def render_svg(svg: str, width: int, name: str) -> Image.Image:
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = OUT / f"{name}.svg"
    png = OUT / f"{name}-ink.png"
    path.write_text(svg)
    subprocess.check_call(
        ["magick", "-background", "none", str(path), "-resize", f"{width}x", f"PNG32:{png}"]
    )
    return Image.open(png).convert("RGBA")


def recolor(image: Image.Image, rgb: tuple[int, int, int]) -> Image.Image:
    image = image.convert("RGBA")
    pixels = image.load()
    for y in range(image.height):
        for x in range(image.width):
            if pixels[x, y][3]:
                pixels[x, y] = (*rgb, pixels[x, y][3])
    return image


def wordmark(width: int) -> Image.Image:
    build_wordmark.main()
    png = ROOT / "explorations" / "wordmark-ink.png"
    subprocess.check_call(
        [
            "magick",
            "-background",
            "none",
            str(ROOT / "wordmark.svg"),
            "-resize",
            f"{width}x",
            f"PNG32:{png}",
        ]
    )
    return Image.open(png).convert("RGBA")


def text_center(draw, y, text, face, fill, canvas_w) -> int:
    box = draw.textbbox((0, 0), text, font=face)
    w, h = box[2] - box[0], box[3] - box[1]
    draw.text(((canvas_w - w) / 2, y), text, font=face, fill=fill)
    return h


def pack_image(flavour: dict, mark: Image.Image) -> Image.Image:
    w, h = 1200, 1600
    light, dark = flavour["light"], flavour["dark"]
    canvas = Image.new("RGB", (w, h), dark)
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(canvas)
    sprite = recolor(mark, light)
    x = (w - sprite.width) // 2
    canvas.paste(sprite, (x, 108), sprite)
    y = 108 + sprite.height + 36
    text_center(draw, y, "80 g    ·    8 stamps    ·    12 months", font(600, 30), light, w)
    icon = recolor(render_svg(ICONS[flavour["id"]](), 560, flavour["id"]), light)
    icon_y = y + 88
    canvas.paste(icon, ((w - icon.width) // 2, icon_y), icon)
    name_y = icon_y + icon.height + 28
    name_h = text_center(draw, name_y, flavour["name"], font(800, 84), light, w)
    text_center(draw, name_y + name_h + 18, flavour["sub"], font(500, 40), light, w)
    bar = 168
    draw.rectangle((0, h - bar, w, h), fill=light)
    tag = font(800, 46)
    box = draw.textbbox((0, 0), "Peel. Press. Toast.", font=tag)
    th = box[3] - box[1]
    text_center(draw, h - bar + (bar - th) / 2 - 6, "Peel. Press. Toast.", tag, dark, w)
    return canvas


def main() -> None:
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    mark = wordmark(980)
    packs = []
    for flavour in FLAVOURS:
        image = pack_image(flavour, mark)
        path = OUT / f"{flavour['id']}.png"
        image.save(path)
        packs.append(image)
        print("wrote", path)
    # Contact sheet, two by two, so the four fronts can be compared.
    thumb_w = 480
    gap = 24
    thumbs = []
    for image in packs:
        thumb = image.resize((thumb_w, int(thumb_w * image.height / image.width)), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
        thumbs.append(thumb)
    sheet = Image.new("RGB", (thumb_w * 2 + gap * 3, thumbs[0].height * 2 + gap * 3), (244, 244, 244))
    for i, thumb in enumerate(thumbs):
        col, row = i % 2, i // 2
        sheet.paste(thumb, (gap + col * (thumb_w + gap), gap + row * (thumb.height + gap)))
    sheet_path = ROOT / "explorations" / "flavour-packs.png"
    sheet.save(sheet_path)
    print("wrote", sheet_path)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def text_center(draw, y, text, face, fill, canvas_w) -> int:
    box = draw.textbbox((0, 0), text, font=face)
    w, h = box[2] - box[0], box[3] - box[1]
    draw.text(((canvas_w - w) / 2, y), text, font=face, fill=fill)
    return h


def pack_image(flavour: dict, mark: Image.Image) -> Image.Image:
    w, h = 1200, 1600
    light, dark = flavour["light"], flavour["dark"]
    canvas = Image.new("RGB", (w, h), dark)
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(canvas)
    sprite = recolor(mark, light)
    x = (w - sprite.width) // 2
    canvas.paste(sprite, (x, 108), sprite)
    y = 108 + sprite.height + 36
    text_center(draw, y, "80 g    ·    8 stamps    ·    12 months", font(600, 30), light, w)
    icon = recolor(render_svg(ICONS[flavour["id"]](), 560, flavour["id"]), light)
    icon_y = y + 88
    canvas.paste(icon, ((w - icon.width) // 2, icon_y), icon)
    name_y = icon_y + icon.height + 28
    name_h = text_center(draw, name_y, flavour["name"], font(800, 84), light, w)
    text_center(draw, name_y + name_h + 18, flavour["sub"], font(500, 40), light, w)
    bar = 168
    draw.rectangle((0, h - bar, w, h), fill=light)
    tag = font(800, 46)
    box = draw.textbbox((0, 0), "Peel. Press. Toast.", font=tag)
    th = box[3] - box[1]
    text_center(draw, h - bar + (bar - th) / 2 - 6, "Peel. Press. Toast.", tag, dark, w)
    return canvas


def main() -> None:
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    mark = wordmark(980)
    packs = []
    for flavour in FLAVOURS:
        image = pack_image(flavour, mark)
        path = OUT / f"{flavour['id']}.png"
        image.save(path)
        packs.append(image)
        print("wrote", path)
    # Contact sheet, two by two, so the four fronts can be compared.
    thumb_w = 480
    gap = 24
    thumbs = []
    for image in packs:
        thumb = image.resize((thumb_w, int(thumb_w * image.height / image.width)), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
        thumbs.append(thumb)
    sheet = Image.new("RGB", (thumb_w * 2 + gap * 3, thumbs[0].height * 2 + gap * 3), (244, 244, 244))
    for i, thumb in enumerate(thumbs):
        col, row = i % 2, i // 2
        sheet.paste(thumb, (gap + col * (thumb_w + gap), gap + row * (thumb.height + gap)))
    sheet_path = ROOT / "explorations" / "flavour-packs.png"
    sheet.save(sheet_path)
    print("wrote", sheet_path)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

The Raspberry drawing resembles a flower or bubbles. The leaves look like ears or a bow. It needs a cone of overlapping drupelets with pointed serrated leaves.

The Peanut drawing looks like kettlebells or eggs. The waist pinch is too subtle. The top is flat and the bottom is round. It should be elongated with a clear middle pinch and a pointed top.

The Peanut should be redrawn with two distinct lobes, a small stem tip, and a seam following the waist. The drawings need to sit on the ground line like the tote icons rather than floating above it. The Butter drawing is already clear.

The Stampmite barley drawing is the strongest. The Y-shaped awns could be cleaner.

The layout has too much empty space below the flavour name. I should move the drawing and name block down into the middle of the remaining field, or enlarge the icon to fill that space.

I will fix the Peanut and Raspberry drawings before presenting. The Peanut needs a strong horizontal seam across its waist instead of a diagonal slash, with pointed ends. The Raspberry should be a simple triangle of bumps tapering from top to bottom, with leaves as single pointed shapes rather than a bow.

The icon and name block will be centered vertically in the space between the meta text and the bar, with a larger icon. The Peanut shell is being redrawn as a vertical outline with a small top bump, a clear waist pinch, and a larger bottom bump, roughly twice as tall as it is wide. A waist seam will be added to complete the shape.

The current Peanut path bulges at the waist instead of pinching. The middle width is 96 while the top and bottom are narrower, making it look like a kettlebell. I am correcting the control points so the waist becomes the narrowest point.

The Peanut shell is being redrawn with a symmetric outline. Control points are being set so the waist becomes the narrowest point.

The Raspberry is being reworked as a single rounded triangle outline with internal arc bumps, or as a pyramid of non-overlapping circles so it no longer reads as a flower.

The Raspberry will be built as a pyramid of three rows of circles with slight overlap, plus a small pointed leaf and a tiny calyx. The icon block is being enlarged to 680 pixels wide and centered vertically in the space between the meta text and the bar. The Butter drawing is being shifted down so its bottom edge sits exactly on the ground line.

The ground line will be shortened to sit directly beneath the objects rather than spanning the full width. The contact sheet will be presented as exploratory drafts, not replacements for the existing pack image. I am also checking whether the butter yellow and peanut orange colour schemes are clearly distinct enough.

The colour contrast between the yellow butter, pink raspberry, purple stampmite, and orange peanut is clearly distinct. The Raspberry pyramid is being mapped to exact pixel coordinates for its three rows of circles. The leaf will be simplified into a basic almond shape with a central vein.
The barley reads clearly. The raspberry is coming out as a flower, and the peanuts look like weights, so I’m redrawing those two and setting each drawing on the ground line.

All four flavour labels share the same layout structure. Each uses a dark field with a light wordmark, icon, type, and bottom bar. The colour schemes are distinct: yellow for butter, hot pink for raspberry, and house purple for stampmite.

The peanut label uses orange on dark brown. Its dark field is nearly identical to the butter label's dark brown, though the bright light colours keep them visually distinct.

The contrast ratio for the house purple label is roughly 4.77 to one, which meets AA standards for large text. The meta row will be smaller at thumbnail scale, but the main bottom bar text is large enough to pass. I am now computing the remaining ratios.

The Toundra style is a unified scene on one ground line. Each pack currently shows a single isolated object. I should add related elements to each label so every pack reads as a complete scene rather than just one icon.

One hero drawing per flavour is the right interpretation of "some drawings." A second small companion element could be added to each pack to echo the tote's unified scene.

Adding decorative companion elements to every pack would dilute flavour distinction, so each label will keep one subject on the shared ground line. The main remaining polish is the butter ground line fix and the raspberry leaf redraw.

items.output:
1→# Stamp product spec

Locked from your choices in Stage 1. One number is a planning assumption and is marked as such: the manufactured cost that sits under the $5.00 shelf price.

## What a Stamp is

A Stamp is a 10 g disc of spread on a food-safe release film, nested in a printed card sheet. You peel one off and press it onto hot toast. The heat softens it into a layer. No knife and no open jar.

An unopened sheet lives in a pantry for 12 months. The home recipes below are kitchen prototypes, eaten from the fridge within 7 days. Only the industrial formulas are the products we sell, and only those claim the 12-month date.
10→
## Who it is for

Someone who eats toast away from a full kitchen: a flat, an office, a hall, or a bag. They want a decided portion of flavour without carrying a jar or washing a knife.

## Range and price

| Sheet | Contents | Net weight | Shelf price | Price per 100 g |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Salted Butter | 8 butter stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
20→| Raspberry | 8 raspberry stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
| Stampmite | 8 yeast-extract stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
| Peanut | 8 peanut stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
| Mixed | 2 of each flavour | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |

$6.25 per 100 g sits above about 90% of branded spread SKUs in the cleaned dataset (90th percentile $5.19 per 100 g). The median branded spread is $2.15 per 100 g. Fix & Fogg's SKUs sit around $2.65 per 100 g. The gap is the portion film and the card, which a jar does not have. The marker is on `data/figures/03-branded-spreads-price-per-100g.png`.

## How to use it

1. Keep the sheet in a pantry.
30→2. Peel one stamp off the release film.
3. Press it onto hot toast.
4. Wait a few seconds. The residual heat lays the spread across the slice.

## Claims we will make

- Peel and press onto hot toast.
- One stamp is one portion, 10 g.
- Four flavours, sold as single-flavour sheets and a mixed sheet.
- No knife and no jar.
40→- Unopened sheet, 12 months in a pantry.

## Claims we will not make

- Health treatment, "better for you," low-sugar, organic, or gluten-free.
- That Salted Butter is a pat of fridge butter. The sold disc is a shelf-stable butter spread. In Australia and New Zealand the word butter on its own is a dairy-identity standard (milkfat, no added oil). The flavour name on the sheet is Salted Butter. The descriptive line under it is "salted butter spread."
- That Stampmite is Marmite or Vegemite. Those names, jars, and trade dress do not appear on the pack or the site.

## Allergens

50→| Flavour | Contains | Also stated on every sheet |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Salted Butter | Milk | Made in a facility that handles milk and peanuts. |
| Raspberry | No major allergen in the recipe | Same facility statement. |
| Stampmite | Gluten (barley) | Same facility statement. |
| Peanut | Peanuts | Same facility statement. |
| Mixed | Milk, gluten, peanuts | Same facility statement. |

## Home prototypes

60→Each batch is eight stamps, 80 g. Shape into 10 g discs, press each onto a square of baking paper, and chill until they hold. Eat within 7 days. These batches test flavour and the peel-and-press gesture. They are not the shelf-stable product.

**Salted Butter.** 78 g unsalted butter, softened, beaten with 2 g fine salt.

**Raspberry.** 120 g raspberries, 30 g caster sugar, and 5 g lemon juice, cooked and stirred until 80 g of thick paste remains. Cool before portioning.

**Stampmite.** 55 g yeast extract, 15 g tomato paste, 8 g black treacle, and 2 g salt, warmed and stirred into a paste that holds a disc. This prototypes the salty yeast flavour. The sold paste is the industrial formula below, not a scooped jar of an existing brand.

**Peanut.** 85 g roasted peanuts and 1.5 g fine salt, ground to a firm paste and portioned before the oil separates.

70→## Industrial formulas

Deposit 10 g ± 0.5 g onto release film, cut, nest eight discs in a card sheet, and flow-wrap. A failed weight check or a film that will not release is a rejected stamp, not a sheet that ships. Shelf life is 12 months, ambient, unopened.

**Salted Butter.** Cultured butterfat and salt at the same 2 g salt per 78 g fat as the home batch. Moisture is low enough that the sealed disc stays stable in a pantry and still softens on hot toast. No added oil, so the dairy description stays honest. The pack line is "salted butter spread."

**Raspberry.** The home ratio (raspberry, sugar, lemon), cooked to the same thick paste and deposited at 10 g. Stability comes from the solids in the cook and the seal, not from a preservative claim.

**Stampmite.** Our yeast-extract paste: yeast extract, barley malt extract, salt, and vegetable concentrate, deposited at 10 g. Contains gluten. The flavour name is Stampmite. The pack does not say Marmite or Vegemite.

80→**Peanut.** Roasted peanut paste and salt, with a small share of a hard fat stabiliser so the disc does not oil off across 12 months. Contains peanuts.

## Manufactured cost (assumption)

You chose the $5.00 shelf price. You did not choose a cost target. Until Stage 4 prices a real manufacturer, the spec uses this stack:

| | Per sheet | Per stamp |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shelf price | $5.00 | $0.63 |
| Retailer keeps 35% | $1.75 | $0.22 |
90→| Stamp receives | $3.25 | $0.41 |
| Target manufactured cost | $1.50 | $0.19 |

$1.50 is 30% of the shelf price. The $1.75 left on Stamp's side of the wholesale price has to carry film, card, freight, and contribution. Change the 35% or the $1.50 and the recipes do not change; the Stage 4 manufacturer comparison does.

## Still open

Distribution (where a sheet is bought) is not decided. The manufacturer is Stage 4. The wordmark, colours, and pack art are in `brand/identity.md`.

Salted Butter spread calculates to 3607.5 kJ per 100g. Saturated fat is roughly 58.8g. Protein, carbohydrate and sugars are zero. The energy value is derived directly from the formula rather than using Anchor's table butter data.

Sodium is calculated at 980 mg per 100g. Per 10g serve: 361 kJ, 9.8 g fat, 5.9 g saturated fat, and 98 mg sodium. Values under 1 g will show as "<1 g" or "0 g". Fat displays one decimal place. Energy and sodium appear as whole numbers.

Energy is refined to 3610 kJ per 100g. Saturated fat and fat are rounded to 58.8 g and 9.8 g per 100g. The Raspberry spread recipe uses 120 g raspberries, 30 g caster sugar, and 5 g lemon juice reduced to 80 g. Raw compositions for these ingredients must be found.

The 80 g Raspberry spread will be scaled up to 100 g by multiplying the raw ingredient values by 1.25. Typical raw raspberry composition is being sourced from FSANZ or USDA data. The figures include roughly 220 kJ energy, 11.9 g carbohydrate, 4.4 g sugars, 6.5 g fibre, and 1 mg sodium per 100 g. FSANZ carbohydrate excludes fibre.

USDA raw raspberry data is being used for the Raspberry spread. The 120 g batch calculates to roughly 264 kJ energy, 1.44 g protein, 0.78 g fat, 0.02 g saturated fat, 6.53 g available carbohydrate, 5.30 g sugars, 7.8 g fibre, and 1.2 mg sodium.

Caster sugar and lemon juice compositions are being added to the Raspberry spread calculation. The 80 g batch totals roughly 779 kJ energy, 1.46 g protein, 0.79 g fat, 0.03 g saturated fat, 36.83 g available carbohydrate, and 35.4 g sugars. These values scale up to about 974 kJ per 100 g, 1.83 g protein, 0.99 g fat, 0 g saturated fat, 46.0 g available carbohydrate, and 44.3 g sugars.

Raspberry spread fibre is 9.75 g per 100 g and sodium is 2 mg. The summed ingredient energy of 974 kJ conflicts with the Atwater cross-check of 928 kJ. The Atwater method will be used for internal consistency, giving 928 kJ per 100 g. Per 10 g serve: 93 kJ, 0.2 g protein, 0.1 g fat, 0 g saturated fat, 4.6 g carbohydrate, 4.4 g sugars, and 0 mg sodium.

Sodium will be displayed as "<5 mg" per 100 g and "<1 mg" per serve to match real food-label conventions. The calculated 2 mg value is too precise for a genuine panel. Fibre content was not requested.

Dietary fibre will be added as an extra row to all four spreads for consistency. The Raspberry spread final values are now fixed at 928 kJ energy, 1.8 g protein, 1.0 g fat, 0 g saturated fat, 46.0 g carbohydrate, 44.3 g sugars, and 9.8 g dietary fibre per 100 g.

Raspberry spread ingredients are declared at 77% raspberries, 19% sugar, and 3% lemon juice. The label will read "Raspberries (77%), sugar, lemon juice." This percentage reflects the ingoing recipe weight rather than the reduced finished product.

FSANZ Standard 1.2.10 confirms that characterising ingredient percentages are based on ingoing weight as a proportion of the finished food. This validates the declared ingredient proportions.

The Raspberry spread's 120 g of fruit per 80 g finished product would yield a 150% ingredient percentage. Labels sometimes declare this as "prepared with 150% raspberries" or "made using 120 g of fruit per 100 g." St Dalfour and similar brands use "prepared with 50 g fruit per 100 g."

The Raspberry spread will declare "Raspberries (150%), sugar, lemon juice." This reflects the exact recipe proportions and is a standard high-fruit jam convention. The 150% figure means 150 g of raspberries were used to make 100 g of finished product.

The Raspberry spread label will use plain language: "Raspberries, sugar, lemon juice. Made with 150 g of raspberries per 100 g." This avoids a confusing percentage figure while matching real jam conventions.

No allergens appear in the recipe. The label will note that the facility handles milk and peanuts.

The Yeast extract spread lists yeast extract, barley malt extract, salt, and vegetable concentrate in descending order. Exact percentages are not yet available.

The home prototype for the Yeast extract spread is 55 g yeast extract, 15 g tomato paste, 8 g treacle, and 2 g salt. These ratios are being mapped to the industrial formula order while keeping yeast extract as the dominant ingredient.

The home prototype ratios conflict with the required ingredient order. Barley malt extract must exceed salt, but the original recipe placed treacle above salt. Vegetable concentrate is last in the spec yet was largest in the prototype. A new formula will follow the exact descending order while keeping yeast extract as the dominant ingredient.

The Yeast extract spread formula is being refined to 72 g yeast extract, 16 g barley malt extract, 8 g salt, and 4 g vegetable concentrate. Eight grams of salt would make the product far too salty, since Marmite contains roughly 3300 mg of sodium per 100 g. The home prototype used only 2 g of salt per 80 g batch, so the industrial salt level must be reduced to about 2.5% to match the home taste while still satisfying the required ingredient order.

The Yeast extract spread formula is being revised to 80 g yeast extract, 15.5 g barley malt extract, 2.5 g salt, and 2 g vegetable concentrate. This matches the home prototype salt level and satisfies the required ingredient order.

The Yeast extract spread formula is finalized at 80 g yeast extract, 15.5 g barley malt extract, 2.5 g salt, and 2 g vegetable concentrate per 100 g. The next step is sourcing the nutritional composition data for each ingredient.

Published Marmite nutritional data is being used as a benchmark for the Yeast extract spread. UK Marmite contains roughly 34–39 g protein and 10 g salt per 100 g, while South African Marmite has about 32 g protein and 4512 mg sodium per 100 g. The Yeast extract spread formula will be calibrated against these figures.

def sig3(value: float) -> float:
    """Round to at most three significant figures, the nutrition-panel rule."""
    if value == 0:
        return 0
    import math

    power = math.floor(math.log10(abs(value)))
    factor = 10 ** (power - 2)
    return round(value / factor) * factor


def gram(value: float) -> str:
    if value < 0.05:
        return "0 g"
    return f"{value:.1f} g"


def milligram(value: float) -> str:

    """Round to at most three significant figures, the nutrition-panel rule."""
    if value == 0:

def draw_runs(draw, runs, x, y, max_w, fill, size, line_h) -> int:
    cursor_x = x
    for text, weight in runs:
        face = font(weight, size)
        parts = text.split(" ")
        for index, part in enumerate(parts):
            token = part if index == 0 else " " + part
            if token == "":
                continue
            width = draw.textlength(token, font=face)
            if cursor_x > x and cursor_x + width > x + max_w:
                y += line_h
                cursor_x = x
                token = token.lstrip()
                width = draw.textlength(token, font=face)

def contact(images: list[Image.Image], path: Path, columns: int = 2) -> None:
    thumb_w = 520
    gap = 28
    thumbs = [
        image.resize((thumb_w, int(thumb_w * image.height / image.width)), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
        for image in images
    ]
    rows = (len(thumbs) + columns - 1) // columns
    sheet = Image.new(
        "RGB",
        (thumb_w * columns + gap * (columns + 1), thumbs[0].height * rows + gap * (rows + 1)),
        (236, 232, 228),
    )
    for i, thumb in enumerate(thumbs):
        col, row = i % columns, i // columns
        sheet.paste(thumb, (gap + col * (thumb_w + gap), gap + row * (thumb.height + gap)), thumb)
    sheet.save(path)
    print("wrote", path)

The nutrition numbers look sensible.

The per-serve sodium values are correctly rounded to three significant figures. The yeast extract's high sodium content is plausible for a 10g spread.

The peanut spread's nutrition values are correct. The 4.65g fat value rounds down to 4.6g, which is acceptable. Next comes visual QA of the front and back labels for layout overflow and rounded corners.

The main bug is that the word "spread" overlaps the flavour name on the back of the packaging.

The overlap happens because `text_center` returns the glyph box height rather than the distance from the y coordinate to the top of the text. The code adds only 4 pixels after the flavour name, which is too small for the full glyph descent.

The glyph box top is offset by internal leading. The text baseline sits at y, but the visual bottom reaches y + box[3]. Advancing by box[3] - box[1] leaves no gap. The next line starts immediately after the previous text.

A positive top offset in the glyph box shrinks the returned height. The next line starts before the previous text ends, causing overlap. For example, a 55-pixel height with a 70-pixel bottom pushes "spread" onto the flavour name.

The fix is to return `box[3]` from `text_center`. That value is the distance from the draw y coordinate to the bottom of the ink. Advancing by that amount plus a gap will place "spread" below the flavour name without overlap.

The front label uses a manual `textbbox` call and a fixed 12-pixel gap, so it is unaffected by the `text_center` change. Returning `box[3]` from that helper will cleanly fix the back label spacing.

The front label spacing is already correct because it uses `box[3]` directly. The back label is broken because `text_center` returns `box[3] - box[1]`. I need to check other callers of that helper before changing the return value, since they rely on the current height for layout calculations.

The front label will shift down slightly when meta_h increases, but that is harmless. The back label overlap will be fixed by advancing by the full ink bottom rather than the glyph height. Returning box[3] correctly accounts for any internal leading, so no other callers need adjustment.

I will update `text_center` to return `box[3]` and add a brief comment explaining the return value.

The back label also has a large empty gap between the storage block and the bottom bar. Shorter ingredient lists leave this void, which makes the layout look bottom-heavy. I may adjust the spacing between sections so the content feels more evenly distributed.

The empty gap under the storage block is acceptable for a real label, but it looks unfinished. I will fix the overlap first, then add small gaps between the name and icon, and between the nutrition table and storage lines, so the void is not one large hole.

The storage block should sit just above the bottom bar to mimic a real pack. Ingredients and NIP will flow from the top, while storage details anchor at the base. I will measure the footer height and place it at `h - bar - 160` from the top. Any gap between the NIP and the footer is acceptable.

The Raspberry and Peanut back labels share the same layout function, so they will be fixed automatically once the overlap is corrected. I will verify all three back labels after the change to confirm no overlap remains and the footer sits properly.

I also noticed a possible rendering issue where an en-dash may have appeared as a hyphen in the nutrition table, producing "- saturated" and "- sugars".

The en-dash rendering is fine; the image viewer may have normalized it. The contact sheet confirms rounded corners are visible on the grey background, while the full image likely shows them as transparent. The front label spacing is correct.

The back footer is now anchored at `h - bar - 28 - 34 * len(footer)`, placing it just above the bottom bar.

I added an overflow guard so the nutrition table cannot overlap the footer. If the table ends below the footer top, the draw position jumps to the footer start. I will also add a few extra pixels between the "spread" text and the icon to prevent a cramped look.

items.content: No overflow was detected. Now reviewing the backs.

The packaging backs now look solid. The word "spread" is clearly positioned beneath the flavour name.

All product details are now included on the packaging: ingredients, allergens, nutrition, storage, date, supplier, and net weight. The corners are rounded. Stampmite has been replaced with "Yeast extract". The gap between the NIP and storage block is intentional. The layout is clean and readable.

Nutrition values are calculated rather than lab-tested. Proportions were filled in where the specification only listed an order. Best-before dates and lot numbers are specimen entries. The supplier is Stamp, Auckland, with no street address yet because the manufacturer is not finalized. The logo, ad, and original purple pack image remain the house set until the user locks them.

The labels now use the flavour name with the word spread under it, rounded corners, and a back panel on each one. Stampmite is Yeast extract on the pack and in the product spec.

![Four fronts](brand/explorations/flavour-packs.png)

![Four backs](brand/explorations/flavour-backs.png)

Each front keeps the same layout. The name is Salted Butter, Raspberry, Yeast extract, or Peanut, and the only line under it is spread.

The back of each label carries the parts a packaged food in New Zealand has to show:

- Ingredients, with the allergen in bold, and a separate contains line where there is one.
- The facility line: made in a facility that handles milk and peanuts.
- A nutrition panel for a 10 g stamp and per 100 g.
- Storage, a best-before date, a lot code, the supplier, and the net weight.

The panels are calculated from the formulas and published composition figures. They are not a laboratory test. A 10 g yeast-extract stamp is about 280 mg of sodium, because the stamp is the serving. The best-before date, 30 SEP 2027, and lot L260930 are specimens. The supplier line is Stamp, Auckland, New Zealand. The street address is still open until a manufacturer is chosen.

The drum sounds will be synthesized with numpy. Kicks will sweep from 150 Hz to 45 Hz. Snares will use noise bursts and sine bodies. Claps, hats, and toms will add texture. The pattern will use ghost snares and open hats on offbeats for a fast feel.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Render a drums-only Stamp sting.

Ten bars at 160 bpm is 15.0 seconds. Numpy builds the kit. ffmpeg writes
the mp3. There is no lyric and no speech engine.
"""

import subprocess
import wave
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUT = ROOT / "stamp-jingle.mp3"
WAV = Path("/tmp/stamp-jingle.wav")

SR = 44100
BPM = 160
BARS = 10
STEPS = 16
STEP = 60.0 / BPM / 4
DURATION = BARS * STEPS * STEP  # 15.0 s

RNG = np.random.default_rng(20261001)


def env(n, curve):
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    return np.exp(-t * curve)


def kick():
    n = int(SR * 0.32)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    freq = 46 + (168 - 46) * np.exp(-t * 32)
    phase = 2 * np.pi * np.cumsum(freq) / SR
    body = np.sin(phase) * env(n, 9.5)
    click = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 1650 * t) * env(n, 240)
    punch = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 80 * t) * env(n, 28)
    return body * 1.05 + click * 0.28 + punch * 0.35


def snare():
    n = int(SR * 0.20)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    noise = np.diff(RNG.normal(0, 1, n), prepend=0.0)
    noise *= env(n, 26)
    body = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 196 * t) * env(n, 34)
    snap = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 3200 * t) * env(n, 180)
    return noise * 0.72 + body * 0.42 + snap * 0.18


def clap():
    n = int(SR * 0.16)
    out = np.zeros(n)
    noise = np.diff(RNG.normal(0, 1, n), prepend=0.0)
    for delay, gain in ((0, 0.55), (int(0.011 * SR), 0.85), (int(0.023 * SR), 1.0)):
        burst = noise * env(n, 38) * gain
        out[delay:] += burst[: n - delay]
    return out * 0.55


def hat(opened=False):
    dur = 0.18 if opened else 0.045
    n = int(SR * dur)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    noise = np.diff(RNG.normal(0, 1, n), prepend=0.0)
    metal = (
        np.sign(np.sin(2 * np.pi * 5840 * t))
        + 0.6 * np.sign(np.sin(2 * np.pi * 8120 * t))
    )
    curve = 14 if opened else 78
    return (noise * 0.65 + metal * 0.22) * env(n, curve)


def tom(freq):
    n = int(SR * 0.26)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    f = freq * (0.72 + 0.28 * np.exp(-t * 24))
    phase = 2 * np.pi * np.cumsum(f) / SR
    body = np.sin(phase) * env(n, 11)
    click = np.diff(RNG.normal(0, 1, n), prepend=0.0) * env(n, 90)
    return body * 0.9 + click * 0.18


def crash():
    n = int(SR * 1.35)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    noise = np.diff(RNG.normal(0, 1, n), prepend=0.0)
    metal = sum(np.sign(np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * t)) for f in (4200, 6100, 8700))
    return (noise * 0.5 + metal * 0.12) * env(n, 3.4) * 0.7


def place(bus, sample, start, gain, pan):
    """pan is -1 (left) to +1 (right). Constant-power."""
    start = int(start)
    if start >= bus.shape[1] or gain <= 0:
        return
    sample = sample[: bus.shape[1] - start]
    left = np.cos((pan + 1) * np.pi / 4)
    right = np.sin((pan + 1) * np.pi / 4)
    bus[0, start : start + len(sample)] += sample * gain * left
    bus[1, start : start + len(sample)] += sample * gain * right


def step_time(bar, step):
    """Light swing: off-16ths sit a little late."""
    swing = 0.010 if step % 2 else 0.0
    return (bar * STEPS + step) * STEP + swing


def main():
    n = int(round(DURATION * SR))
    bus = np.zeros((2, n), dtype=np.float64)
    kit = {
        "kick": kick(),
        "snare": snare(),
        "clap": clap(),
        "hat": hat(False),
        "open": hat(True),
        "crash": crash(),
        "tom_hi": tom(240),
        "tom_mid": tom(170),
        "tom_lo": tom(118),
    }

    # 16th-note grids. Kick pushes off the grid; snare holds 2 and 4.
    kick_main = {0, 3, 6, 8, 11}
    snare_main = {4, 12}
    ghost = {7, 15}
    open_hat = {6, 14}

    for bar in range(BARS):
        fill = bar == 7
        ending = bar == 9
        hat_gain = 0.34 if bar == 0 else 0.46
        kick_gain = 0.78 if bar == 0 else 0.98
        for step in range(STEPS):
            when = step_time(bar, step) * SR
            accent = 1.0 if step % 4 == 0 else 0.62
            if not (ending and step >= 8):
                place(bus, kit["hat"], when, hat_gain * accent, 0.35)
            if step in open_hat and not fill and not ending:
                place(bus, kit["open"], when, 0.40, 0.45)
            if fill:
                # Snare roll, louder toward the last step.
                roll = 0.35 + 0.65 * (step / 15)
                place(bus, kit["snare"], when, 0.55 * roll, -0.15)
                if step in (0, 4, 8, 12):
                    drum = ("tom_hi", "tom_mid", "tom_lo", "tom_lo")[step // 4]
                    place(bus, kit[drum], when, 0.72, -0.4 + 0.25 * (step // 4))
            if ending and step == 0:
                place(bus, kit["crash"], when, 0.85, 0.1)
            kicks = {0, 8} if bar == 0 or fill or ending else kick_main
            if step in kicks:
                place(bus, kit["kick"], when, kick_gain, 0.0)
            if not fill and step in snare_main and not (ending and step == 12):
                place(bus, kit["snare"], when, 0.82, -0.12)
                place(bus, kit["clap"], when, 0.48, 0.05)
            if not fill and not ending and step in ghost:
                place(bus, kit["snare"], when, 0.16, -0.12)

    # Soft clip, then a 12 ms fade so the file does not click.
    peak = np.max(np.abs(bus))
    bus *= 1.7 / peak
    bus = np.tanh(bus) 
    bus *= 0.89 / np.max(np.abs(bus))
    fade = int(0.012 * SR)
    bus[:, :fade] *= np.linspace(0, 1, fade)
    bus[:, -fade:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, fade)

    pcm = np.clip(bus.T, -1, 1)
    pcm = (pcm * 32767).astype(np.int16)
    with wave.open(str(WAV), "w") as handle:
        handle.setnchannels(2)
        handle.setsampwidth(2)
        handle.setframerate(SR)
        handle.writeframes(pcm.tobytes())

    subprocess.run(
        [
            "ffmpeg", "-y", "-i", str(WAV),
            "-ar", "44100", "-ac", "2",
            "-c:a", "libmp3lame", "-b:a", "192k",
            str(OUT),
        ],
        check=True,
        capture_output=True,
    )
    probe = subprocess.run(
        [
            "ffprobe", "-v", "error",
            "-show_entries", "format=duration",
            "-of", "default=nw=1:nk=1",
            str(OUT),
        ],
        check=True,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    print(f"wrote {OUT}")
    print(f"duration {float(probe.stdout.strip()):.3f}s")
    print(f"wav peak {np.max(np.abs(bus)):.3f}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
