I'll create two or three alternate drum variations and present them for the user to choose from.

The Toundra brand calls for a bright, playful, lime-acid aesthetic. I'll avoid aggressive EDM or trap darkness. The strongest alternate will become the main jingle file.

The current beat feels too clubby and harsh. I'm exploring three fresh directions: a dry, woody sticker-pop kit with congas and shakers; a warm breakbeat or funk groove with tighter hi-hats; and a bright marching-percussion ensemble that matches the "Stamp" name.

The "Stamp" name suggests a foot-stomp and hand-clap pattern. That would feel physical and human rather than like a club loop.

The current hi-hats use cheap square-wave synth sounds. The user may want better drum samples rather than just a new groove.

The new kit will use a rounder kick, a body-heavy snare, and a shaker instead of the harsh square hats. It adds a tambourine, hand clap, and woodblock for playful texture. The tempo is 126 BPM, giving about eight bouncy bars in fifteen seconds.

The tempo is now fixed at 120–128 BPM for a punchy brand sting. Three distinct kits are planned: a physical stomp-clap with tambourine, a warm breakbeat, and a light percussion ensemble. The main jingle file will not be overwritten until the user picks.

The PDF description will stay unchanged until the user picks a vibe. The current official file remains untouched, and the three new alternatives will be saved as separate files so they can listen side by side.

I'll iterate from the current file rather than overwrite it. The new kit and groove will keep the same 15-second length and high energy, but change the drum character so the vibe shifts.

The stomp sound will be a low thump with a noise burst around 60 Hz and a 40 ms attack. The clap will use delayed noise hits for a warmer, less metallic snap.

The tambourine will use sine-wave metallic partials instead of the harsh square-wave hats. The shaker will be a filtered noise burst at 16th-note speed. The tempo is fixed at 128 BPM for exactly eight bars in fifteen seconds. The pattern places stomp on beats one and three, clap on two and four, tambourine on eighth notes, and a light shaker on sixteenths. A clap fill will close the loop.

The stomp-clap pattern will be more syncopated and light so it does not feel like a stadium chant.

The breakbeat will use a boomier kick, looser snare, and swing hi-hats. It will run at 144 BPM for nine bars in fifteen seconds.

The hand-percussion kit will feature conga slaps, woodblock, shaker, and soft cowbell. The tempo is 126 BPM for an afro-pop highlife vibe.

I will consolidate the three drum variations into a single render script. The chosen kit will be written directly to stamp-jingle.mp3. I am avoiding square-wave synth sounds entirely, using only filtered noise and sine partials for a warmer, buzzer-free drum character.

The percussion pattern will use a conga tumbao: tone, slap, open, tone. Woodblock hits the offbeats and the shaker plays sixteenths. The official stamp-jingle.mp3 will be the sunny hand-percussion take. The other two files are saved for comparison.

1→# Stamp product spec

Locked from your choices in Stage 1. One number is a planning assumption and is marked as such: the manufactured cost that sits under the $5.00 shelf price.

## What a Stamp is

A Stamp is a 10 g disc of spread on a food-safe release film, nested in a printed card sheet. You peel one off and press it onto hot toast. The heat softens it into a layer. No knife and no open jar.

An unopened sheet lives in a pantry for 12 months. The home recipes below are kitchen prototypes, eaten from the fridge within 7 days. Only the industrial formulas are the products we sell, and only those claim the 12-month date.
10→
## Who it is for

Someone who eats toast away from a full kitchen: a flat, an office, a hall, or a bag. They want a decided portion of flavour without carrying a jar or washing a knife.

## Range and price

| Sheet | Contents | Net weight | Shelf price | Price per 100 g |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Salted Butter | 8 butter stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
20→| Raspberry | 8 raspberry stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
| Yeast extract | 8 yeast-extract stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
| Peanut | 8 peanut stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
| Mixed | 2 of each flavour | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |

$6.25 per 100 g sits above about 90% of branded spread SKUs in the cleaned dataset (90th percentile $5.19 per 100 g). The median branded spread is $2.15 per 100 g. Fix & Fogg's SKUs sit around $2.65 per 100 g. The gap is the portion film and the card, which a jar does not have. The marker is on `data/figures/03-branded-spreads-price-per-100g.png`.

## How to use it

1. Keep the sheet in a pantry.
30→2. Peel one stamp off the release film.
3. Press it onto hot toast.
4. Wait a few seconds. The residual heat lays the spread across the slice.

## Claims we will make

- Peel and press onto hot toast.
- One stamp is one portion, 10 g.
- Four flavours, sold as single-flavour sheets and a mixed sheet.
- No knife and no jar.
40→- Unopened sheet, 12 months in a pantry.

## Claims we will not make

- Health treatment, "better for you," low-sugar, organic, or gluten-free.
- That Salted Butter is a pat of fridge butter. The sold disc is a shelf-stable butter spread. In Australia and New Zealand the word butter on its own is a dairy-identity standard (milkfat, no added oil). The sheet shows the flavour name, then the word spread. The ingredient list names cultured butterfat.
- That Yeast extract is Marmite or Vegemite. Those names, jars, and trade dress do not appear on the pack or the site.

## Allergens

50→| Flavour | Contains | Also stated on every sheet |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Salted Butter | Milk | Made in a facility that handles milk and peanuts. |
| Raspberry | No major allergen in the recipe | Same facility statement. |
| Yeast extract | Gluten (barley) | Same facility statement. |
| Peanut | Peanuts | Same facility statement. |
| Mixed | Milk, gluten, peanuts | Same facility statement. |

## Home prototypes

60→Each batch is eight stamps, 80 g. Shape into 10 g discs, press each onto a square of baking paper, and chill until they hold. Eat within 7 days. These batches test flavour and the peel-and-press gesture. They are not the shelf-stable product.

**Salted Butter.** 78 g unsalted butter, softened, beaten with 2 g fine salt.

**Raspberry.** 120 g raspberries, 30 g caster sugar, and 5 g lemon juice, cooked and stirred until 80 g of thick paste remains. Cool before portioning.

**Yeast extract.** 55 g yeast extract, 15 g tomato paste, 8 g black treacle, and 2 g salt, warmed and stirred into a paste that holds a disc. This prototypes the salty yeast flavour. The sold paste is the industrial formula below, not a scooped jar of an existing brand.

**Peanut.** 85 g roasted peanuts and 1.5 g fine salt, ground to a firm paste and portioned before the oil separates.

70→## Industrial formulas

Deposit 10 g ± 0.5 g onto release film, cut, nest eight discs in a card sheet, and flow-wrap. A failed weight check or a film that will not release is a rejected stamp, not a sheet that ships. Shelf life is 12 months, ambient, unopened.

**Salted Butter.** Cultured butterfat and salt at the same 2 g salt per 78 g fat as the home batch. Moisture is low enough that the sealed disc stays stable in a pantry and still softens on hot toast. No added oil, so the dairy description stays honest. On the sheet the flavour name is Salted Butter and the word under it is spread.

**Raspberry.** The home ratio (raspberry, sugar, lemon), cooked to the same thick paste and deposited at 10 g. Stability comes from the solids in the cook and the seal, not from a preservative claim. The label says it is made with 150 g of raspberries per 100 g, which is this cook: 120 g of fruit reduced to 80 g.

**Yeast extract.** Our yeast-extract paste, deposited at 10 g: yeast extract 80%, barley malt extract 15.5%, salt 2.5%, vegetable concentrate 2%. The salt share matches the home batch. Barley malt extract sits above salt, and vegetable concentrate sits below it, so the ingredient list stays in the order above. Contains gluten. The flavour name is Yeast extract. The pack does not say Marmite or Vegemite.

80→**Peanut.** Roasted peanuts 96%, vegetable fat 2.3% as the hard-fat stabiliser, and salt 1.7%, close to the 1.5 g salt in the home batch. The stabiliser keeps the disc from oiling off across 12 months. Contains peanuts.

The nutrition panels on the backs are calculated from these proportions and published composition figures. They are not a laboratory assay.

## Manufactured cost (assumption)

You chose the $5.00 shelf price. You did not choose a cost target. Until Stage 4 prices a real manufacturer, the spec uses this stack:

| | Per sheet | Per stamp |
| --- | --- | --- |

items.content:
The British pronunciation of "Raspberry" is r'aasb3ri.

The en-gb voice is chosen for clear intelligibility. The script is set: a 32-second music bed, espeak-ng vocal lines at 22050 Hz, and ffmpeg mixing with resampling, delay, and volume control.

The drum pattern is set to 120 BPM over 16 bars. Kicks land on beats 1 and 3, snares on 2 and 4, and hi-hats play every eighth note with accents on the downbeats.

The melody uses a C pentatonic scale to avoid clashing with speech. A 2-bar motif in eighths is defined for the first phrase, followed by an answer phrase. MIDI note frequencies are being calculated from the 440 Hz reference.

The melody will duck during vocal lines and only reappear between them. The first two bars will feature the full phrase, followed by a sparse bass line that keeps speech in front.

The initial plan of eight separate vocal clips would leave the jingle feeling slow and empty. The approach is shifting to fewer clips with natural pauses via espeak word gaps, plus musical fills. The final structure will be four main vocal sections.

The six vocal clips are now timed precisely. "Stamp." appears at 2.2 s and again at 21.5 and 27.5 s. The other lines land at 4.6 s, 10.5 s, and 17.0 s. The final clip ends near 28.7 s, leaving a short music tail before the 32-second mark. The name is heard three times. No silence is added after the button.

The drum synthesis is being coded in Python. The kick uses a frequency sweep and a high-frequency click. The snare uses filtered noise with a short sine tone.

The hi-hat generator is now defined. It uses filtered noise with a highpass filter and exponential decay, producing either a closed or open hat sound. Reusing the same random seed for every hit will make all snares identical, which is acceptable for a drum machine.

The pluck generator is being defined. It uses a sine wave with slight inharmonicity, an exponential decay envelope, and a short attack to mimic a struck string.

A simple bass line will play root notes on beats with a sine wave and longer decay. Chord stabs were considered but rejected to avoid clutter.

The script will render speech clips first, probe their durations, place them at fixed start times with gaps, render the full music bed, then mix everything with ffmpeg.

Music will duck by about 4–6 dB during vocal windows to keep the voice in front.

The music bed will be ducked in numpy before ffmpeg, so ffmpeg only mixes the vocal clips into the pre-ducked bed. A short moving average will remove DC offset from the drum noise. A soft shaker with quiet hats on sixteenth notes was considered for the hook but rejected as too busy; eighth-note hats are sufficient. The `add_drums` function will place hits on the global beat grid within a given time window.

The drum pattern will place kicks on beats 0 and 2, snares on beats 1 and 3, and eighth-note hats on every beat plus a half-beat later. An open hat on the "and" of bar four will fire every other bar.

The open hat on the offbeat will fire only during full drum sections, replacing the closed hat every other bar. The final kick at 23.30 will land with the chord and no snare. The bass line will use G3 for 1.5 beats and D3 for 1.4 beats, repeating every four beats, then a final G3 at 23.30 lasting six beats with slower decay.

A `phrase` helper will generate note tuples from a list of pitch names at fixed intervals. Two eight-note motifs, A and B, are defined for the lead line. Each note lasts 0.48 beats so they almost touch but remain separated by fade-out.

The lead phrase timing is being tightened. Motif A will run from 0.0 to 1.50 seconds, ending before the first Stamp line at 1.70. The middle section will use a short four-note phrase ending at 9.60 seconds, followed by the Raspberry line at 10.00. The hook will layer Motif A and Motif B from 17.30 to 21.30 seconds. To avoid colliding with the final Stamp line at 22.40, the trailing fragment will end at 22.30 seconds and the last Stamp line will shift to 22.55.

The final pickup notes end at 21.80 seconds, followed by the Stamp line at 22.40 and the chord at 23.35. This leaves a 0.6-second gap before the name and a 0.22-second gap after it, giving the phrase a natural breath.

Drums will stop at 22.35 seconds so the final Stamp line is clean. The last kick lands on the beat grid at 22.0 seconds, and the name at 22.40 sits just after it as an accent. The chord will land at 23.40 seconds with a kick, even though that time is not a grid beat.

The final chord will ring for 4.6 seconds with decay 1.3, fading from roughly 7.4 percent amplitude at two seconds to about 0.5 percent by four seconds. The tail will not be silent, so the file avoids a dead ending. The script will verify that the last two seconds are not mostly silence and may trim the duration to 26 seconds if the tail is too quiet.

The final duration is fixed at 26.0 seconds. The chord will ring from 23.40 to 26.0, giving a tight two-and-a-half-second tail. This length is an exact sample boundary and keeps the piece within the 20–40 second target. The timeline is being reviewed to ensure the middle section is not too cramped and the melody remains identifiable.

The lead melody will sit between the vocal lines rather than underneath them, keeping the lyrics clear. The hook spans four seconds of full tune plus a brief intro and middle section, totaling about 6.5 seconds of melody. This is acceptable for a short background line. The intro motif is too brief to layer beneath the opening voice.

The script will print the espeak and ffmpeg commands it runs. A final bug review is planned before execution. The place() helper will clip any signal that overflows the buffer.

The `place()` helper will silently truncate any signal that overflows the 26-second buffer. All instruments will be generated as mono float64 and duplicated to stereo at the end, with lead and bass centered in the mix so the vocal stays in front.

The script will be written and executed next, with any needed adjustments applied afterward. The temporary audio directory will be removed once encoding finishes. The final reply will include the duration, lyric, and exact commands used. A potential pause issue from trailing periods in espeak was considered and dismissed because the measured timing already accounts for them. The Raspberry line will use pitch 48 and speed 136, and the received-pronunciation accent is preferred for clearer diction.

The middle riff is fixed at 6.40 seconds, lasting about 2.17 seconds and ending near 8.57. A doubled or higher-pitched voice for the final "Stamp" was considered but rejected to keep the consonants clear.

The middle riff is now fixed at 8.70 seconds, ending at 9.70 so the Raspberry line at 10.05 has a comfortable quarter-second gap. The full cue list is finalized with exact timestamps for every vocal line.

The final Stamp line at 22.40 leaves a comfortable 0.45-second gap. All other vocal windows and the intro motif are also checked and spaced correctly.

The opening Stamp line is shifted to 1.85 seconds so the intro motif has a comfortable gap. The revised timeline now runs from 1.85 to 26.00 seconds, with the final Stamp at 22.50 and the chord at 23.40.

The final cue list is locked at eight lines with exact timestamps. The lead line will use a middle four-note phrase at 8.95 seconds, Motif A at 17.60, Motif B at 19.60, and the pickup at 21.60. Drums stop at 22.45 so the final Stamp line at 22.50 is clean. A kick lands on the downbeat at 22.0 seconds before that name.

Drums will stop at 22.30 seconds so the final Stamp line at 22.50 is clean and unbroken by a drum hit. Harmony will be added only to Motif A and Motif B, one diatonic third below the lead line. The final chord will use G4, B4, D5 plus a soft G5, with decay 1.35, amplitude scaled to 90 percent of the lead, and a long tail.

The `sustain` function will use a 30 ms fade at each note's end. This risks cutting the long ring of the final chord, so the fade may be removed or shortened.

Per-second RMS levels will be printed for debugging. numpy is already available in the Python 3.14 environment, so no extra packages need installation.

The bass line will use a simple oom-pah pattern: G3 for 1.2 beats, then D3 for 1.2 beats, with rests between. This avoids a drone and keeps the rhythm clear on laptop speakers.

The vocal track will be mixed at 0.72 volume in ffmpeg to avoid clipping, since espeak already outputs int16 audio and trimming does not change gain. A comment will be added to the script noting that the vocal text is read from lyrics.txt so the recording matches the lyric file.

The ducking ratio is set to 0.45 so the bed stays audible under the voice rather than becoming a dry silence track. Peak levels are estimated at roughly 0.40 for the bed and 0.72 for the vocal, giving a 5:1 peak ratio that should keep the speech in front. The script will print these ratios and allow constant tweaks if needed.

The script will report the numpy peak amplitude as a "not silent" check. A spectrogram or waveform plot is not possible without matplotlib, so per-second RMS levels serve as the visual monitor. The espeak output was also checked for clipping; one file peaked at 0.999, which is nearly saturated.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Render the Stamp jingle.

Melody and drums are numpy. The vocal is espeak-ng, one clip per line of
lyrics.txt, so the recording says that file. ffmpeg mixes the vocal in front
of the bed and writes stamp-jingle.mp3.
"""

import subprocess
import sys
import wave
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
LYRICS = ROOT / "lyrics.txt"
BED = ROOT / "bed.wav"
MIX = ROOT / "mix.wav"
OUT = ROOT / "stamp-jingle.mp3"

SR = 44100
BPM = 120
BEAT = 60.0 / BPM
EIGHTH = BEAT / 2
DURATION = 26.0

# One cue per non-empty line in lyrics.txt. Stamp lines are slower.
# start seconds, speed wpm, pitch, amplitude, word gap (10 ms units).
CUES = [
    (1.85, 112, 44, 160, 2),
    (2.95, 138, 46, 150, 16),
    (6.50, 142, 46, 150, 8),
    (10.20, 136, 48, 155, 4),
    (11.45, 140, 46, 150, 14),
    (14.70, 138, 46, 150, 8),
    (16.70, 112, 44, 160, 2),
    (22.50, 112, 44, 160, 2),
]

BED_PEAK = 0.42
DUCK = 0.40
VOCAL_GAIN = 0.78

MIDI = {
    "D3": 50,
    "G3": 55,
    "B3": 59,
    "D4": 62,
    "G4": 67,
    "A4": 69,
    "B4": 71,
    "C5": 72,
    "D5": 74,
    "E5": 76,
    "F#5": 78,
    "G5": 79,
    "A5": 81,
}
THIRD_BELOW = {
    "E5": "C5",
    "D5": "B4",
    "B4": "G4",
    "G5": "E5",
    "A5": "F#5",
    "C5": "A4",
}
MOTIF_A = ["E5", "D5", "B4", "D5", "G5", "E5", "D5", "B4"]
MOTIF_B = ["D5", "B4", "E5", "G5", "A5", "G5", "E5", "D5"]

RNG = np.random.default_rng(20260328)


def midi_freq(name):
    return 440.0 * 2.0 ** ((MIDI[name] - 69) / 12.0)


def read_lines():
    lines = [ln.strip() for ln in LYRICS.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()]
    lines = [ln for ln in lines if ln]
    if len(lines) != len(CUES):
        sys.exit(f"lyrics.txt has {len(lines)} lines, expected {len(CUES)}")
    if not any(ln.lower().startswith("stamp") for ln in lines):
        sys.exit("lyrics.txt does not say Stamp")
    return lines


def write_wav(path, audio, sr):
    audio = np.asarray(audio, dtype=np.float64)
    audio = np.clip(audio, -1.0, 1.0)
    if audio.ndim == 1:
        pcm = (audio * 32767.0).astype(np.int16)
        channels = 1
    else:
        pcm = (audio * 32767.0).astype(np.int16)
        channels = audio.shape[1]
    with wave.open(str(path), "wb") as handle:
        handle.setnchannels(channels)
        handle.setsampwidth(2)
        handle.setframerate(sr)
        handle.writeframes(pcm.tobytes())


def read_wav(path):
    with wave.open(str(path), "rb") as handle:
        sr = handle.getframerate()
        channels = handle.getnchannels()
        frames = handle.getnframes()
        pcm = np.frombuffer(handle.readframes(frames), dtype=np.int16).astype(np.float64)
        pcm /= 32768.0
    if channels > 1:
        pcm = pcm.reshape(-1, channels)
    return pcm, sr


def trim_speech(samples, sr):
    """Drop espeak's padding. Keep the stop release on Stamp."""
    active = np.flatnonzero(np.abs(samples) > 0.015)
    if len(active) == 0:
        return samples
    start = max(0, active[0] - int(0.012 * sr))
    end = min(len(samples), active[-1] + int(0.07 * sr))
    return samples[start:end]


def render_vocals(lines):
    clips = []
    for index, (line, cue) in enumerate(zip(lines, CUES), start=1):
        start, speed, pitch, amp, gap = cue
        path = ROOT / f"vox-{index}.wav"
        cmd = [
            "espeak-ng",
            "-v",
            "en-gb",
            "-s",
            str(speed),
            "-p",
            str(pitch),
            "-a",
            str(amp),
            "-g",
            str(gap),
            "-z",
            "-w",
            str(path),
            line,
        ]
        print(" ", " ".join(cmd))
        subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)
        samples, sr = read_wav(path)
        if sr != 22050:
            sys.exit(f"unexpected espeak rate {sr}")
        samples = trim_speech(samples, sr)
        if float(np.max(np.abs(samples))) < 0.05:
            sys.exit(f"vocal clip {path.name} is silent")
        write_wav(path, samples, sr)
        clips.append((path, start, len(samples) / sr, line))
    for i in range(len(clips) - 1):
        end = clips[i][1] + clips[i][2]
        nxt = clips[i + 1][1]
        if end > nxt - 0.08:
            sys.exit(f"vocal overlap: line {i + 1} ends {end:.2f}, next starts {nxt:.2f}")
    last_end = clips[-1][1] + clips[-1][2]
    if last_end > DURATION - 0.5:
        sys.exit(f"last vocal ends at {last_end:.2f}, past the bed")
    return clips


def place(buf, sig, start):
    if start >= DURATION or len(sig) == 0:
        return
    i = int(round(start * SR))
    if i >= len(buf):
        return
    n = min(len(sig), len(buf) - i)
    buf[i : i + n] += sig[:n]


def env_fade(n, attack, decay):
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    env = np.exp(-t * decay)
    a = min(max(int(attack * SR), 1), n)
    env[:a] *= np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, a)
    f = min(max(int(0.012 * SR), 1), n // 2)
    env[-f:] *= np.linspace(1.0, 0.0, f)
    return env


def kick():
    n = int(SR * 0.20)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    freq = 46.0 + 130.0 * np.exp(-t * 24.0)
    phase = 2.0 * np.pi * np.cumsum(freq) / SR
    body = np.sin(phase) * np.exp(-t * 11.0)
    click_n = int(SR * 0.008)
    click = np.zeros(n)
    ct = np.arange(click_n) / SR
    click[:click_n] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * 1650.0 * ct) * np.exp(-ct * 320.0)
    return (body * 0.9 + click * 0.28) * env_end_guard(n)


def env_end_guard(n):
    # Returned as a multiplier of ones so kick math stays in one expression.
    return 1.0


def snare():
    n = int(SR * 0.16)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    noise = RNG.standard_normal(n)
    noise = noise - np.convolve(noise, np.ones(6) / 6.0, mode="same")
    body = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * 188.0 * t) * np.exp(-t * 32.0)
    sig = noise * np.exp(-t * 26.0) * 0.55 + body * 0.32
    return sig


def hat(open_hat=False):
    dur = 0.20 if open_hat else 0.045
    n = int(SR * dur)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    noise = RNG.standard_normal(n)
    hp = np.diff(noise, prepend=noise[0])
    hp = np.diff(hp, prepend=hp[0])
    decay = 12.0 if open_hat else 48.0
    metal = np.zeros(n)
    for freq in (3100.0, 5400.0, 7900.0):
        metal += np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * freq * t)
    sig = (hp * 0.75 + metal / 3.0 * 0.25) * np.exp(-t * decay)
    return sig * (0.22 if open_hat else 0.16)


def bass_note(name, beats, decay=5.0):
    freq = midi_freq(name)
    n = int(SR * beats * BEAT)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    wave = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * freq * t) + 0.35 * np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * freq * 2.0 * t)
    return wave * env_fade(n, 0.008, decay) * 0.55


def lead_note(name, beats, amp=0.32, decay=8.0):
    freq = midi_freq(name)
    n = int(SR * beats * BEAT)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    wave = (
        0.20 * np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * (freq * 0.5) * t)
        + 0.64 * np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * freq * t)
        + 0.16 * np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * freq * 2.0 * t)
    )
    return wave * env_fade(n, 0.006, decay) * amp


def add_drums(buf, t_end):
    first = 0
    last = int(np.floor((t_end - 1e-6) / BEAT))
    for i in range(first, last + 1):
        t = i * BEAT
        pos = i % 4
        if pos in (0, 2):
            place(buf, kick() * 0.95, t)
        if pos in (1, 3):
            place(buf, snare() * 0.72, t)
        place(buf, hat(False), t)
        off = t + BEAT * 0.5
        if pos == 3 and (i // 4) % 2 == 1:
            place(buf, hat(True), off)
        else:
            place(buf, hat(False) * 0.8, off)


def add_bass(buf, t_end):
    t = 0.0
    while t < t_end - 1e-6:
        place(buf, bass_note("G3", 1.35), t)
        place(buf, bass_note("D3", 1.15), t + 2.0 * BEAT)
        t += 4.0 * BEAT


def add_phrase(buf, t0, names, harmony=False):
    for i, name in enumerate(names):
        t = t0 + i * EIGHTH
        place(buf, lead_note(name, 0.46), t)
        if harmony and name in THIRD_BELOW:
            place(buf, lead_note(THIRD_BELOW[name], 0.46, amp=0.14, decay=8.0), t)


def add_chord(buf, t0):
    for name, amp in (("G4", 0.22), ("B4", 0.18), ("D5", 0.16), ("G5", 0.10)):
        freq = midi_freq(name)
        n = int(SR * 3.2)
        t = np.arange(n) / SR
        wave = (
            0.30 * np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * freq * t)
            + 0.12 * np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * freq * 2.0 * t)
        )
        env = np.exp(-t * 1.45)
        env[: int(0.02 * SR)] *= np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, int(0.02 * SR))
        place(buf, wave * env * amp, t0)
    place(buf, bass_note("G3", 4.0, decay=1.6) * 0.8, t0)
    place(buf, kick() * 0.8, t0)


def duck(mono, clips):
    env = np.ones(len(mono), dtype=np.float64)
    ramp_n = int(0.045 * SR)
    for _path, start, dur, _line in clips:
        a = max(0, int((start - 0.06) * SR))
        b = min(len(mono), int((start + dur + 0.10) * SR))
        seg = np.full(b - a, DUCK)
        r = min(ramp_n, max((b - a) // 2, 1))
        curve = 0.5 - 0.5 * np.cos(np.linspace(0.0, np.pi, r))
        seg[:r] = 1.0 + (DUCK - 1.0) * curve
        seg[-r:] = DUCK + (1.0 - DUCK) * curve
        env[a:b] = np.minimum(env[a:b], seg)
    return mono * env


def render_bed(clips):
    n = int(DURATION * SR)
    mono = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.float64)
    add_drums(mono, 22.30)
    add_bass(mono, 22.0)
    add_phrase(mono, 0.00, MOTIF_A[:6])
    add_phrase(mono, 8.95, ["A5", "G5", "E5", "D5"])
    add_phrase(mono, 17.60, MOTIF_A, harmony=True)
    add_phrase(mono, 19.60, MOTIF_B, harmony=True)
    add_phrase(mono, 21.60, ["B4", "D5"])
    add_chord(mono, 23.45)
    peak = float(np.max(np.abs(mono)))
    if peak < 1e-6:
        sys.exit("music bed is silent")
    mono *= BED_PEAK / peak
    mono = duck(mono, clips)
    fade_in = int(0.01 * SR)
    fade_out = int(0.20 * SR)
    mono[:fade_in] *= np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, fade_in)
    mono[-fade_out:] *= np.linspace(1.0, 0.0, fade_out)
    stereo = np.column_stack([mono, mono])
    write_wav(BED, stereo, SR)
    return stereo


def ffmpeg_mix(clips):
    cmd = ["ffmpeg", "-y", "-i", str(BED)]
    filters = [
        "[0:a]aformat=sample_fmts=fltp:sample_rates=44100:channel_layouts=stereo[bed]"
    ]
    labels = ["[bed]"]
    for index, (path, start, _dur, _line) in enumerate(clips, start=1):
        cmd += ["-i", str(path)]
        ms = int(round(start * 1000))
        filters.append(
            f"[{index}:a]aresample=44100,"
            f"aformat=sample_fmts=fltp:channel_layouts=stereo,"
            f"adelay={ms}:all=1,volume={VOCAL_GAIN}[v{index}]"
        )
        labels.append(f"[v{index}]")
    n = len(labels)
    filters.append(
        f"{''.join(labels)}amix=inputs={n}:duration=longest:"
        f"dropout_transition=0:normalize=0[m]"
    )
    cmd += [
        "-filter_complex",
        ";".join(filters),
        "-map",
        "[m]",
        "-c:a",
        "pcm_f32le",
        str(MIX),
    ]
    print(" ", " ".join(cmd))
    subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)


def float_wav_samples(path):
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", str(path), "-f", "f32le", "-ac", "2", "pipe:1"],
        check=True,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
    )
    audio = np.frombuffer(proc.stdout, dtype=np.float32).astype(np.float64).copy()
    if audio.size == 0:
        sys.exit("mix decoded empty")
    return audio.reshape(-1, 2)


def encode(peak):
    gain = 0.95 / peak
    cmd = [
        "ffmpeg",
        "-y",
        "-i",
        str(MIX),
        "-af",
        f"volume={gain:.6f}",
        "-ar",
        "44100",
        "-ac",
        "2",
        "-c:a",
        "libmp3lame",
        "-b:a",
        "192k",
        str(OUT),
    ]
    print(" ", " ".join(cmd))
    subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)
    return gain


def probe_duration(path):
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [
            "ffprobe",
            "-v",
            "error",
            "-show_entries",
            "format=duration",
            "-of",
            "default=nw=1:nk=1",
            str(path),
        ],
        check=True,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        text=True,
    )
    return float(proc.stdout.strip())


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    print("espeak-ng:")
    clips = render_vocals(lines)
    for path, start, dur, line in clips:
        print(f"  {start:5.2f}s  {dur:4.2f}s  {path.name}  {line}")
    print("bed:")
    render_bed(clips)
    print("ffmpeg mix:")
    ffmpeg_mix(clips)
    mix = float_wav_samples(MIX)
    peak = float(np.max(np.abs(mix)))
    print(f"mix peak before makeup {peak:.3f}")
    if peak < 0.05:
        sys.exit("mix is silent")
    for path, start, dur, line in clips:
        a = int(start * SR)
        b = int((start + dur) * SR)
        vocal_rms = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(mix[a:b] ** 2)))
        print(f"  under {line!r:28} mix rms {vocal_rms:.3f}")
    gain = encode(peak)
    duration = probe_duration(OUT)
    decoded = subprocess.run(
        ["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", str(OUT), "-f", "f32le", "-ac", "1", "pipe:1"],
        check=True,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
    )
    mono = np.frombuffer(decoded.stdout, dtype=np.float32).astype(np.float64).copy()
    out_peak = float(np.max(np.abs(mono)))
    print(f"makeup gain {gain:.3f}")
    print(f"mp3 peak {out_peak:.3f}")
    print(f"duration {duration:.3f}s")
    if not (15.0 <= duration <= 60.0):
        sys.exit("duration outside 15–60 seconds")
    if out_peak < 0.05:
        sys.exit("mp3 is silent")
    # Per-second energy, so a dead bar is obvious without a speaker.
    seconds = len(mono) / SR
    print("rms by second:")
    for s in range(int(seconds)):
        chunk = mono[int(s * SR) : int((s + 1) * SR)]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Render the Stamp jingle.

Melody and drums are numpy. The vocal is espeak-ng, one clip per line of
lyrics.txt, so the recording says that file. ffmpeg mixes the vocal in front
of the bed and writes stamp-jingle.mp3.
"""

import subprocess
import sys
import wave
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
LYRICS = ROOT / "lyrics.txt"
BED = ROOT / "bed.wav"
MIX = ROOT / "mix.wav"
OUT = ROOT / "stamp-jingle.mp3"

SR = 44100
BPM = 120
BEAT = 60.0 / BPM
EIGHTH = BEAT / 2
DURATION = 26.0

# One cue per non-empty line in lyrics.txt. Stamp lines are slower.
# start seconds, speed wpm, pitch, amplitude, word gap (10 ms units).
CUES = [
    (1.85, 112, 44, 160, 2),
    (2.95, 138, 46, 150, 16),
    (6.50, 142, 46, 150, 8),
    (10.20, 136, 48, 155, 4),
    (11.45, 140, 46, 150, 14),
    (14.70, 138, 46, 150, 8),
    (16.70, 112, 44, 160, 2),
    (22.50, 112, 44, 160, 2),
]

BED_PEAK = 0.42
DUCK = 0.40
VOCAL_GAIN = 0.78

MIDI = {
    "D3": 50,
    "G3": 55,
    "B3": 59,
    "D4": 62,
    "G4": 67,
    "A4": 69,
    "B4": 71,
    "C5": 72,
    "D5": 74,
    "E5": 76,
    "F#5": 78,
    "G5": 79,
    "A5": 81,
}
THIRD_BELOW = {
    "E5": "C5",
    "D5": "B4",
    "B4": "G4",
    "G5": "E5",
    "A5": "F#5",
    "C5": "A4",
}
MOTIF_A = ["E5", "D5", "B4", "D5", "G5", "E5", "D5", "B4"]
MOTIF_B = ["D5", "B4", "E5", "G5", "A5", "G5", "E5", "D5"]

RNG = np.random.default_rng(20260328)


def midi_freq(name):
    return 440.0 * 2.0 ** ((MIDI[name] - 69) / 12.0)


def read_lines():
    lines = [ln.strip() for ln in LYRICS.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()]
    lines = [ln for ln in lines if ln]
    if len(lines) != len(CUES):
        sys.exit(f"lyrics.txt has {len(lines)} lines, expected {len(CUES)}")
    if not any(ln.lower().startswith("stamp") for ln in lines):
        sys.exit("lyrics.txt does not say Stamp")
    return lines


def write_wav(path, audio, sr):
    audio = np.asarray(audio, dtype=np.float64)
    audio = np.clip(audio, -1.0, 1.0)
    if audio.ndim == 1:
        pcm = (audio * 32767.0).astype(np.int16)
        channels = 1
    else:
        pcm = (audio * 32767.0).astype(np.int16)
        channels = audio.shape[1]
    with wave.open(str(path), "wb") as handle:
        handle.setnchannels(channels)
        handle.setsampwidth(2)
        handle.setframerate(sr)
        handle.writeframes(pcm.tobytes())


def read_wav(path):
    with wave.open(str(path), "rb") as handle:
        sr = handle.getframerate()
        channels = handle.getnchannels()
        frames = handle.getnframes()
        pcm = np.frombuffer(handle.readframes(frames), dtype=np.int16).astype(np.float64)
        pcm /= 32768.0
    if channels > 1:
        pcm = pcm.reshape(-1, channels)
    return pcm, sr


def trim_speech(samples, sr):
    """Drop espeak's padding. Keep the stop release on Stamp."""
    active = np.flatnonzero(np.abs(samples) > 0.015)
    if len(active) == 0:
        return samples
    start = max(0, active[0] - int(0.012 * sr))
    end = min(len(samples), active[-1] + int(0.07 * sr))
    return samples[start:end]


def render_vocals(lines):
    clips = []
    for index, (line, cue) in enumerate(zip(lines, CUES), start=1):
        start, speed, pitch, amp, gap = cue
        path = ROOT / f"vox-{index}.wav"
        cmd = [
            "espeak-ng",
            "-v",
            "en-gb",
            "-s",
            str(speed),
            "-p",
            str(pitch),
            "-a",
            str(amp),
            "-g",
            str(gap),
            "-z",
            "-w",
            str(path),
            line,
        ]
        print(" ", " ".join(cmd))
        subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)
        samples, sr = read_wav(path)
        if sr != 22050:
            sys.exit(f"unexpected espeak rate {sr}")
        samples = trim_speech(samples, sr)
        if float(np.max(np.abs(samples))) < 0.05:
            sys.exit(f"vocal clip {path.name} is silent")
        write_wav(path, samples, sr)
        clips.append((path, start, len(samples) / sr, line))
    for i in range(len(clips) - 1):
        end = clips[i][1] + clips[i][2]
        nxt = clips[i + 1][1]
        if end > nxt - 0.08:
            sys.exit(f"vocal overlap: line {i + 1} ends {end:.2f}, next starts {nxt:.2f}")
    last_end = clips[-1][1] + clips[-1][2]
    if last_end > DURATION - 0.5:
        sys.exit(f"last vocal ends at {last_end:.2f}, past the bed")
    return clips


def place(buf, sig, start):
    if start >= DURATION or len(sig) == 0:
        return
    i = int(round(start * SR))
    if i >= len(buf):
        return
    n = min(len(sig), len(buf) - i)
    buf[i : i + n] += sig[:n]


def env_fade(n, attack, decay):
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    env = np.exp(-t * decay)
    a = min(max(int(attack * SR), 1), n)
    env[:a] *= np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, a)
    f = min(max(int(0.012 * SR), 1), n // 2)
    env[-f:] *= np.linspace(1.0, 0.0, f)
    return env


def kick():
    n = int(SR * 0.20)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    freq = 46.0 + 130.0 * np.exp(-t * 24.0)
    phase = 2.0 * np.pi * np.cumsum(freq) / SR
    body = np.sin(phase) * np.exp(-t * 11.0)
    click_n = int(SR * 0.008)
    click = np.zeros(n)
    ct = np.arange(click_n) / SR
    click[:click_n] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * 1650.0 * ct) * np.exp(-ct * 320.0)
    return (body * 0.9 + click * 0.28) * env_end_guard(n)


def env_end_guard(n):
    # Returned as a multiplier of ones so kick math stays in one expression.
    return 1.0


def snare():
    n = int(SR * 0.16)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    noise = RNG.standard_normal(n)
    noise = noise - np.convolve(noise, np.ones(6) / 6.0, mode="same")
    body = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * 188.0 * t) * np.exp(-t * 32.0)
    sig = noise * np.exp(-t * 26.0) * 0.55 + body * 0.32
    return sig


def hat(open_hat=False):
    dur = 0.20 if open_hat else 0.045
    n = int(SR * dur)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    noise = RNG.standard_normal(n)
    hp = np.diff(noise, prepend=noise[0])
    hp = np.diff(hp, prepend=hp[0])
    decay = 12.0 if open_hat else 48.0
    metal = np.zeros(n)
    for freq in (3100.0, 5400.0, 7900.0):
        metal += np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * freq * t)
    sig = (hp * 0.75 + metal / 3.0 * 0.25) * np.exp(-t * decay)
    return sig * (0.22 if open_hat else 0.16)


def bass_note(name, beats, decay=5.0):
    freq = midi_freq(name)
    n = int(SR * beats * BEAT)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    wave = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * freq * t) + 0.35 * np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * freq * 2.0 * t)
    return wave * env_fade(n, 0.008, decay) * 0.55


def lead_note(name, beats, amp=0.32, decay=8.0):
    freq = midi_freq(name)
    n = int(SR * beats * BEAT)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    wave = (
        0.20 * np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * (freq * 0.5) * t)
        + 0.64 * np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * freq * t)
        + 0.16 * np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * freq * 2.0 * t)
    )
    return wave * env_fade(n, 0.006, decay) * amp


def add_drums(buf, t_end):
    first = 0
    last = int(np.floor((t_end - 1e-6) / BEAT))
    for i in range(first, last + 1):
        t = i * BEAT
        pos = i % 4
        if pos in (0, 2):
            place(buf, kick() * 0.95, t)
        if pos in (1, 3):
            place(buf, snare() * 0.72, t)
        place(buf, hat(False), t)
        off = t + BEAT * 0.5
        if pos == 3 and (i // 4) % 2 == 1:
            place(buf, hat(True), off)
        else:
            place(buf, hat(False) * 0.8, off)


def add_bass(buf, t_end):
    t = 0.0
    while t < t_end - 1e-6:
        place(buf, bass_note("G3", 1.35), t)
        place(buf, bass_note("D3", 1.15), t + 2.0 * BEAT)
        t += 4.0 * BEAT


def add_phrase(buf, t0, names, harmony=False):
    for i, name in enumerate(names):
        t = t0 + i * EIGHTH
        place(buf, lead_note(name, 0.46), t)
        if harmony and name in THIRD_BELOW:
            place(buf, lead_note(THIRD_BELOW[name], 0.46, amp=0.14, decay=8.0), t)


def add_chord(buf, t0):
    for name, amp in (("G4", 0.22), ("B4", 0.18), ("D5", 0.16), ("G5", 0.10)):
        freq = midi_freq(name)
        n = int(SR * 3.2)
        t = np.arange(n) / SR
        wave = (
            0.30 * np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * freq * t)
            + 0.12 * np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * freq * 2.0 * t)
        )
        env = np.exp(-t * 1.45)
        env[: int(0.02 * SR)] *= np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, int(0.02 * SR))
        place(buf, wave * env * amp, t0)
    place(buf, bass_note("G3", 4.0, decay=1.6) * 0.8, t0)
    place(buf, kick() * 0.8, t0)


def duck(mono, clips):
    env = np.ones(len(mono), dtype=np.float64)
    ramp_n = int(0.045 * SR)
    for _path, start, dur, _line in clips:
        a = max(0, int((start - 0.06) * SR))
        b = min(len(mono), int((start + dur + 0.10) * SR))
        seg = np.full(b - a, DUCK)
        r = min(ramp_n, max((b - a) // 2, 1))
        curve = 0.5 - 0.5 * np.cos(np.linspace(0.0, np.pi, r))
        seg[:r] = 1.0 + (DUCK - 1.0) * curve
        seg[-r:] = DUCK + (1.0 - DUCK) * curve
        env[a:b] = np.minimum(env[a:b], seg)
    return mono * env


def render_bed(clips):
    n = int(DURATION * SR)
    mono = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.float64)
    add_drums(mono, 22.30)
    add_bass(mono, 22.0)
    add_phrase(mono, 0.00, MOTIF_A[:6])
    add_phrase(mono, 8.95, ["A5", "G5", "E5", "D5"])
    add_phrase(mono, 17.60, MOTIF_A, harmony=True)
    add_phrase(mono, 19.60, MOTIF_B, harmony=True)
    add_phrase(mono, 21.60, ["B4", "D5"])
    add_chord(mono, 23.45)
    peak = float(np.max(np.abs(mono)))
    if peak < 1e-6:
        sys.exit("music bed is silent")
    mono *= BED_PEAK / peak
    mono = duck(mono, clips)
    fade_in = int(0.01 * SR)
    fade_out = int(0.20 * SR)
    mono[:fade_in] *= np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, fade_in)
    mono[-fade_out:] *= np.linspace(1.0, 0.0, fade_out)
    stereo = np.column_stack([mono, mono])
    write_wav(BED, stereo, SR)
    return stereo


def ffmpeg_mix(clips):
    cmd = ["ffmpeg", "-y", "-i", str(BED)]
    filters = [
        "[0:a]aformat=sample_fmts=fltp:sample_rates=44100:channel_layouts=stereo[bed]"
    ]
    labels = ["[bed]"]
    for index, (path, start, _dur, _line) in enumerate(clips, start=1):
        cmd += ["-i", str(path)]
        ms = int(round(start * 1000))
        filters.append(
            f"[{index}:a]aresample=44100,"
            f"aformat=sample_fmts=fltp:channel_layouts=stereo,"
            f"adelay={ms}:all=1,volume={VOCAL_GAIN}[v{index}]"
        )
        labels.append(f"[v{index}]")
    n = len(labels)
    filters.append(
        f"{''.join(labels)}amix=inputs={n}:duration=longest:"
        f"dropout_transition=0:normalize=0[m]"
    )
    cmd += [
        "-filter_complex",
        ";".join(filters),
        "-map",
        "[m]",
        "-c:a",
        "pcm_f32le",
        str(MIX),
    ]
    print(" ", " ".join(cmd))
    subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)


def float_wav_samples(path):
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", str(path), "-f", "f32le", "-ac", "2", "pipe:1"],
        check=True,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
    )
    audio = np.frombuffer(proc.stdout, dtype=np.float32).astype(np.float64).copy()
    if audio.size == 0:
        sys.exit("mix decoded empty")
    return audio.reshape(-1, 2)


def encode(peak):
    gain = 0.95 / peak
    cmd = [
        "ffmpeg",
        "-y",
        "-i",
        str(MIX),
        "-af",
        f"volume={gain:.6f}",
        "-ar",
        "44100",
        "-ac",
        "2",
        "-c:a",
        "libmp3lame",
        "-b:a",
        "192k",
        str(OUT),
    ]
    print(" ", " ".join(cmd))
    subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)
    return gain


def probe_duration(path):
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [
            "ffprobe",
            "-v",
            "error",
            "-show_entries",
            "format=duration",
            "-of",
            "default=nw=1:nk=1",
            str(path),
        ],
        check=True,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        text=True,
    )
    return float(proc.stdout.strip())


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    print("espeak-ng:")
    clips = render_vocals(lines)
    for path, start, dur, line in clips:
        print(f"  {start:5.2f}s  {dur:4.2f}s  {path.name}  {line}")
    print("bed:")
    render_bed(clips)
    print("ffmpeg mix:")
    ffmpeg_mix(clips)
    mix = float_wav_samples(MIX)
    peak = float(np.max(np.abs(mix)))
    print(f"mix peak before makeup {peak:.3f}")
    if peak < 0.05:
        sys.exit("mix is silent")
    for path, start, dur, line in clips:
        a = int(start * SR)
        b = int((start + dur) * SR)
        vocal_rms = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(mix[a:b] ** 2)))
        print(f"  under {line!r:28} mix rms {vocal_rms:.3f}")
    gain = encode(peak)
    duration = probe_duration(OUT)
    decoded = subprocess.run(
        ["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", str(OUT), "-f", "f32le", "-ac", "1", "pipe:1"],
        check=True,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
    )
    mono = np.frombuffer(decoded.stdout, dtype=np.float32).astype(np.float64).copy()
    out_peak = float(np.max(np.abs(mono)))
    print(f"makeup gain {gain:.3f}")
    print(f"mp3 peak {out_peak:.3f}")
    print(f"duration {duration:.3f}s")
    if not (15.0 <= duration <= 60.0):
        sys.exit("duration outside 15–60 seconds")
    if out_peak < 0.05:
        sys.exit("mp3 is silent")
    # Per-second energy, so a dead bar is obvious without a speaker.
    seconds = len(mono) / SR
    print("rms by second:")
    for s in range(int(seconds)):
        chunk = mono[int(s * SR) : int((s + 1) * SR)]
        rms = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(chunk ** 2)))
        print(f"  {s:02d}  {rms:.3f}  {'#' * int(rms * 80)}")
    MIX.unlink(missing_ok=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import wave, numpy as np
from pathlib import Path
root = Path("/home/jacob/Documents/INFO123 Project/audio")

def load(p):
    w = wave.open(str(p))
    sr = w.getframerate(); ch = w.getnchannels()
    x = np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()), np.int16).astype(np.float64)/32768
    if ch>1: x = x.reshape(-1, ch).mean(axis=1)
    return x, sr

def bands(x, sr):
    spec = np.abs(np.fft.rfft(x * np.hanning(len(x))))
    freqs = np.fft.rfftfreq(len(x), 1/sr)
    def e(a,b):
        m = (freqs>=a)&(freqs<b)
        return float(np.sqrt(np.mean(spec[m]**2)))

1→# Stamp product spec

Locked from your choices in Stage 1. One number is a planning assumption and is marked as such: the manufactured cost that sits under the $5.00 shelf price.

## What a Stamp is

A Stamp is a 10 g disc of spread on a food-safe release film, nested in a printed card sheet. You peel one off and press it onto hot toast. The heat softens it into a layer. No knife and no open jar.

An unopened sheet lives in a pantry for 12 months. The home recipes below are kitchen prototypes, eaten from the fridge within 7 days. Only the industrial formulas are the products we sell, and only those claim the 12-month date.
10→
## Who it is for

Someone who eats toast away from a full kitchen: a flat, an office, a hall, or a bag. They want a decided portion of flavour without carrying a jar or washing a knife.

## Range and price

| Sheet | Contents | Net weight | Shelf price | Price per 100 g |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Salted Butter | 8 butter stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
20→| Raspberry | 8 raspberry stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
| Yeast extract | 8 yeast-extract stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
| Peanut | 8 peanut stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
| Mixed | 2 of each flavour | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |

$6.25 per 100 g sits above about 90% of branded spread SKUs in the cleaned dataset (90th percentile $5.19 per 100 g). The median branded spread is $2.15 per 100 g. Fix & Fogg's SKUs sit around $2.65 per 100 g. The gap is the portion film and the card, which a jar does not have. The marker is on `data/figures/03-branded-spreads-price-per-100g.png`.

## How to use it

1. Keep the sheet in a pantry.
30→2. Peel one stamp off the release film.
3. Press it onto hot toast.
4. Wait a few seconds. The residual heat lays the spread across the slice.

## Claims we will make

- Peel and press onto hot toast.
- One stamp is one portion, 10 g.
- Four flavours, sold as single-flavour sheets and a mixed sheet.
- No knife and no jar.
40→- Unopened sheet, 12 months in a pantry.

## Claims we will not make

- Health treatment, "better for you," low-sugar, organic, or gluten-free.
- That Salted Butter is a pat of fridge butter. The sold disc is a shelf-stable butter spread. In Australia and New Zealand the word butter on its own is a dairy-identity standard (milkfat, no added oil). The sheet shows the flavour name, then the word spread. The ingredient list names cultured butterfat.
- That Yeast extract is Marmite or Vegemite. Those names, jars, and trade dress do not appear on the pack or the site.

## Allergens

50→| Flavour | Contains | Also stated on every sheet |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Salted Butter | Milk | Made in a facility that handles milk and peanuts. |
| Raspberry | No major allergen in the recipe | Same facility statement. |
| Yeast extract | Gluten (barley) | Same facility statement. |
| Peanut | Peanuts | Same facility statement. |
| Mixed | Milk, gluten, peanuts | Same facility statement. |

## Home prototypes

60→Each batch is eight stamps, 80 g. Shape into 10 g discs, press each onto a square of baking paper, and chill until they hold. Eat within 7 days. These batches test flavour and the peel-and-press gesture. They are not the shelf-stable product.

**Salted Butter.** 78 g unsalted butter, softened, beaten with 2 g fine salt.

**Raspberry.** 120 g raspberries, 30 g caster sugar, and 5 g lemon juice, cooked and stirred until 80 g of thick paste remains. Cool before portioning.

**Yeast extract.** 55 g yeast extract, 15 g tomato paste, 8 g black treacle, and 2 g salt, warmed and stirred into a paste that holds a disc. This prototypes the salty yeast flavour. The sold paste is the industrial formula below, not a scooped jar of an existing brand.

**Peanut.** 85 g roasted peanuts and 1.5 g fine salt, ground to a firm paste and portioned before the oil separates.

70→## Industrial formulas

Deposit 10 g ± 0.5 g onto release film, cut, nest eight discs in a card sheet, and flow-wrap. A failed weight check or a film that will not release is a rejected stamp, not a sheet that ships. Shelf life is 12 months, ambient, unopened.

**Salted Butter.** Cultured butterfat and salt at the same 2 g salt per 78 g fat as the home batch. Moisture is low enough that the sealed disc stays stable in a pantry and still softens on hot toast. No added oil, so the dairy description stays honest. On the sheet the flavour name is Salted Butter and the word under it is spread.

**Raspberry.** The home ratio (raspberry, sugar, lemon), cooked to the same thick paste and deposited at 10 g. Stability comes from the solids in the cook and the seal, not from a preservative claim. The label says it is made with 150 g of raspberries per 100 g, which is this cook: 120 g of fruit reduced to 80 g.

**Yeast extract.** Our yeast-extract paste, deposited at 10 g: yeast extract 80%, barley malt extract 15.5%, salt 2.5%, vegetable concentrate 2%. The salt share matches the home batch. Barley malt extract sits above salt, and vegetable concentrate sits below it, so the ingredient list stays in the order above. Contains gluten. The flavour name is Yeast extract. The pack does not say Marmite or Vegemite.

80→**Peanut.** Roasted peanuts 96%, vegetable fat 2.3% as the hard-fat stabiliser, and salt 1.7%, close to the 1.5 g salt in the home batch. The stabiliser keeps the disc from oiling off across 12 months. Contains peanuts.

The nutrition panels on the backs are calculated from these proportions and published composition figures. They are not a laboratory assay.

## Manufactured cost (assumption)

You chose the $5.00 shelf price. You did not choose a cost target. Until Stage 4 prices a real manufacturer, the spec uses this stack:

| | Per sheet | Per stamp |
| --- | --- | --- |
90→| Shelf price | $5.00 | $0.63 |
| Retailer keeps 35% | $1.75 | $0.22 |
| Stamp receives | $3.25 | $0.41 |
| Target manufactured cost | $1.50 | $0.19 |

$1.50 is 30% of the shelf price. The $1.75 left on Stamp's side of the wholesale price has to carry film, card, freight, and contribution. Change the 35% or the $1.50 and the recipes do not change; the Stage 4 manufacturer comparison does.

## Still open

Distribution (where a sheet is bought) is not decided. The manufacturer is Stage 4. The wordmark, colours, and pack art are in `brand/identity.md`.

args.CodeContent:
# Sheet making and release

Figure: `diagrams/process.png`, from `diagrams/process.mmd`.

The pass path is order in, batch deposit onto film, cut, nest, check, pack, dispatch. At the check, a stamp outside 10 g ± 0.5 g, or a film that will not release, goes to Reject. That path stops. It does not join Pack or Dispatch, and the stamp does not ship.

## Bottlenecks

**1. Deposit weight.** Peanut paste and yeast extract thicken or slacken while they sit in the hopper, so the depositor drifts outside 10 g ± 0.5 g and the check rejects a run of discs.

Response: stop the depositor. Weigh the next five discs. Restart only when all five sit between 9.5 g and 10.5 g. Discs that failed are rejected and are not nested.

**2. Release film.** A roll that will not peel fails only after spread is already on it, so one bad roll can reject a whole deposit run before pack.

Response: peel-test the first eight discs of each new roll. If one will not release, stop, quarantine that roll, and reject every stamp already on it. Load a fresh roll and test eight more before nesting continues. Nothing from the failed roll is packed or dispatched.

args.CodeContent:
# Information notes

Entities in `diagrams/erd.mmd`: Customer, Order, OrderLine (the order line), Sheet (the sellable pack), Product (the flavour), Batch, Manufacturer, Campaign.

A Sheet includes one Product when the pack is a single flavour (8 stamps). The mixed sheet includes all four Products, two stamps of each. A Batch deposits one Product. A Batch supplies a Sheet only when the stamps passed the check. A Batch with release_rejects above zero failed release and those stamps are not on a dispatched Sheet.

## KPIs

**1. Repeat purchase rate.** Entity: Customer, counted from Order.

Formula: number of Customers with two or more Orders, divided by the number of Customers with at least one Order.

**2. Stamps per order.** Entity: OrderLine, using Sheet.

Formula: sum of (OrderLine.sheet_qty times Sheet.stamps_on_sheet) across all order lines, divided by the number of Orders. stamps_on_sheet is 8 on every pack, including mixed.

**3. On-time dispatch rate.** Entity: Order.

Formula: number of Orders whose dispatched_on is on or before promised_dispatch, divided by the number of Orders that have a dispatched_on. An order with no dispatch date is not in this rate.

**4. Batch rejection rate.** Entity: Batch.

Formula: (sum of weight_rejects + sum of release_rejects) divided by sum of stamps_checked. A weight reject is a stamp outside 10 g ± 0.5 g. A release reject is a stamp whose film will not release. Each checked stamp is counted once, under the first failure found. Rejected stamps are not packed and are not dispatched.

**5. Gross margin per sheet after manufacturer cost.** Entity: Sheet, for the shelf price. The cost term is an assumption, not a figure stored on Manufacturer, and not a quote from Griffiths & Co.

Formula, labelled as an assumption: shelf price $5.00, retailer share 35% ($1.75), so Stamp receives $5.00 times (1 minus 0.35) = $3.25. Subtract the assumed manufactured cost of $1.50. Gross margin per sheet = $3.25 minus $1.50 = $1.75. Change the 35% or the $1.50 and this margin changes. The recipes do not.

## Questions this model can answer

Which flavour is reordered? A flavour is a Product. Follow Customer to Order to OrderLine to Sheet to Product. A reorder of a flavour is a later Order from the same Customer for a single-flavour Sheet whose only included Product is that flavour. A mixed Sheet is a separate pack (two of each), not a reorder of one flavour.

Which batch failed release? Read Batch.release_rejects. Any Batch with release_rejects above zero failed the film-release check. Those stamps do not supply a Sheet and do not go to dispatch. Manufacturer says who ran that batch.

## Question this model cannot answer

Whether a flavour has a medical effect. No entity records a symptom, a diagnosis, a test result, or any health outcome. Orders, batches, and flavours cannot support that claim, and the product does not make it.

The Mermaid linkStyle color property is invalid in this version, or the hash symbol was corrupted.

The `#` in the linkStyle color value is likely being parsed as a comment. I will remove the color property from that line and rely on the existing node classDef for red styling.

The failure path will loop back to the Reject node. This prevents any fall-through to dispatch.

A self-loop back to Reject might render poorly in Mermaid. I will add an explicit end node with a clear label such as "Do not pack. Do not dispatch." to make the failure path obvious without relying on a cycle.

I will keep only one Reject node. The back-edge from Reject to the Check node will carry a label explaining that only the next stamp is reprocessed and the failed one stays rejected.

A loop back to the Check node risks looking like a recheck, so I will keep the failure path as a terminal Reject node with an unmistakable label.

A self-cycle loop was rejected as too silly. I will render the charts and verify the failure path does not reach dispatch. I will also check if erd.png exists and fix any ERD entity naming issues. The ERD attribute blocks will be removed entirely. Mermaid requires types for attributes, so omitting them avoids technical database semantics while preserving the business-level model.

The KPI formulas reference specific attribute names, so the ERD must retain them. The Mermaid syntax requires type names, but the absence of keys, foreign keys, and junction tables keeps the model business-level. Standard data types will be kept rather than replaced with non-technical labels.

The manufacturer page lists a phone number but no email address. The contact details were copied exactly from the source. The process diagram is tall at 4000 pixels, yet it remains well composed and sharp at scale two.

The failure path will remain a simple termination rather than looping back to Reject. A self-loop on the reject box risks looking messy and could degrade the diagram. The current design is sufficient and clear.

Gross margin arithmetic checks out. The stamps-per-order formula correctly totals eight stamps per order. Repeat purchase rate references Customer and Order entities present in the ERD. Campaign cardinality is properly represented with an optional circle on Campaign and a crow's foot on Order.

The ERD correctly models Product to Sheet as many-to-many with the "included on" label. Batch to Sheet is also many-to-many under "supplies if the check passes". The $1.50 manufactured cost stays labelled as an assumption unless the manufacturer page states a real price, in which case quote that price separately and keep the assumption labelled.

Claims you must not make: health treatment, better for you, low-sugar, organic, gluten-free. Salted Butter is a shelf-stable butter spread, not a pat of fridge butter. Yeast extract is not Marmite or Vegemite and is not called Stampmite. It contains gluten from barley. Peanut contains peanuts. Salted Butter contains milk. Every sheet is made in a facility that handles milk and peanuts. Nutrition figures on the pack backs are calculated, not lab assays. Do not present them as tested. No fake certification marks.

1→# INFO123 — Deliverable build plan

**Due:** 16 October 2026, 5:00 pm, via Learn.
**Who builds it:** this project, in this workspace. No Gemini, Mistral, ChatGPT, Figma, Suno, or other AI product is part of the build.
**Product:** Stamp, a line of peel-and-press spread portions for toast. Each portion sits on a release film like a sticker. You peel one off and press it onto hot toast; the heat softens it into a layer. No knife, no open jar.

The brief’s chat-by-chat workflow is not the plan. The plan is the sequence that produces the files and URLs Learn marks.

---
10→
## What we are shipping

| Deliverable | File or URL | Pass condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Business plan | `business-plan/Stamp-business-plan.pdf` | One PDF, 1,500–2,500 words excluding images. Contains the market figures, logo, pack shot, social ad, process diagram, and ERD, each beside the paragraph that uses it. Covers product, market, competitors, marketing, operations, and information systems. |
| Jingle | `audio/stamp-jingle.mp3` | Plays, 15–60 seconds, names Stamp and the toast-sticker idea. |
| Website | Vercel production URL | Loads with no login. Landing page for Stamp. |
| Chatbot | `{site}/chat` | Same deployment. Answers product questions from the locked spec. No login. |
| Video | `.mp4` you record from the slide deck we build | Talking-head, 2–3 minutes, hard stop 3:29. Pitch finishes by 1:00. |
20→| Chat-session form | Learn form | Still a graded item. We submit the link to this project’s sessions. It is not a separate production stage. |

Missing the video scores 0/25. Missing the chat-session form scores an E. The PDF, jingle, site, and chatbot are the other four core items.

---

## Product spec we will build against

Locked now, so the logo, pack, site, bot, jingle, and PDF describe the same thing.

30→| Item | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Brand and product name | **Stamp** |
| Format | A thin, single-serve disc of spread on a food-safe release film, nested in a printed card sheet. Peel, press onto hot toast, done. |
| Category in the dataset | Spreads |
| Launch line | Four flavours, locked with you: Salted Butter, Raspberry, Yeast extract, Peanut. |
| Packs | An 8-stamp sheet of one flavour (10 g each, 80 g), and a mixed sheet with two of each. $5.00 a sheet. |
| Buyer | Someone who eats toast away from a full kitchen: a flat, an office, a hall, a school bag. They want flavour without a knife or a jar. |
| Position | Pantry-stable for 12 months. $5.00 a sheet is $6.25 per 100 g, above about 90% of branded spread SKUs. |
| Allergen we will state | Peanut contains peanuts. Salted Butter is dairy. Yeast extract contains gluten from barley. Full list is in `brand/product-spec.md`. |
40→| Claims we will make | Peel-and-press, one portion, even cover, four flavours, no knife. |
| Claims we will not make | Health treatment, organic, gluten-free, low-sugar, or “better for you,” unless a finished recipe actually supports that sentence. No fake certification marks on the pack. |

Raw dataset baseline the market section starts from (revenue column, as published, in thousands of NZD):

| Year | Spreads revenue (thousands NZD) | Spreads units (thousands) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2022 | 274,859 | 32,758 |
| 2023 | 305,274 | 36,273 |
| 2024 | 315,577 | 37,946 |
50→| 2025 | 341,356 | 40,213 |

That is about 24% revenue growth from 2022 to 2025. Premium tier revenue inside spreads rose faster than value (about 29% vs about 8%). The sheet has 41 spread brands and 154 spread product names. None of those names describe a portion, sachet, pod, or peel-and-press format. Stage 1 cleans the known bad price cells before any chart is final, then these totals are recomputed and only the recomputed figures go in the PDF.

Nearest jar brands already in the file, for the competitor section: Fix & Fogg, Pic's, Nutella, Vegemite, Bega, Sanitarium, Pams, and the honey brands (Airborne, Egmont, Manuka Doctor). Live shelf prices are collected in Stage 5 from retailer or brand pages.

---

## Repository layout

60→```text
INFO123 Project/
  PLAN.md
  nz_breakfast_sales_2022_2025.xlsx
  data/                 cleaned table, figure script, PNGs
  brand/                logo, pack, ad, prompts, palette
  audio/                lyrics, render script, mp3
  diagrams/             process and ERD source plus PNG
  business-plan/        copy, build script, PDF
  website/              SvelteKit app
70→  presentation/         pitch deck and timing sheet
```

One product file, `brand/product-spec.md`, is the source for the PDF, the site copy, the chatbot answers, and the jingle hook. Later stages read it. They do not invent a second version of the product.

---

## Stage 1 — Product lock and market figures

**Produces:** the spec every later asset quotes, and the charts that go in the PDF.
80→
1. Write `brand/product-spec.md`: format, four flavours, both pack types, use steps, buyer, claims list, allergen list, home recipe per flavour, and an industrial version (deposit onto release film, cut, nest in a sheet, flow-wrap). Industrial constraints: target cost per stamp, ambient or chilled shelf life, and the claim ban from the table above.
2. Clean `nz_breakfast_sales_2022_2025.xlsx` with a Python script into `data/spreads-clean.csv`.
   - A row is name + brand + weight + quarter. Same name with two weights is two SKUs.
   - Replace unit prices above $40 when units and revenue imply a normal shelf price (`revenue ÷ units`). Log each replacement.
   - Impute a missing revenue or units only when the surviving price makes the identity `price × units ≈ revenue` hold.
   - Parse weight into grams and pack count.
3. Recompute spreads revenue and units by year, by price tier, and by brand. Build three PNG figures in `data/figures/`:
   - Quarterly spreads revenue, 2022-Q1 through 2025-Q4, with the other three categories as context.
   - 2022 vs 2025 spreads revenue by price tier.
90→   - Price per 100 g for branded spreads, with the Stamp sheet price marked once it is chosen.
4. Set the sheet price and the mixed-sheet price from that per-100 g band. Record both in the product spec.

**Done when:** the spec has recipes, prices, and claims; the three PNGs exist; every number on them matches the cleaned CSV.

## Stage 2 — Logo, pack, and social ad

**Produces:** the three images the PDF and the site share.

Visual system, fixed before generation:
100→
- Wordmark: STAMP, all capitals. A custom drawing in the Toundra construction (heavy stems, round feet, semicircular arches). No symbol.
- One colour pair on every flavour: light purple `#E24BFF` and dark purple `#3B0764`. Dark on light, the same relationship as Toundra's forest green on lime. Flavour is type, not a second colour.
- Manrope is the text face only. It is not the wordmark.
- Pack: flat front. Forest field, purple STAMP, flavour name, and the line “Peel. Press. Toast.”
- Ad: 4:5, purple field, STAMP, and the same line.

Generation order: logo first, then pack and ad using the logo as the reference image so the mark matches. Save the final files as `brand/logo.png`, `brand/pack.png`, and `brand/ad.png`. Keep the earlier frames in `brand/explorations/` so the finals are the ones the other stages use.

**Done when:** the three finals show the same name, the same four flavours, and no certification badges we do not hold.
110→
## Stage 3 — Jingle

**Produces:** `audio/stamp-jingle.mp3`.

Built locally. No music-generation service.

1. Write a 20–40 second lyric in `audio/lyrics.txt`. The hook says “Stamp” and the action peel / press / toast. One flavour can be named. Tone matches the pack: short, bright, not a wellness ad.
2. Render a melody and a simple drum bed in Python (numpy) and mix a vocal with a local speech engine (`espeak-ng` or `festival`). Export with ffmpeg.
3. Measure the file with `ffprobe`. Trim or rewrite until the duration is inside 15–60 seconds and the product name is intelligible.
120→
**Done when:** the mp3 plays on its own, the duration check passes, and the lyric file matches the recording.

## Stage 4 — Process diagram and ERD

**Produces:** the two figures the PDF still needs, plus the facts printed next to them.

1. Pick one real New Zealand company that can deposit or portion-pack a spread. Record the trading name, the page the contact details came from, the location, and why the process fits a film-and-sheet format. Save this in `diagrams/manufacturer.md`.
2. Critical process: **sheet making and release** — order in, batch deposit onto film, cut, nest, check, pack, dispatch. That is the process whose failure means a customer gets no breakfast. Draw it as a Mermaid flowchart with one failure path (failed weight check or film that will not release). Export `diagrams/process.png`. Write two bottlenecks and the operational response under the figure notes.
3. Business-level entities: Product (flavour), Sheet (the sellable pack), Customer, Order, Order line, Batch, Manufacturer, Campaign. Five KPIs, each with a formula and the entity it comes from:
130→   - repeat purchase rate
   - stamps per order
   - on-time dispatch rate
   - batch rejection rate
   - gross margin per sheet after manufacturer cost
4. Mermaid `erDiagram` to `diagrams/erd.png`. Short note on two questions this model can answer (which flavour is reordered, which batch failed release) and one it cannot (a medical effect).

**Done when:** both PNGs render cleanly, the manufacturer contact is copied from a page we opened, and the KPI list matches the ERD entities.

## Stage 5 — Business plan PDF
140→
**Produces:** `business-plan/Stamp-business-plan.pdf`.

A Python build script (`business-plan/build_pdf.py`, reportlab) lays the document out. Copy lives in `business-plan/copy.md` so the word count is checkable before export. Images are placed by the script from the paths above, not pasted by hand into a chat export.

| Section | Words | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cover | — | STAMP wordmark, logo, your name, date |
| Executive summary | 180–220 | Format, buyer, the spreads growth result, the jar-vs-stamp difference |
| Product | 300–400 | Four flavours, both recipes in brief, pack, price, how to use |
150→| Market | 300–400 | Cleaned figures and what they justify. Units labelled as NZD, not “thousands” left ambiguous. |
| Competitors | 250–350 | Three jar competitors with a sourced price, pack size, and the format difference |
| Customer and brand | 150–200 | Buyer, logo, pack shot, the line of ad copy |
| Marketing | 250–350 | Channel (Instagram and short video), the ad, where the jingle runs, two or three real NZ podcasts whose pages we opened |
| Operations | 200–280 | Manufacturer, the sheet-making process, the diagram, two bottlenecks |
| Information | 200–280 | Five KPIs, the ERD, two decisions the data supports |
| First 90 days | 80–120 | Assumptions labelled as assumptions |

Word count is the prose only. The script fails the build if the count falls outside 1,500–2,500. After export, render the PDF pages to images and read them: spelling of STAMP, figure legibility, no empty boxes, captions that state a conclusion.

160→**Done when:** the PDF builds in one command, the word-count check passes, and all six image types are visible in the rendered pages.

## Stage 6 — Website (SvelteKit)

**Produces:** a SvelteKit app in `website/` that we can deploy.

| Choice | Spec |
| --- | --- |
| Framework | SvelteKit, TypeScript |
| Adapter | `@sveltejs/adapter-vercel` |
170→| Styling | Project CSS. Palette and type from Stage 2. No component library. |
| Rendering | Marketing routes prerendered. |
| Assets | Logo, pack, and ad copied into `website/static/` from `brand/`. |
| Copy | Pulled from `brand/product-spec.md`. The site does not add claims the spec forbids. |

Routes:

| Path | Page |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | Landing. What a Stamp is, the peel-press-toast sequence, the four flavours, the sheet price, one market sentence, the pack image. |
180→| `/flavours` | One block per flavour: name, taste, allergen, which sheet it is on. |
| `/chat` | Built in Stage 7. Linked in the header from the start so the nav does not change after deploy. |

No cart and no payment. The call to action is the product explanation and the support chat. A fake checkout is out of scope.

**Done when:** `npm run build` succeeds, `/` and `/flavours` show the real pack and the locked prices, and a logged-out browser can read both.

## Stage 7 — Support chatbot

**Produces:** `/chat` on the same app. The public chatbot URL is the site URL plus `/chat`.
190→
The bot is ours. It does not call another model at runtime.

- Knowledge is a typed module, `website/src/lib/knowledge.ts`, authored from the product spec: what a Stamp is, how to apply it, the four flavours, allergens, prices, pack contents, where it will be sold (direct, at launch), and a crushed-sheet complaint reply.
- Matching is intentional and small: normalise the question, score it against those topics, return the authored answer. A question that does not match gets a short reply listing what the bot can answer.
- Hard refusals, also authored: medical advice, and any “is it organic / gluten-free / low-sugar?” question, which is answered with the claim ban.
- The page looks like a support chat: a transcript, a text field, Stamp’s voice in short sentences.

2. How do I use it?
3. What flavours are there?
4. Does the Peanut stamp contain nuts?
5. Is it gluten-free?

210→
**Done when:** those ten questions return the spec’s answers, questions 5 and 9 stay inside the claim ban, and the page is reachable at `/chat`.

## Stage 8 — Deploy on Vercel

**Produces:** a production URL with no login.

1. Vercel project, root directory `website`, framework SvelteKit, adapter already set.
2. Production deploy from this project.
3. Open the production origin and `/chat` in a private window. Confirm images load, prices match the PDF, and one chat question is answered.

1→# Stamp product spec

Locked from your choices in Stage 1. One number is a planning assumption and is marked as such: the manufactured cost that sits under the $5.00 shelf price.

## What a Stamp is

A Stamp is a 10 g disc of spread on a food-safe release film, nested in a printed card sheet. You peel one off and press it onto hot toast. The heat softens it into a layer. No knife and no open jar.

An unopened sheet lives in a pantry for 12 months. The home recipes below are kitchen prototypes, eaten from the fridge within 7 days. Only the industrial formulas are the products we sell, and only those claim the 12-month date.
10→
## Who it is for

Someone who eats toast away from a full kitchen: a flat, an office, a hall, or a bag. They want a decided portion of flavour without carrying a jar or washing a knife.

## Range and price

| Sheet | Contents | Net weight | Shelf price | Price per 100 g |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Salted Butter | 8 butter stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
20→| Raspberry | 8 raspberry stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
| Yeast extract | 8 yeast-extract stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
| Peanut | 8 peanut stamps | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |
| Mixed | 2 of each flavour | 80 g | $5.00 | $6.25 |

$6.25 per 100 g sits above about 90% of branded spread SKUs in the cleaned dataset (90th percentile $5.19 per 100 g). The median branded spread is $2.15 per 100 g. Fix & Fogg's SKUs sit around $2.65 per 100 g. The gap is the portion film and the card, which a jar does not have. The marker is on `data/figures/03-branded-spreads-price-per-100g.png`.

## How to use it

1. Keep the sheet in a pantry.
30→2. Peel one stamp off the release film.
3. Press it onto hot toast.
4. Wait a few seconds. The residual heat lays the spread across the slice.

## Claims we will make

- Peel and press onto hot toast.
- One stamp is one portion, 10 g.
- Four flavours, sold as single-flavour sheets and a mixed sheet.
- No knife and no jar.
40→- Unopened sheet, 12 months in a pantry.

## Claims we will not make

- Health treatment, "better for you," low-sugar, organic, or gluten-free.
- That Salted Butter is a pat of fridge butter. The sold disc is a shelf-stable butter spread. In Australia and New Zealand the word butter on its own is a dairy-identity standard (milkfat, no added oil). The sheet shows the flavour name, then the word spread. The ingredient list names cultured butterfat.
- That Yeast extract is Marmite or Vegemite. Those names, jars, and trade dress do not appear on the pack or the site.

## Allergens

50→| Flavour | Contains | Also stated on every sheet |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Salted Butter | Milk | Made in a facility that handles milk and peanuts. |
| Raspberry | No major allergen in the recipe | Same facility statement. |
| Yeast extract | Gluten (barley) | Same facility statement. |
| Peanut | Peanuts | Same facility statement. |
| Mixed | Milk, gluten, peanuts | Same facility statement. |

## Home prototypes

60→Each batch is eight stamps, 80 g. Shape into 10 g discs, press each onto a square of baking paper, and chill until they hold. Eat within 7 days. These batches test flavour and the peel-and-press gesture. They are not the shelf-stable product.

**Salted Butter.** 78 g unsalted butter, softened, beaten with 2 g fine salt.

**Raspberry.** 120 g raspberries, 30 g caster sugar, and 5 g lemon juice, cooked and stirred until 80 g of thick paste remains. Cool before portioning.

**Yeast extract.** 55 g yeast extract, 15 g tomato paste, 8 g black treacle, and 2 g salt, warmed and stirred into a paste that holds a disc. This prototypes the salty yeast flavour. The sold paste is the industrial formula below, not a scooped jar of an existing brand.

**Peanut.** 85 g roasted peanuts and 1.5 g fine salt, ground to a firm paste and portioned before the oil separates.

70→## Industrial formulas

Deposit 10 g ± 0.5 g onto release film, cut, nest eight discs in a card sheet, and flow-wrap. A failed weight check or a film that will not release is a rejected stamp, not a sheet that ships. Shelf life is 12 months, ambient, unopened.

**Salted Butter.** Cultured butterfat and salt at the same 2 g salt per 78 g fat as the home batch. Moisture is low enough that the sealed disc stays stable in a pantry and still softens on hot toast. No added oil, so the dairy description stays honest. On the sheet the flavour name is Salted Butter and the word under it is spread.

**Raspberry.** The home ratio (raspberry, sugar, lemon), cooked to the same thick paste and deposited at 10 g. Stability comes from the solids in the cook and the seal, not from a preservative claim. The label says it is made with 150 g of raspberries per 100 g, which is this cook: 120 g of fruit reduced to 80 g.

**Yeast extract.** Our yeast-extract paste, deposited at 10 g: yeast extract 80%, barley malt extract 15.5%, salt 2.5%, vegetable concentrate 2%. The salt share matches the home batch. Barley malt extract sits above salt, and vegetable concentrate sits below it, so the ingredient list stays in the order above. Contains gluten. The flavour name is Yeast extract. The pack does not say Marmite or Vegemite.

80→**Peanut.** Roasted peanuts 96%, vegetable fat 2.3% as the hard-fat stabiliser, and salt 1.7%, close to the 1.5 g salt in the home batch. The stabiliser keeps the disc from oiling off across 12 months. Contains peanuts.

The nutrition panels on the backs are calculated from these proportions and published composition figures. They are not a laboratory assay.

## Manufactured cost (assumption)

You chose the $5.00 shelf price. You did not choose a cost target. Until Stage 4 prices a real manufacturer, the spec uses this stack:

| | Per sheet | Per stamp |
| --- | --- | --- |
90→| Shelf price | $5.00 | $0.63 |
| Retailer keeps 35% | $1.75 | $0.22 |
| Stamp receives | $3.25 | $0.41 |
| Target manufactured cost | $1.50 | $0.19 |

$1.50 is 30% of the shelf price. The $1.75 left on Stamp's side of the wholesale price has to carry film, card, freight, and contribution. Change the 35% or the $1.50 and the recipes do not change; the Stage 4 manufacturer comparison does.

## Still open

Distribution (where a sheet is bought) is not decided. The manufacturer is Stage 4. The wordmark, colours, and pack art are in `brand/identity.md`.
100→
