Colors are dark purple #3B0764, light purple #E24BFF, cream background #FFF8FC, and near-black text #1A1024. The cover page will use a full dark or light purple background with the existing logo centered.

The cover page will use the existing logo.png as-is. It will display "Business plan", the user's name, 30 September 2026, and a one-line tagline. Section headings will be dark purple in Manrope type. Body text will use Manrope. Image captions will be italic and smaller, stating a conclusion.

ReportLab platypus will handle word wrapping for paragraphs, while images will be sized to prevent collisions.

Deciding between BaseDocTemplate and SimpleDocTemplate for the PDF structure. Wide market charts will sit full-width under their paragraph. Pack shots, logo, and ad images will form a side-by-side row in the customer section.

The customer section will pair the logo, pack shot, and social ad. The operations section will use the process diagram, and the information section will use the ERD. The PDF will contain seven images in total: two market figures, the logo, the pack shot, the social ad, the process diagram, and the ERD. The target page count is ten to fourteen pages. Charts and diagrams will be rendered at full content width.

Reserve Force commanders and soldiers play a crucial role in supplementing the full-time regular component of the NZ Army.  It is essential they can seamlessly integrate into the Regular Force to provide combat readiness that will meet the range of security situations the New Zealand Defence Force is required to act on.

### On today’s show

### 09:05 Union survey finds parents keen on publicly-funded ECE system

A new survey of parents and family members has found there is growing support for a publicly-funded early childhood education system. Around 70 per cent of the early childhood education sector is made up of private, for-profit providers. The survey, undertaken by the union for early childhood and primary schools, NZEI, asked parents and whanau a range of questions about their access to ECE and their experiences. 92 per cent of respondents support the establishment of a public early childhood education system that’s free to attend, just like schools. This is up from 78.2 per cent in last year’s survey. Parent and former ECE teacher of 15 years Claire Southee and kindergarten head teacher Sally Griffin are on the line.

![Early childhood centre learning. (File pic)](https://media.rnztools.nz/rnz/image/upload/s--3ZQ1Dt6D--/ar_16:10,c_fill,f_auto,g_auto,q_auto,w_1050/v1643489003/4NRYEMZ_image_crop_60982?_a=BACCd2AD)

Photo: 123rf 

### 09:20 Political focus on supermarket structure

Supermarket reform has become a key focus of the election campaign. National and New Zealand First want to split Foodstuffs in two - separating New World and Pak n Save, while Labour would force Foodstuffs and Woolworths to run their wholesale arms independently of the retail side. The Greens' policy is to create a state-owned KiwiMart. University of Auckland senior marketing lecturer Drew Franklin says structural reform has been shown to work overseas where it lowers the concentration of power in the market. 

![Composite of Nicola Willis, supermarket signs and groceries.](https://media.rnztools.nz/rnz/image/upload/s--c7N7Tpc3--/ar_16:10,c_fill,f_auto,g_auto,q_auto,w_1050/v1789693719/4JI3WTN_willis_supermarkets_jpg?_a=BACCd2AD)

 Photo: RNZ 

### 09:30 How a new charity aims to level the playing field when it comes to cancer treatment

![Image from Equitable Oncology](https://media.rnztools.nz/rnz/image/upload/s--xbXbtV9B--/ar_16:10,c_fill,f_auto,g_auto,q_auto,w_1050/v1790702627/4JHIACG_Equitable_Oncology_Hero_Image_jpg?_a=BACCd2AD)

 Photo: Supplied 

A new Kiwi charity launched this morning is taking on one of the biggest challenges in cancer care: how to make new treatments more affordable and accessible to the people who need them. [Equitable Oncology](https://www.equitableoncology.com/) aims to bring together researchers, clinicians, healthcare providers, industry, philanthropists, governments, patients and advocacy organisations - so affordability and access to cancer treatment is considered alongside scientific and clinical development right from the outset. The new charity says inequity often begins much earlier than the point at which a treatment reaches a patient. Its first clinical programme is K5K, a potential cancer treatment using immunotherapy. The programme is preparing for first-in-human clinical trials once funding is secured, with a stated target treatment cost of less than US$5,000 per course and a design intended to remain stable at temperatures above 40 degrees Celsius. Christine Gill is the Chief Executive of Equitable Oncology.

### 09:45 Australia: Websites hacked, rates up, strangulation 'epidemic'

![NEW YORK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 24: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese speaks at the 80th session of the UN’s General Assembly (UNGA) on September 24, 2025 in New York City. Rosenfeld/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by Alexi J. Rosenfeld / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP)](https://media.rnztools.nz/rnz/image/upload/s--NkHMCYVr--/ar_16:10,c_fill,f_auto,g_auto,q_auto,w_1050/v1758769744/4K0IPX1_AFP__20250925__2237213396__v1__HighRes__WorldLeadersGatherForThe80thSessionOfTheUnit_jpg?_a=BACCd2AD)

(File) Since PM Anthony Albanese revealed at last week's UN General Assembly that AI agents had hacked a government website, cybersecurity in the public sector has been beefed up. Photo: AFP / Getty Images / Alexi J Rosenfeld 

Australia correspondent Karen Middleton looks at the stepping up of cybersecurity for all public-sector websites that's followed revelations AI agents had infiltrated a site containing Medicare data. Open AI has offered a formal apology. Rates are up again, with the Reserve Bank pushing the OCR up to 4.6%. Australian doctors have warned women engaging in strangulation during sex are dramatically increasing their risk of stroke or death, the trial of a former police officer accused of killing his former lover and his new boyfriend is dominating headlines and it was a devastating grand-final loss in the AFL for the Fremantle Dockers.

*Karen Middleton is a political correspondent based in Canberra*

### 10:05 What doctor-turned-author Adam Kay wants you to know about hospitals at Christmas

![](https://media.rnztools.nz/rnz/image/upload/s--TSO3aPGI--/ar_16:10,c_fill,f_auto,g_auto,q_auto,w_1050/v1742503992/4KA7CNE_adam_kay_jpeg?_a=BACCd2AD)

 Photo: 

When British comedian, author, and former junior doctor Adam Kay's book *This Is Going to Hurt* was released nearly a decade ago it became a publishing and television phenomenon. He [last joined us on Nine to Noon in 2024](https://www.rnz.co.nz/national/programmes/ninetonoon/audio/2018936158/doctor-turned-comedian-adam-kay-on-finding-the-funny-in-a-job-he-found-toxic), and much of the conversation centred on his extraordinary transition from medicine to comedy and writing, and on the experiences that shaped This Is Going to Hurt and his follow up book *Undoctored*. He's returning to New Zealand later this year with *Twas the Nightshift Before Christmas*, a festive live show combining new stand-up, Christmas songs and stories from his time working in hospitals over the festive period. It's a celebration of the doctors, nurses and other healthcare workers who keep working while most of us are at home celebrating. Adam's also published his first crime novel, *A Particularly Nasty Case*, and continued to develop a career that's taken him a long way from the hospital wards. You can find more details about his New Zealand shows [here](https://www.bohmpresents.com/current-events/show/adam-kay-3).

### 10:35 Book review: Quentin Johnson on the Aubrey–Maturin series by Patrick O’Brian

The cleaning report price percentiles will be used for the chart. The draft also notes that home prototypes are kept in the fridge for seven days, while industrial products use a deposit film and flow-wrap with a twelve-month ambient shelf life. Salted Butter is defined as cultured butterfat and salt with no added oil.

Raspberry spread is fruit, sugar and lemon cooked down. Yeast extract contains barley malt extract and vegetable concentrate. Peanut spread contains peanuts and vegetable fat stabiliser. Mixed sheet is two of each. Allergen and facility statements are included. Nutrition figures are calculated not assayed. Use by heating softens the spread for pantry or toast. The pack contains eight stamps at 80 g for $5.00 on a card sheet with release film. Retailer margin is assumed at 35% leaving Stamp $3.25. Manufacturing cost is assumed at $1.50.

The $1.75 retailer margin leaves roughly $1.25 for film, card, freight and contribution. The $1.50 manufacturing cost assumption belongs in operations rather than product. The first ninety days will be a cautious launch preview with all assumptions explicitly marked and no locked distribution claims. Manufacturer details are still needed before writing the operations, information and jingle sections. I will check the wait status now.

I will also check whether the diagrams directory has appeared. To prevent transparency rendering issues, I will flatten RGBA images onto a solid background with PIL before embedding them in the PDF.

All images will be flattened to RGB on a white background before embedding, including the process and ERD diagrams. Captions will wrap naturally using Paragraph with KeepTogether, and images will scale to fit their frame width. Long URLs will wrap inside paragraphs rather than overflow fixed-height boxes.

I will insert zero-width spaces into URLs in the paragraph XML so reportlab can wrap them naturally. Images are non-splitting flowables, so they will push to the next page if space is tight; that gap is acceptable.

KeepTogether will be applied only to the image and its caption, not to the preceding paragraph. A long paragraph followed by a tall image risks pushing the paragraph onto the next page and leaving a large white gap.

Chart height is confirmed at 440 points, fitting comfortably within the available frame. The process diagram will be capped at 460 points so it does not overflow a page, scaling down if it exceeds that limit. Wide Mermaid exports will be handled by scaling to content width and then clamping height. The cover page will have no header or footer.

Later pages will use a thin purple rule with "STAMP" in small caps on the left and the page number on the right, avoiding any box. The color palette is fixed: purple #E24BFF, ink #3B0764, text #1A1024, muted #5C4A6E, and white paper. The cover is full purple; the interior stays clean with purple headings on white pages for chart contrast.

The nine PDF sections will be titled Executive summary, Product, Market, Competitors, Customer and brand, Marketing, Operations, Information, and First 90 days. The final section will be labeled Information to match the plan. The word-count script will split copy.md by ## headings and exclude figure blocks from prose counts.

A simple whitespace split will count prose words, since regex splitting on URLs produces too many fragments.

Markdown bold markers will be stripped before counting so they do not glue words together. URLs will remain as single words rather than being removed.

The dependent files are not ready yet. I will draft the build script and copy that does not depend on them, then wait.

I will write the PDF builder and a copy template with honest placeholder sections. I will not run the build until the dependent files exist.

I am drafting the full copy now, counting words with a Python one-liner. The executive summary will be 200 words. I have started with a description of STAMP: peel-and-press toast spreads on food-safe release film.

The copy now covers pantry storage, the target buyer, and the New Zealand breakfast spreads market. The 2022–2025 revenue figures show about 24% growth, with premium spreads outpacing value. A jar is described as a shared tub.

The copy now contrasts jars with stamps. A stamp is a single portion that travels without a knife or fridge. The $5.00 sheet price sits above the 90th percentile of branded spreads. The extra cost covers the film and card. No existing spread name describes a peel-and-press format. The gap is the format itself, not another jar.

The Product section will list four flavours: Salted Butter, Raspberry, Yeast extract, and Peanut.

Single-flavour sheets hold eight 10 g stamps. Mixed sheets hold two of each flavour. Every sheet costs $5.00 NZD and weighs 80 g net. The price per 100 g is $6.25 NZD.

Salted Butter is a shelf-stable spread. It uses cultured butterfat and salt with no added oil. It contains milk.

The home prototype is a 78 g unsalted butter disc with 2 g salt, shaped and eaten from the fridge within seven days. It only tests flavour and the peel-and-press gesture, not the final product.

Raspberry is a cooked paste of raspberries, caster sugar, and lemon juice reduced until thick enough to hold a disc. The home batch starts with 120 g of fruit and finishes at 80 g. The industrial disc uses that same ratio at 10 g. The label states 150 g of raspberries per 100 g because of the cooking.

Raspberry contains no major allergen.

Yeast extract is a proprietary paste, not Marmite or Vegemite. The home prototype mixes yeast extract, tomato paste, black treacle, and salt. The sold formula uses 80% yeast extract, 15.5% barley malt extract, 2.5% salt, and vegetable concentrate. Barley malt extract means the stamp contains gluten.

Peanut is roasted peanuts ground with salt. The home batch uses 85 g peanuts and 1.5 g salt, portioned before the oil separates.

The sold Peanut disc uses 96% roasted peanuts, 2.3% vegetable fat as a hard-fat stabiliser, and 1.7% salt. The stabiliser prevents oil separation across the twelve-month shelf life.

Every sheet is made in a facility that handles milk and peanuts. Mixed sheets therefore carry milk, gluten, and peanuts.

Nutrition figures on pack backs are calculated from these proportions and published composition tables. They are not laboratory assays, and this plan does not present them as tested.

The industrial step is identical for every flavour.

The industrial process deposits a 10 g disc onto release film, cuts it, nests eight in a card sheet, and flow-wraps. A stamp that fails the weight check or will not release is rejected; only a sealed sheet claims twelve months at ambient temperature.

The four-step user guide keeps the sheet in a pantry, peels one stamp off the release film, presses it onto hot toast, and waits briefly so residual heat spreads the spread across the slice.

I will avoid marketing claims such as gluten-free, organic, low-sugar, or better-for-you.

The Market section will draw from the source cleaning report.

The Market section will use the cleaned report numbers. Revenue is $275 million in 2022, $305.3 million in 2023, $319.0 million in 2024, and $341.4 million in 2025. Unit sales are 32,820, 36,346, 37,995, and 40,236 thousand. The category splits into Value $36.1–39.1 million, Standard $150.6–188.9 million, and Premium $88.3–113.4 million. The 10th percentile is $1.46 per 100 g, the median is $2.15, the 75th percentile is $2.77, and the 90th

The premium price is justified by category growth and faster premium expansion, not by targeting a shrinking tier. Stamp sits to the right of the main branded jar cluster on the chart. The goal is not to be the cheapest jar but to charge for a decided portion. Standard remains the largest tier, so ordinary jars still dominate the market; that is the competitive set, not a reason to copy the jar. I will use "million NZD" instead of "thousands". I am now drafting the Competitors section.

The Competitors section names three ordinary jars: Fix & Fogg Smooth Peanut Butter, Pic's Smooth Peanut Butter, and Nutella Hazelnut Spread. Their prices per 100 g are $1.60, $2.05, and $2.25 NZD. All were opened on 30 September 2026. I will not claim these are the only prices in the country.

The stamp is priced at roughly $0.63 per breakfast, while a jar holds about 38 to 75 portions for the same $5.00. The comparison is not a race to the lowest price per 100 g; a jar wins that race. The stamp exists for the morning when the jar is the wrong object: no knife, no shared tub, and no fridge butter. I will not claim Pic's is gluten-free as a Stamp comparison.

I will avoid marketing claims from the competitor pages. I can quote Pic's instruction to use a knife and stir, but I will not adopt any health claims. Fix & Fogg is a peanut jar; Stamp's peanut disc adds a stabiliser so it holds for twelve months. I will not overclaim quality superiority. The Customer and Brand section is next.

The brand mark is the word STAMP in light purple on dark purple. There is no symbol. The pack front for Salted Butter shows the flavour name, the word spread, a line drawing, and the phrase Peel. Press. Toast. The social ad uses the same line on a purple field. One line of ad copy is Peel. Press. Toast. The buyer is not a household stocking a pantry with the cheapest jar.

The buyer is a busy person who wants a single breakfast portion without carrying a heavy jar. Marketing will use Instagram and short video to show the peel-and-press gesture, with no wellness language or health claims. The jingle will run on podcasts, and three podcast names will be listed once the lyrics are ready.

The three podcast names are The Detail, The Front Page, and Nine to Noon. The Detail is a short RNZ explainer. The Front Page is the NZ Herald daily news podcast. Nine to Noon is an RNZ weekday morning programme.

The jingle is planned for short podcast spots on New Zealand shows. The three names are candidates whose pages were opened, not confirmed placements. No listener numbers will be invented.

The $1.50 manufacturing cost is an assumption unless the manufacturer provides a price. Distribution is not yet decided, so no supermarket is selected for the first ninety days. A trial batch will test deposit weight and film release before any sheet is offered for sale. Instagram is the first public channel using the existing ad, and one podcast test spot is requested rather than a national buy. No retailer has agreed to carry the product.

I will wait to write the final copy until all facts are in place, but I can draft the build script now. I am designing it carefully so the first PDF is close to correct. I will flatten images with PIL and use reportlab Image with file paths to preserve quality.

The flatten function removes transparency by pasting the image onto a white background and converting it to RGB. Flattened PNGs will be saved to /tmp/stamp-pdf-images/ so reportlab can read them as file paths. Layout classes are next.

A CaptionImage flowable will wrap an image and its caption together. The image and caption will be separate flowables so the caption can wrap naturally. A figure_flowables helper will scale images to fit within maximum width and height.

A KeepTogether flowable will pair each scaled image with its caption, separated by spacers. An ImageRow class is being sketched for side-by-side layouts such as the logo, pack front, and ad. It will divide the available width into three columns with a fixed gap, drawing captions beneath each image.

The logo will sit centered above the pack and ad pair. The logo is landscape; the pack and ad are portrait. Equal columns would squeeze the wide wordmark vertically. A caption under the logo will explain that the mark is the word STAMP.

The ImageRow flowable scales each image to fit its column width and maximum height, wraps the caption, and stores the layout for drawing. The draw method will align images to the top of the row.

items.content:
Writing the build script and drafting copy to /tmp for word counting.

Drafting copy.md once the missing pieces are in hand. The prose will be a clear student business plan: short sentences, concrete numbers, and no marketing fluff or AI-style vocabulary.

Drafting the executive summary for STAMP. Leaving placeholder markers for the operations and information sections until the missing files arrive.

Fleshing out the product description with pantry storage, no knife or jar, and a target buyer who wants flavour without kitchen equipment. Adding the New Zealand spreads market data: about $275 million in 2022 and $341 million in 2025, roughly 24% growth.

Premium spreads grew faster than value spreads. The category is expanding beyond the cheapest jars.

A stamp is one portion in a sheet priced at $5.00 NZD for 80 g. That equals $6.25 per 100 g. This sits above the 90th percentile of branded spreads at $5.19 per 100 g.

Stamp is a format, not another jar. The 154 spread names in the file describe jars, so none describe a peel-and-press portion. The launch line has four flavours: Salted Butter, Raspberry, Yeast extract, and Peanut. A single-flavour sheet holds eight stamps; a mixed sheet holds two of each. Every sheet is 80 g net and $5.00 NZD on the shelf.

Salted Butter is a shelf-stable spread, not a pat of fridge butter. The sheet labels it as a spread to comply with dairy-identity standards in Australia and New Zealand. The disc uses cultured butterfat and salt at a 2:78 ratio, matching the home batch. Low moisture keeps the sealed disc stable in a pantry while still softening on hot toast. No oil is added, and the stamp contains milk.

The home prototype is softened unsalted butter beaten with salt, pressed onto baking paper, chilled until it holds, and eaten within seven days. It tests flavour and the peel-and-press gesture but is not the sold product.

Raspberry uses 120 g of raspberries, 30 g of caster sugar, and 5 g of lemon juice. The home batch is stirred until 80 g of thick paste remains. The industrial disc deposits that same cooked paste at 10 g. The label can state 150 g of raspberries per 100 g because 120 g of fruit reduces to 80 g.

Raspberry stability comes from the cooked solids and the seal, not a preservative claim. The recipe has no major allergen, though the sheet still carries the facility line.

Yeast extract is an original paste, not Marmite or Vegemite. The home prototype warms 55 g of yeast extract with 15 g of tomato paste, 8 g of black treacle, and 2 g of salt until it holds a disc.

The sold Yeast extract formula is 80% yeast extract, 15.5% barley malt extract, 2.5% salt, and 2% vegetable concentrate. Barley malt extract sits above salt in the list, so the stamp contains gluten.

Peanut uses roasted peanuts at 96%, 2.3% vegetable fat as a hard-fat stabiliser to prevent oiling off across twelve months, and 1.7% salt.

Every sheet is produced in a facility that handles milk and peanuts. The mixed sheet contains milk, gluten, and peanuts because it holds all four flavours. Nutrition figures printed on the pack backs are calculated from these proportions and published composition data, not from a laboratory assay. The plan does not treat them as tested results, and the pack does not carry a certification mark we do not hold. The industrial path is identical for every flavour.

The industrial stamping process deposits a 10 g disc onto release film, cuts it, nests eight in the card, and flow-wraps the sheet. Any stamp that fails a weight check or will not release is rejected before shipping. Only the sealed, unopened sheet claims twelve months at ambient temperature.

A single stamp is consumed in one use. The user keeps the sheet in a pantry, peels a disc off the release film, presses it onto hot toast, and waits briefly for residual heat to spread the spread across the slice.

The 2023 revenue figure is about $305 million NZD and the 2024 figure is about $319 million NZD. The 2024 total is slightly higher than the raw spreadsheet because blank revenue cells were filled during cleaning.

Unit volume rose from about 32.8 million in 2022 to about 40.2 million in 2025. Revenue grew slightly faster than unit volume, so the category was not selling more packs at a flat price.

The tier chart shows Standard as the largest segment, moving from about $151 million NZD to about $189 million NZD. Premium spreads grew fastest, rising from about $88 million NZD to about $113 million NZD. Value spreads moved from about $36 million NZD to about $39 million NZD.

Standard spreads added the most revenue dollars. A new product priced like a value jar would enter the slow part of the category. Pricing above ordinary jars targets a tier that grew, though it does not capture the bulk of the money. The chart supports this honest limit. The price-per-100-g figure for branded spreads will show where $6.25 sits.

The 168 branded spreads range from $1.46 to $5.19 per 100 g. Fix & Fogg's median is about $2.65 per 100 g. The stamp sheet costs $6.25 per 100 g, above the 90th percentile. That price covers the film and card, not a premium inside the jar.

The 154 spread names describe jars, not portions. The market can afford a high per-100-g price in a few SKUs, but it has not yet filled this format. That is the opening, not proof that buyers will pay $6.25 for a disc. The first ninety days will not pretend they will.

Distribution is not yet decided, so the chart will not be turned into a sales forecast.

Three competitor jars were priced from New World pages opened on 30 September 2026. The non-Club+ price is used as the shelf price; Club+ prices are noted but treated as promotional only. None of these items are peel-and-press sheets. Fix & Fogg Smooth Peanut Butter is a 750 g jar.

Fix & Fogg Smooth Peanut Butter is hi-oleic peanuts and New Zealand sea salt. The non-Club+ shelf price is $11.99 NZD, or $1.60 per 100 g. The Club+ price on that page was $9.49 NZD.

Pic's Smooth Peanut Butter is a 380 g jar priced at $7.79 NZD non-Club+, or $2.05 per 100 g. The Club+ price shown was $6.79 NZD.

Pic's own page tells buyers to use a table knife and stir, because oil rises and salt sinks. That jar behaviour is exactly what Stamp avoids.

Nutella Hazelnut Spread is a 400 g jar priced at $8.99 NZD non-Club+, or $2.25 per 100 g. The Club+ price shown was $7.29 NZD. It is a hazelnut and cocoa spread in an open tub that still needs a spoon.

The Nutella page is https://www.newworld.co.nz/shop/product/5001098_ea_000nw?name=nutella-hazelnut-spread.

Stamp costs $6.25 NZD per 100 g. Fix & Fogg's 750 g jar is $1.60 per 100 g. Pic's 380 g jar is $2.05 per 100 g. Nutella's 400 g jar is $2.25 per 100 g. The eight-stamp sheet costs $5.00 NZD. One 10 g portion is about $0.63 NZD at the shelf. A buyer with a knife and cupboard should buy the jar.

The sheet targets buyers who do not want to carry a 380 g or 750 g jar to eat just 10 g. The format difference is the whole comparison. Fix & Fogg, Pic's, and Nutella are jars. Stamp is a disc on release film in a card. The peanut disc is not a claim to beat those brands on taste. The yeast-extract disc is not a jar of Vegemite or Marmite under another name. Those jar brands stay jars.

The customer is the person whose toast happens away from a full kitchen.

The customer is a flat-dweller with one knife already in the sink, a desk, and a hall. They are not shopping for the cheapest spread per 100 g. They want a pre-decided portion that needs no wash-up and can sit in a pantry until opened.

The mark is the word STAMP in capitals. There is no symbol beside it. On the logo the field is light purple and the letters are dark purple. Flavour is type, not a second colour.

The Salted Butter pack shot shows a rounded front with the flavour name and the word spread beneath it. The line drawing of a pat on a board is meant to stop the sheet from being read as a fridge pat of butter. The bottom line is the same “Peel. Press. Toast.” advertising line. The social ad places that line under the wordmark on the light purple field, with “Toast spreads” at the foot. It makes no health claim and lists no certification.

The brand is the gesture and the name. A buyer who already eats toast can read the pack without a paragraph of explanation.

Marketing channels are Instagram and short video. The still ad shows only the word STAMP, the line Peel. Press. Toast., and nothing else fighting it. A short video must prove the gesture that a still cannot show: a hand peels a disc, presses it onto hot toast, and residual heat softens it into a layer. Flavours can be named, but Salted Butter must appear as a spread rather than a pat from the fridge.

The video avoids health claims and allergen surprises. Yeast extract and peanut are named plainly.

The jingle is for podcast audio, not the silent Instagram still.

Three New Zealand shows were opened on 30 September 2026 to pitch a short podcast spot.

No listener numbers or confirmed bookings appear on the podcast pages. The Detail is an RNZ production with Newsroom and NZ On Air support, offering a daily six-day story explanation. The Front Page is the New Zealand Herald’s daily news podcast, carrying the morning’s productivity episode.

Nine to Noon is RNZ National’s weekday morning programme with Kathryn Ryan. It targets the hours when people actually eat toast. The three podcast names are a first list, not a signed schedule. A news or interview show can carry a short produced spot between segments. If a show declines, it drops off the list. The Instagram video does not depend on any of these bookings.

The first ninety days are a making trial and a small public test. They are not a national launch. Distribution is not yet decided, so the section does not pick a supermarket, a cafe chain, or a website cart.

Three assumptions are flagged. The first is that the $1.50 NZD manufacturing cost stays in the margin sketch unless a quoted manufacturer price replaces it. Even then, that figure remains an assumption until a real invoice matches it.

The second assumption is that the first paid work is a trial batch. Its job is deposit weight and film release, not a full order.

The third assumption is that the first public move is the Instagram video and one podcast spot request. It uses the existing ad and jingle.

No buyer is assumed yet. The cleaned file shows a grown spreads category and an empty format. It does not prove anyone will pay five dollars for a sheet.

The ninety days are for testing whether the disc releases cleanly, whether the sheet survives a bag, and whether the gesture is clear on a phone screen.

The script will be counted and adjusted before writing. The process diagram must fit within the page frame. A single figure is capped at 460 points so its caption sits below it. The frame height is 746 points. A tall vertical flowchart could still make text too small.

A configurable `max-height` parameter will be added to the figure block. Charts default to 360 points. Process and ERD diagrams can scale up to 640 points. The script is now being written.

The script will exit with an error if the word count is outside the required range. It will run from any directory because paths resolve relative to the script file itself. Figure sources in the markdown are also resolved relative to the project root.

A temporary directory will hold the flattened PNGs. Reportlab reads image files at build time, so the temp files must survive until `doc.build()` returns. The cover logo will use the original RGB path rather than the white-flattened version.

The script will flatten images by compositing them onto a white background with PIL. The cover logo will stay unflattened so its purple field matches the cover. A thin purple rule will sit at the top of every body page.

The script will exclude markdown tables from the word count. It will print section counts when running. The exit code will be 1 with a stderr message if the total is out of range.

Headings are excluded from the word count because they are not prose. The standard market estimate will be stated as about $151 million to about $189 million NZD.

The script will reject any remaining TODO or WAIT placeholders with an error. The 2022 to 2025 market figures and unit counts are now rounded to the nearest million.

The script will exit with an error if copy.md still contains TODO or WAIT_FOR_INPUT placeholders. Reportlab font names are being registered as Manrope, Manrope-Med, and their weight variants.

The Manrope font family is registered with its weight variants. Italic is unavailable because the font files only contain weights, so italic styling will be avoided.

Captions will use the Medium weight at a slightly smaller size instead of italic. A test PDF will be built only after copy.md is fully complete. The process diagram will be capped at ninety percent of the page frame height.

Tall diagrams will be capped at 640 points in height. A portrait ERD scales to about 457 by 640 points, which may still be too small for readable text. The rendered pages will be inspected after building, and the diagram can be bumped up or given its own page if the text is muddy. A full page at 150 dpi renders to roughly 1240 by 1754 pixels.

The cover logo is 233 points tall, so the wordmark letters are roughly ninety points high. This should create a strong visual anchor. The purple background will make the wordmark appear to sit directly on the page. A faint white rectangle from compression is possible, and that will be checked after rendering.

A cropping step is being added to the cover logo. The wordmark will be trimmed to its ink bounding box plus padding so no image edge appears. This avoids any faint white rectangle from compression. The script will check whether numpy is installed and fall back to pure PIL if it is not.

The wordmark crop will use a simple PIL loop to find the ink bounding box. The logo is 1.8 million pixels, so memory is not a concern. The cropped image keeps its purple background, which should match the cover page and avoid any edge artifacts.

The pack image would render at 224 points tall, making a three-column row with the logo look uneven. A better layout is to place the logo full-width and short above a separate row of pack and ad images.

The logo will be centered at 280 points wide with a caption beneath it. The pack and ad images will sit side by side in a row with equal height and captions underneath each. This prevents the logo caption from floating high while the pack caption sits low.

A `width:` parameter will be added to figures, defaulting to full frame. The logo lockup will be about 320 by 178 points. Pack and ad images will each be roughly 200 points wide, yielding heights of about 267 and 250 points respectively for a balanced side-by-side row.

The customer section will follow the PLAN.md instruction to place each figure beside the paragraph that uses it. The prose will introduce the buyer and mark first, then show the logo figure. The pack and ad images will sit side by side in a row beneath their shared paragraph.

The customer section will use three stacked paragraphs instead of a single combined one. The logo sits first with its own paragraph. The pack image follows with its own paragraph. A shared paragraph then introduces the ad line, and the pack and ad images sit side by side in a row beneath it. Each figure stays beside the paragraph that uses it. The two-column row will be about 246 points wide.

The pack image will be capped at 240 points tall, scaling to about 180 points wide. The ad image will scale to about 192 points wide. Both will sit centered in their columns with side margins. The logo lockup is fixed at 340 by 189 points. Page balance will be checked during rendering and adjusted if needed. A word counter and section counts will be written to stdout. A forbidden phrase check is also being considered.

I will not auto-fail on words like "gluten-free" or "organic" because the copy correctly negates them. I will also avoid "healthy". Next I will write the script and draft copy to /tmp, count words, adjust, and wait for the remaining inputs.

The operations section will cite manufacturer.md for the factory name, location, contact, and URL. The sheet-making process will follow the task diagram exactly, with no assumptions. The script will be data-driven from copy.md so layout code stays untouched unless rendering fails. A safety check will warn if any required image is missing. Body text starts at topMargin and the onPage header draws in the margin area to avoid collision. The cover template may use different margins.

The cover page will use a custom BaseDocTemplate with two frames: one for the cover centered on the full page, and one for the body text. The body frame will sit inset by 48 points on all sides. showBoundary is set to zero so no debug boxes appear. The cover story will begin with a NextPageTemplate switch to the body template, followed by a vertical spacer and the centered logo flowable.

The cover story now appends the subtitle, name, and date paragraphs with exact vertical spacing before a page break. A custom Wordmark Flowable class is being defined to render the transparent wordmark centered on the cover.

The Wordmark Flowable now scales the image to a fixed width and centers it with mask='auto'. The cover layout is being pinned to roughly 434 points from the top of the page, accounting for the top padding, spacer, wordmark height, and text spacing.

Body paragraphs will be left-aligned rather than justified to prevent rivers and overflow. Each paragraph gets 8 points of spaceAfter, with 2 points before the first paragraph after a heading. Paragraph splitting is enabled, and hyphenation is left off.

Sections will be split into two to four paragraphs each so pages do not look like walls and page breaks fall cleanly. Figures will sit 6 points above and 12 points below their preceding paragraph. A quick height check confirms the chart and paragraph fit comfortably within the frame.

To prevent LayoutError, figures will be capped at frame height minus 80 points so they always fit alone. A CondPageBreak of about 280 points will precede charts to avoid starting them with too little space. The caption and image will stay together via KeepTogether.

The cover will include "Business plan" for identification. I verified that "stamps" is the correct plural for the discs, not "stamp". I will check for spelling issues by extracting text from the PDF with pdftotext.

The build script will verify that all required image paths exist and are non-empty before generating the PDF. It will exit immediately if any source file is missing, preventing a broken document with blank spots.

I will draft the copy in /tmp and keep it there until all three waiting sections are filled. The build script will check for WAIT_FOR_INPUT placeholders and refuse to compile if any remain. I will run the word counter after the final draft is complete.

Caption text is now finalized. Each figure will state a clear conclusion: the tier chart compares growth rates, the price chart places the sheet beyond the 90th percentile, the logo asserts it is only the word STAMP, the pack shows the word spread beneath the flavour name, and the ad gives one instruction: Peel. Press. Toast.

The process diagram caption will state that a stamp failing weight or release is rejected before shipping. The ERD caption will note it links reorders to flavour and rejections to batch, but cannot record medical effects. I am now writing the build script, importing ReportLab enums and styles, setting the document subject, and defining page templates.

The cover will be a solid purple rectangle. The body header will place the word STAMP on the left and the page number with the date on the right, using Manrope 8.5.

The body page template now includes horizontal divider lines at the top and bottom margins. The frame is set to 744 points tall with a 10-point gap above the header line.

The header line is now fixed at 810 points, the footer line at 38 points, and the frame sits 46 points from the page top with a 50-point bottom margin. The cover frame uses 40-point padding on all sides.

A custom CoverPage Flowable will draw the cover in fixed positions to avoid flowable layout issues. The background fills the entire page, and the frame only manages text flow.

The CoverPage Flowable will fill the entire cover frame. Inside draw(), the wordmark will be centered horizontally and placed at 48 percent of the frame height. The "Business plan" subtitle, name, and date will sit below it.

The cover text will sit 36 points below the wordmark image. It will use Manrope-Semi 13 for the subtitle, Manrope-Bold 20 for the name, and Manrope 12 for the date. The frame origin is bottom-left.

The cover layout is being recalculated for optical centering. The wordmark image will be roughly 115 points tall. The text group below it totals about 236 points including gaps. These measurements will be computed dynamically inside the draw() method to keep the cover visually balanced.

The cover text group will be vertically centered using the formula (frame height - 236) / 2 - 10, with a small visual adjustment for canvas baseline. The cover will contain only the wordmark, subtitle, name, and date; no extra product claims. I am now writing build_pdf.py and the draft copy to /tmp/stamp-draft.md.

The build script will be written in the workspace and the draft copy via shell heredoc. The script will use UTF-8 encoding, include a one-command docstring, and exit with code 1 or 2 if the word count check fails before generating the PDF.

The PDF will be written to a temporary file first. It will only be renamed to the final path after the build succeeds. This prevents a stale or broken document from remaining if the process fails. I will also handle images that use CMYK or palette color modes.

All source images are PNGs, so palette and transparency handling is straightforward. The ERD and process diagrams will be flattened to white backgrounds. Narrower figures will be centered with `hAlign='CENTER'` on the RLImage objects.

A custom FigureBlock flowable will scale images to fit the frame width and height. Captions will be centered beneath each figure rather than left-aligned.

The FigureBlock flowable computes its scaled image dimensions and wraps the caption to match the image width. It then sets the block width to the larger of the image and caption widths, and its total height to the image height plus a small gap plus the caption height.

Caption text will be left-aligned within each figure block and centered beneath it. Captions will wrap to the image width or frame width, whichever is smaller, to prevent overflow.

An ImageRow flowable will handle multi-column layouts. Each column gets an equal width, images scale to fit that width and maximum height, and captions sit directly below each image. The row height will be the tallest image plus a small gap plus the caption height.

The ImageRow flowable will top-align each image and place its caption directly beneath it. The row height will be the tallest combined image-and-caption pair in that column, preventing text from spilling into the next flowable.

A partial preview PDF will be built in /tmp from the draft copy and available images to catch layout bugs before the other files arrive. The final document will not be written until all required inputs exist. Figure 02 and figure 03 will be used, omitting figure 01.

The prose will describe the tier chart's conclusion without referencing figure 01, since that image is excluded. The draft will note that spreads rose smoothly across sixteen quarters while cereals moved around them, pointing readers to the visible chart for the price-tier comparison.

The draft will cite annual totals from the cleaning report prose rather than figure 02, which shows tier bars. The tier caption and prose will supply the exact figures. Figure 03's dashed line sits near $6.25 with mass to its left, so its caption is accurate. The document will note 168 SKUs as the cleaning report states. Everything is ready to write.

The marketing section will use a placeholder for the jingle. Competitor prices are being double-checked against fetched pages, starting with Fix & Fogg Smooth Peanut Butter at $11.99 per 750g or $1.60 per 100g.

Fix & Fogg Smooth Peanut Butter is $1.27 per 100 g under the Club+ promotion. Pic's Smooth 380 g is $2.05 per 100 g Non-Club+ and $1.79 per 100 g under the same promotion. Nutella 400 g is $2.25 per 100 g Non-Club+ and $1.82 per 100 g, with no Club+ label on that second price.

The Fix & Fogg price description will be revised to avoid implying a Club+ label. The page snippet shows "Non-Club+ Price" next to the higher amount, but the lower price is only marked "Limit 12 assorted" without an explicit "Club+" title. The draft will state that the New World page listed a non-Club+ price of $11.99 NZD for 750 g ($1.60 per 100 g) and also showed $9.49 NZD ($1.27 per 100 g).

The draft will avoid claiming the lower Fix & Fogg price is Club+ unless the page explicitly labels it. New World prices may vary by store, so the URL alone will be cited rather than asserting a specific location.

The podcast page for The Detail has been confirmed at the RNZ website.

The Front Page podcast page is confirmed on the NZ Herald website. The Nine to Noon page is confirmed on RNZ. The draft will not claim audience size or that the podcasts have been booked. The $1.50 price stack will be placed in the operations section, while the product section will state the $5.00 shelf price.

The operations section will list the $1.50 manufacturer cost as a labeled assumption, not a confirmed quote. The manufacturer file may contain an actual price that will be quoted separately if it arrives. The first 90 days references will rely on this assumption. The prose stays honest and within claim rules. "Pantry-stable" will not be used as a health claim.

The "even cover" claim is permitted by the product specification and PLAN.md. The draft will describe the heat softening the spread into a layer rather than asserting an even cover. Allergen information is clear.

The draft will cite Pic's instruction to stir with a knife as format evidence rather than copying its marketing language. Claims about nutrition, certification marks, yeast versus marmite, gluten from barley, facility allergen handling, and salted butter composition are all confirmed as stated.

Fix & Fogg ingredients will be described as peanuts and salt to show the jar contents without making a claim. Competitor descriptions will stay brief. A unit test for word count will be added to the script. The preview PDF will be tested with long unbreakable strings such as competitor URLs to catch layout issues. No fabricated manufacturer data will be included in any generated document.

The script will remain simple and omit a preview flag. Layout bugs will be caught by a separate /tmp test script that imports the PDF-building functions directly. The module will expose parse_copy, count_prose, build(story), and main.

Section word counts will be logged for every band. The script only enforces the total target, so I will check each section manually and edit copy if it falls outside its band. Target words will be verified with the counter. The full draft will be written at /tmp/stamp-copy-draft.md first, then finalized into business-plan/copy.md once all required inputs are ready.

I will poll for the remaining files after writing and read them immediately if they appear. The PDF script will be comprehensive but not bloated. I am fixing a layout bug in FigureBlock.draw where the wrapped paragraph must be stored and recomputed if wrap is called with different widths. I will also use canvas.drawImage with mask='auto' to handle flattened RGB images correctly.

The cover page template will be registered first in BaseDocTemplate so the document opens with the cover. Manrope at 8.5 points is registered before the page templates draw.

The document structure is now clear: the cover template draws the front page, then a NextPageTemplate('body') switches to the body template before the first PageBreak. The BaseDocTemplate title and author properties will be set to "STAMP business plan" and "Jacob".

I will set the PDF title and author on both the cover and body pages to prevent overwrites. I am adding an `assert_no_placeholder` check to catch any remaining placeholders before building the document. The manufacturer file will be read as loose markdown. I am also preparing to measure the jingle duration with ffprobe.

args.CodeContent: #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Build business-plan/Stamp-business-plan.pdf from business-plan/copy.md. Prose words are the section paragraphs only. Headings, figure captions, image paths, and markdown tables are not counted. The build stops if that count is outside 1,500–2,500. """ from __future__ import annotations import re import sys import tempfile from pathlib import Path from PIL import Image as PILImage from reportlab.lib.colors import HexColor, white from reportlab.lib.enums import TA_CENTER, TA_LEFT from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import A4 from reportlab.lib.styles import ParagraphStyle from reportlab.pdfbase import pdfmetrics from reportlab.pdfbase.ttfonts import TTFont from reportlab.platypus import ( BaseDocTemplate, CondPageBreak, Flowable, Frame, HRFlowable, KeepTogether, NextPageTemplate, PageBreak, PageTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, ) HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent ROOT = HERE.parent COPY_PATH = HERE / "copy.md" OUT_PATH = HERE / "Stamp-business-plan.pdf" FONT_DIR = ROOT / "brand" / "fonts" PURPLE = HexColor("#E24BFF") INK = HexColor("#3B0764") TEXT = HexColor("#1A1024") MUTED = HexColor("#4A3560") BG_PURPLE = (226, 75, 255) MIN_WORDS = 1500 MAX_WORDS = 2500 LEFT = 46 RIGHT = 46 FRAME_BOTTOM = 52 FRAME_TOP = 48 REQUIRED_INPUTS = [ "audio/stamp-jingle.mp3", "audio/lyrics.txt", "diagrams/manufacturer.md", "diagrams/process.png", "diagrams/erd.png", "diagrams/process-notes.md", "diagrams/information-notes.md", ] def register_fonts() -> None: pdfmetrics.registerFont(TTFont("Manrope", str(FONT_DIR / "Manrope-400.ttf"))) pdfmetrics.registerFont(TTFont("Manrope-Med", str(FONT_DIR / "Manrope-500.ttf"))) pdfmetrics.registerFont(TTFont("Manrope-Semi", str(FONT_DIR / "Manrope-600.ttf"))) pdfmetrics.registerFont(TTFont("Manrope-Bold", str(FONT_DIR / "Manrope-700.ttf"))) pdfmetrics.registerFontFamily( "Manrope", normal="Manrope", bold="Manrope-Bold", italic="Manrope-Med", boldItalic="Manrope-Semi", ) def styles() -> dict[str, ParagraphStyle]: return { "h": ParagraphStyle( "h", fontName="Manrope-Bold", fontSize=15, leading=18, textColor=INK, spaceBefore=2, spaceAfter=2, alignment=TA_LEFT, ), "body": ParagraphStyle( "body", fontName="Manrope", fontSize=10.5, leading=14.4, textColor=TEXT, spaceBefore=0, spaceAfter=8, alignment=TA_LEFT, ), "cap": ParagraphStyle( "cap", fontName="Manrope-Med", fontSize=8.5, leading=11, textColor=INK, spaceBefore=0, spaceAfter=0, alignment=TA_LEFT, ), "cover_kicker": ParagraphStyle( "cover_kicker", fontName="Manrope-Semi", fontSize=13, leading=16, textColor=INK, alignment=TA_CENTER, ), } def parse_copy(text: str) -> list[dict]: """Return sections of prose, figure, and row blocks.""" sections: list[dict] = [] current: dict | None = None prose: list[str] = [] lines = text.splitlines() index = 0 def flush() -> None: nonlocal prose if current is None: prose = [] return chunk = "\n".join(prose).strip() prose = [] if chunk: current["blocks"].append(("prose", chunk)) while index < len(lines): line = lines[index] stripped = line.strip() if stripped.startswith("## "): flush() current = {"title": stripped[3:].strip(), "blocks": []} sections.append(current) index += 1 continue if stripped == ":::figure": flush() if current is None: raise SystemExit("figure block before any section") index += 1 fields: dict[str, str] = {} while index < len(lines) and lines[index].strip() != ":::": raw = lines[index].strip() if ":" in raw: key, value = raw.split(":", 1) fields[key.strip()] = value.strip() index += 1 current["blocks"].append(("figure", fields)) index += 1 continue if stripped == ":::row": flush() if current is None: raise SystemExit("row block before any section") index += 1 items: list[dict[str, str]] = [] pending: dict[str, str] = {} while index < len(lines) and lines[index].strip() != ":::": raw = lines[index].strip() if raw.startswith("src:"): if pending.get("src") and pending.get("caption"): items.append(pending) pending = {"src": raw.split(":", 1)[1].strip()} elif raw.startswith("caption:"): pending["caption"] = raw.split(":", 1)[1].strip() index += 1 if pending.get("src") and pending.get("caption"): items.append(pending) current["blocks"].append(("row", items)) index += 1 continue if stripped.startswith("# "): index += 1 continue prose.append(line) index += 1 flush() return sections def prose_word_counts(sections: list[dict]) -> tuple[int, dict[str, int]]: per: dict[str, int] = {} total = 0 for section in sections: parts: list[str] = [] for block in section["blocks"]: if block[0] != "prose": continue for line in block[1].splitlines(): if line.strip().startswith("|"): continue parts.append(line) raw = "\n".join(parts) raw = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]+)\]\([^)]+\)", r"\1", raw) raw = raw.replace("**", "").replace("*", "").replace("`", "") words = raw.split() per[section["title"]] = len(words) total += len(words) return total, per def xml_text(text: str) -> str: text = text.replace("&", "&").replace("<", "<").replace(">", ">") def soften(match: re.Match[str]) -> str: return match.group(0).replace("/", "/​") text = re.sub(r"https?://[^\s<]+", soften, text) text = re.sub(r"\*\*([^*]+)\*\*", r"\1", text) return text def prepare_image(src: Path, dest: Path) -> tuple[int, int]: image = PILImage.open(src).convert("RGBA") base = PILImage.new("RGBA", image.size, (255, 255, 255, 255)) flat = PILImage.alpha_composite(base, image).convert("RGB") flat.save(dest, "PNG") return flat.size def knock_out_wordmark(src: Path, dest: Path) -> tuple[int, int]: image = PILImage.open(src).convert("RGBA") pixels = image.load() width, height = image.size min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y = width, height, 0, 0 found = False for y in range(height): for x in range(width): red, green, blue, _alpha = pixels[x, y] if ( abs(red - BG_PURPLE[0]) > 18 or abs(green - BG_PURPLE[1]) > 18 or abs(blue - BG_PURPLE[2]) > 18 ): pixels[x, y] = (red, green, blue, 255) found = True min_x = min(min_x, x) min_y = min(min_y, y) max_x = max(max_x, x) max_y = max(max_y, y) else: pixels[x, y] = (red, green, blue, 0) if not found: raise SystemExit(f"no wordmark ink found in {src}") pad = 20 box = ( max(0, min_x - pad), max(0, min_y - pad), min(width, max_x + 1 + pad), min(height, max_y + 1 + pad), ) crop = image.crop(box) crop.save(dest, "PNG") return crop.size class CoverPage(Flowable): def __init__(self, path: str, width_px: int, height_px: int): super().__init__() self.path = path self.px_w = width_px self.px_h = height_px def wrap(self, avail_width, avail_height): self.avail_width = avail_width self.avail_height = avail_height return avail_width, avail_height def draw(self): draw_w = min(self.avail_width - 10, 450) draw_h = draw_w * self.px_h / self.px_w block_h = draw_h + 28 + 16 + 30 + 18 bottom = max(24, (self.avail_height - block_h) / 2 - 12) name_y = bottom + 18 kicker_y = name_y + 30 image_y = kicker_y + 28 image_x = (self.avail_width - draw_w) / 2 self.canv.drawImage( self.path, image_x, image_y, draw_w, draw_h, mask="auto", preserveAspectRatio=True, ) self.canv.setFillColor(INK) self.canv.setFont("Manrope-Semi", 13) self.canv.drawCentredString(self.avail_width / 2, kicker_y, "Business plan") self.canv.setFont("Manrope-Bold", 22) self.canv.drawCentredString(self.avail_width / 2, name_y, "Jacob") self.canv.setFont("Manrope", 12) self.canv.drawCentredString(self.avail_width / 2, bottom, "30 September 2026") class FigureBlock(Flowable): def __init__(self, path: str, caption: str, max_height: float, pref_width: float | None): super().__init__() self.path = path self.caption = caption self.max_height = max_height self.pref_width = pref_width with PILImage.open(path) as image: self.px_w, self.px_h = image.size def wrap(self, avail_width, avail_height): max_w = avail_width if self.pref_width is None else min(avail_width, self.pref_width) scale = min(max_w / self.px_w, self.max_height / self.px_h) self.draw_w = self.px_w * scale self.draw_h = self.px_h * scale self.paragraph = Paragraph(xml_text(self.caption), styles()["cap"]) _cw, self.cap_h = self.paragraph.wrap(self.draw_w, 800) self.avail_width = avail_width self.height = self.draw_h + 5 + self.cap_h return avail_width, self.height def draw(self): image_x = (self.avail_width - self.draw_w) / 2 self.canv.drawImage( self.path, image_x, self.cap_h + 5, self.draw_w, self.draw_h, mask="auto", preserveAspectRatio=True, ) self.paragraph.drawOn(self.canv, image_x, 0) class ImageRow(Flowable): def __init__(self, items: list[tuple[str, str]], max_height: float): super().__init__() self.items = items self.max_height = max_height self.sizes = [] for path, _caption in items: with PILImage.open(path) as image: self.sizes.append(image.size) def wrap(self, avail_width, avail_height): count = len(self.items) gap = 12 col_w = (avail_width - gap * (count - 1)) / count self.cols = [] row_h = 0 cap_style = styles()["cap"] for (path, caption), (px_w, px_h) in zip(self.items, self.sizes): scale = min(col_w / px_w, self.max_height / px_h) draw_w = px_w * scale draw_h = px_h * scale paragraph = Paragraph(xml_text(caption), cap_style) _cw, cap_h = paragraph.wrap(col_w, 800) self.cols.append((path, draw_w, draw_h, paragraph, cap_h, col_w)) row_h = max(row_h, draw_h + 5 + cap_h) self.gap = gap self.avail_width = avail_width self.row_h = row_h return avail_width, row_h def draw(self): x = 0 for path, draw_w, draw_h, paragraph, cap_h, col_w in self.cols: image_x = x + (col_w - draw_w) / 2 image_y = self.row_h - draw_h self.canv.drawImage( path, image_x, image_y, draw_w, draw_h, mask="auto", preserveAspectRatio=True, ) paragraph.drawOn(self.canv, x, image_y - 5 - cap_h) x += col_w + self.gap def draw_cover(canvas, _doc) -> None: canvas.saveState() canvas.setFillColor(PURPLE) canvas.rect(0, 0, A4[0], A4[1], stroke=0, fill=1) canvas.setTitle("STAMP business plan") canvas.setAuthor("Jacob") canvas.restoreState() def draw_body(canvas, doc) -> None: canvas.saveState() canvas.setFillColor(white) canvas.rect(0, 0, A4[0], A4[1], stroke=0, fill=1) canvas.setStrokeColor(PURPLE) canvas.setLineWidth(1.5) canvas.line(LEFT, A4[1] - 34, A4[0] - RIGHT, A4[1] - 34) canvas.line(LEFT, 40, A4[0] - RIGHT, 40) canvas.setFillColor(INK) canvas.setFont("Manrope-Semi", 8.5) canvas.drawString(LEFT, 24, "STAMP") canvas.setFont("Manrope", 8.5) canvas.drawRightString(A4[0] - RIGHT, 24, f"{doc.page}") canvas.setTitle("STAMP business plan") canvas.setAuthor("Jacob") canvas.restoreState() def resolve_src(src: str) -> Path: path = Path(src) if not path.is_absolute(): path = ROOT / path if not path.is_file() or path.stat().st_size == 0: raise SystemExit(f"missing or empty image: {path}") return path def check_inputs(copy_text: str) -> None: if "WAIT_FOR_INPUT" in copy_text or "TODO" in copy_text: raise SystemExit("copy.md still has placeholders; PDF not written") missing = [] for relative in REQUIRED_INPUTS: path = ROOT / relative if not path.is_file() or path.stat().st_size == 0: missing.append(relative) if missing: raise SystemExit("missing inputs, PDF not written: " + ", ".join(missing)) def build_story(sections: list[dict], work: Path, wordmark: tuple[str, int, int]) -> list: style = styles() story: list = [] path, px_w, px_h = wordmark story.append(CoverPage(path, px_w, px_h)) story.append(NextPageTemplate("body")) story.append(PageBreak()) for section_index, section in enumerate(sections): if section_index: story.append(CondPageBreak(88)) story.append(Paragraph(xml_text(section["title"]), style["h"])) story.append( HRFlowable( width="100%", thickness=1.25, color=PURPLE, spaceBefore=1, spaceAfter=8, ) ) for kind, payload in section["blocks"]: if kind == "prose": paragraphs = [part.strip() for part in payload.split("\n\n") if part.strip()] for part in paragraphs: story.append(Paragraph(xml_text(part), style["body"])) continue if kind == "figure": src = resolve_src(payload["src"]) caption = payload.get("caption", "").strip() if not caption: raise SystemExit(f"figure missing a caption: {src}") flat = work / f"fig-{len(list(work.iterdir()))}.png" prepare_image(src, flat) pref = float(payload["width"]) if payload.get("width") else None max_h = float(payload["max-height"]) if payload.get("max-height") else 430 story.append(Spacer(1, 3)) story.append(FigureBlock(str(flat), caption, max_h, pref)) story.append(Spacer(1, 10)) continue if kind == "row": prepared = [] for item in payload: src = resolve_src(item["src"]) flat = work / f"row-{len(list(work.iterdir()))}.png" prepare_image(src, flat) prepared.append((str(flat), item["caption"])) max_h = 250 story.append(Spacer(1, 3)) story.append(ImageRow(prepared, max_h)) story.append(Spacer(1, 10)) return story def main() -> int: if not COPY_PATH.is_file() or COPY_PATH.stat().st_size == 0: raise SystemExit(f"missing copy: {COPY_PATH}") copy_text = COPY_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8") check_inputs(copy_text) sections = parse_copy(copy_text) if not sections: raise SystemExit("copy.md has no sections") total, per_section = prose_word_counts(sections) for title, count in per_section.items(): print(f"{count:4d} {title}") print(f"{total:4d} TOTAL") if total < MIN_WORDS or total > MAX_WORDS: print( f"error: prose word count {total} is outside {MIN_WORDS}–{MAX_WORDS}", file=sys.stderr, ) return 1 register_fonts() with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="stamp-plan-") as temporary: work = Path(temporary) mark = work / "wordmark.png" px_w, px_h = knock_out_wordmark(ROOT / "brand" / "logo.png", mark) story = build_story(sections, work, (str(mark), px_w, px_h)) tmp_out = work / "plan.pdf" frame_h = A4[1] - FRAME_BOTTOM - FRAME_TOP frame_w = A4[0] - LEFT - RIGHT document = BaseDocTemplate( str(tmp_out), pagesize=A4, title="STAMP business plan", author="Jacob", ) document.addPageTemplates( [ PageTemplate( id="cover", frames=[ Frame( 36, 36, A4[0] - 72, A4[1] - 72, id="cover", showBoundary=0, ) ], onPage=draw_cover, ), PageTemplate( id="body", frames=[ Frame( LEFT, FRAME_BOTTOM, frame_w, frame_h, id="body", showBoundary=0, ) ], onPage=draw_body, ), ] ) document.build(story) OUT_PATH.write_bytes(tmp_out.read_bytes()) print(f"wrote {OUT_PATH}") return 0 if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main())

count {total} is outside {MIN_WORDS}–{MAX_WORDS}", file=sys.stderr, ) return 1 register_fonts() with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="stamp-plan-") as temporary: work = Path(temporary) mark = work items.content:
A bug was found in FigureBlock.wrap and ImageRow.

styles() is called during wrap and creates new ParagraphStyle objects each time. KeepTogether is imported but unused.

FigureBlock captions risk overflowing narrow columns. Charts are full-width and the logo has a width attribute. The wordmark knockout is slow but acceptable. check_inputs requires all files even for word counts, so prose_word_counts will be called directly for draft counts.

The figure parser splits on the first colon to handle captions containing colons. Captions must remain single-line in the source file, though they can wrap in the PDF. A potential bug was spotted in ImageRow caption positioning: the paragraph y-coordinate is calculated from the bottom of the paragraph.

The caption positioning math checks out. The tallest column's caption sits flush against the row bottom with no overflow. Shorter images leave empty whitespace below their captions, which is acceptable.

The caption paragraph aligns flush with the image edges. Paragraph styles have no padding, so captions will not overflow their columns. URLs in captions are not supported. Draft copy will be written and word counts tallied next.

Draft copy will be written to /tmp first for iteration. A small counter script will tally words without running main. ImageRow captions are kept short to prevent overflow.

Draft copy is being written now. A page-break spacing issue was noted: an 88-point conditional break before the first section may leave too little room for the executive summary header. The layout will be checked by building a temporary PDF once the stable sections are counted.

A temporary preview PDF will be built from the existing sections to check layout, using a dummy placeholder for the operations section. The draft copy will be finalized next, omitting the operations, information, and jingle sentence sections.

args.CodeContent:
# STAMP

## Executive summary

Stamp is a sheet of peel-and-press spreads for toast. Each stamp is a 10 g disc on a food-safe release film, nested in a printed card. You peel one off and press it onto hot toast. The heat softens it into a layer. There is no knife and no open jar. An unopened sheet is made to keep for 12 months in a pantry. The home recipes that test flavour are not that product. They stay in the fridge and are eaten within 7 days.

The buyer is someone who eats toast away from a full kitchen. That might be a flat, an office, a hall, or a bag. They want a decided portion of flavour without carrying a jar or washing a knife.

Cleaned New Zealand breakfast sales put spreads revenue at about $275 million NZD in 2022 and about $341 million NZD in 2025. That is about 24% growth. Premium spreads grew faster than value spreads, from about $88 million NZD to about $113 million NZD, while value moved only from about $36 million NZD to about $39 million NZD. The category got larger, and the growth was not confined to the cheapest jars.

A jar is a shared tub. It needs a knife and somewhere to set the open pack. A stamp is one portion, already the right size, and it travels in a sheet. The sheet is $5.00 NZD for 80 g, which is $6.25 NZD per 100 g. That sits above the 90th percentile of branded spreads in the cleaned file, $5.19 NZD per 100 g. The gap is the film and the card, which a jar does not carry. None of the 154 spread names describes a portion or a peel-and-press product. Stamp is a different format, not another jar.

## Product

The launch line is four flavours: Salted Butter, Raspberry, Yeast extract, and Peanut. A single-flavour sheet holds eight stamps of one flavour. A mixed sheet holds two of each. Every sheet is 80 g net and $5.00 NZD on the shelf, so every sheet is $6.25 NZD per 100 g. One stamp is 10 g, about $0.63 NZD of that shelf price.

Salted Butter is a shelf-stable butter spread, not a pat of fridge butter. The word butter on its own is a dairy-identity standard in Australia and New Zealand, so the sheet shows the flavour name and then the word spread. The sold disc is cultured butterfat and salt, in the same ratio as the home batch: 2 g of salt to 78 g of fat. No oil is added. Moisture is kept low enough that the sealed disc stays stable in a pantry and still softens on hot toast. The stamp contains milk. The home prototype is softened unsalted butter beaten with that salt, pressed onto baking paper, and eaten from the fridge within 7 days. It tests the flavour and the gesture. It is not what we sell.

Raspberry is fruit, sugar, and lemon, cooked down. The home batch starts with 120 g of raspberries, 30 g of caster sugar, and 5 g of lemon juice, and it is stirred until 80 g of thick paste remains. The industrial disc uses that same cook, deposited at 10 g. The label says it is made with 150 g of raspberries per 100 g because 120 g of fruit was reduced to 80 g. The paste holds its shape from the solids in the cook and from the seal, not from a preservative claim. The recipe itself names no major allergen. The sheet still carries the facility line.

Yeast extract is our own paste. It is not Marmite and it is not Vegemite, and those names do not appear on the pack. The home prototype warms 55 g of yeast extract with 15 g of tomato paste, 8 g of black treacle, and 2 g of salt until it holds a disc. The sold formula is the one on the label: yeast extract 80%, barley malt extract 15.5%, salt 2.5%, and vegetable concentrate 2%. The salt share matches the home batch. Barley malt extract means the stamp contains gluten from barley.

Peanut contains peanuts. The home paste is 85 g of roasted peanuts and 1.5 g of fine salt, ground until firm and portioned before the oil separates. The sold disc is roasted peanuts 96%, vegetable fat 2.3% as a hard-fat stabiliser, and salt 1.7%. The stabiliser is there so the disc does not oil off across 12 months.

Every sheet, including Raspberry and the mixed sheet, is made in a facility that handles milk and peanuts. The mixed sheet contains milk, gluten, and peanuts because it contains all four flavours. Nutrition figures on the pack backs are calculated from these proportions and from published composition figures. They are not a laboratory assay, and this plan does not treat them as tested results. The pack carries no certification mark.

The making step is the same shape for every flavour. Deposit 10 g, give or take 0.5 g, onto release film. Cut the disc. Nest eight discs in the card. Flow-wrap the sheet. If the weight check fails, or the film will not release, that stamp is rejected. It does not ship inside a sheet that looks finished. Only the sealed, unopened sheet claims 12 months at ambient temperature.

Use is four moves. Keep the sheet in a pantry. Peel a stamp off the release film. Press it onto hot toast. Wait a few seconds so the residual heat lays the spread across the slice.

## Market

The figures here come from the cleaned sales file, not from the raw spreadsheet totals. Money is in million NZD. The source column was stored in thousands of NZD, and it has been scaled so the unit is written out.

Spreads revenue was about $275 million NZD in 2022, about $305 million NZD in 2023, about $319 million NZD in 2024, and about $341 million NZD in 2025. From 2022 to 2025 that is about 24% growth. The 2024 total sits a little above the raw column because blank revenue cells in that year were filled during cleaning. Other years barely moved. Unit volume, counted here in millions of units rather than in the source's thousands, rose from about 32.8 million in 2022 to about 40.2 million in 2025. Revenue grew slightly faster than the number of units, so the category was not only moving more packs at a flat price.

The tier split is the sharper reading. Value spreads moved from about $36 million NZD to about $39 million NZD. Premium moved from about $88 million NZD to about $113 million NZD. Standard, still the largest tier, moved from about $151 million NZD to about $189 million NZD. Premium's rate of growth was faster than value's. Standard added the most dollars. A new sheet priced like a value jar would be walking into the slow part of the category. A sheet priced above ordinary jars is at least pointed at a tier that grew. It is not pointed at the bulk of the money, which is still standard jars. That is the limit on what the bars can justify.

:::figure
src: data/figures/02-spreads-revenue-by-tier-2022-vs-2025.png
caption: Premium revenue rose faster than value revenue, and standard stayed the largest tier.
:::

Price per 100 g, for branded spreads, says where $6.25 sits. Across 168 branded SKUs the 10th percentile is $1.46 NZD, the median is $2.15 NZD, the 75th percentile is $2.77 NZD, and the 90th percentile is $5.19 NZD. The far tail is manuka honey, not peanut butter or jam. Fix & Fogg's SKU medians in the cleaned file sit around $2.65 NZD per 100 g. The Stamp sheet is $6.25 NZD per 100 g, above that 90th percentile. The price is the portion film and the card. It is not a claim that the spread inside is a dearer version of the median jar.

:::figure
src: data/figures/03-branded-spreads-price-per-100g.png
caption: At $6.25 NZD per 100 g, the Stamp sheet sits to the right of almost every branded spread in this chart.
:::

The cleaned file holds 41 spread brands and 154 spread names. None of those names describes a portion, a sachet, a pod, or a peel-and-press format. The category can carry a high price per 100 g in a few SKUs, and it has grown, but it has not already filled this format. That is the opening. It is not evidence that a buyer will pay $5.00 NZD for a sheet. Distribution is not decided, so these charts are not a sales forecast.

## Competitors

Three jars were priced from New World pages opened on 30 September 2026. Each page shows a non-Club+ price and a second, lower figure. The non-Club+ price is the shelf price used here. The lower figure is recorded because it was on the page, and it is not treated as the standing price. None of the three is a peel-and-press sheet.

Fix & Fogg Smooth Peanut Butter is a 750 g jar. The non-Club+ price was $11.99 NZD, which the page states as $1.60 NZD per 100 g. The same page also showed $9.49 NZD ($1.27 NZD per 100 g). The jar is peanuts and salt. You open it, you take what you want with a knife, and you put it back. The page is https://www.newworld.co.nz/shop/product/5267959_ea_000nw?name=fix--fogg-smooth-peanut-butter

Pic's Smooth Peanut Butter is a 380 g jar. The non-Club+ price was $7.79 NZD, stated as $2.05 NZD per 100 g. The page also showed $6.79 NZD ($1.79 NZD per 100 g). The copy on that page tells the buyer to take a sturdy table knife and stir, because the oil rises and the salt sinks. That is the jar behaviour a stamp is built not to need. The page is https://www.newworld.co.nz/shop/product/5019876_ea_000nw?name=pic%27s-smooth-peanut-butter

Nutella Hazelnut Spread is a 400 g jar. The non-Club+ price was $8.99 NZD, stated as $2.25 NZD per 100 g. The page also showed $7.29 NZD ($1.82 NZD per 100 g). It is a hazelnut and cocoa spread aimed at toast, and it still needs a knife and an open tub. The page is https://www.newworld.co.nz/shop/product/5001098_ea_000nw?name=nutella-hazelnut-spread

Set beside a Stamp sheet, the jars are much cheaper per 100 g. Stamp is $6.25 NZD per 100 g. The Fix & Fogg jar on this page is $1.60, the Pic's jar is $2.05, and the Nutella jar is $2.25, all NZD per 100 g. A jar also holds many breakfasts in one container. Eight stamps cost $5.00 NZD, so one 10 g breakfast is about $0.63 NZD at the shelf. The buyer who has a knife and a cupboard should buy the jar. The buyer who does not want to carry 380 g or 750 g in order to eat 10 g is the one the sheet is for.

The format is the whole comparison. Fix & Fogg, Pic's, and Nutella are jars. Stamp is a disc on release film in a card. You peel it and press it. You do not stir it, and you do not dip a knife into a shared tub. The peanut disc is not a claim to beat Pic's or Fix & Fogg on taste. The yeast-extract disc is not a jar of Vegemite or Marmite under another name. Those products stay jars.

## Customer and brand

The buyer is the person whose toast happens away from a full kitchen. A flat with the one knife already in the sink, a desk, a hall, a bag on the way somewhere else. They are not shopping for the lowest price per 100 g. They want a portion that is already decided, that does not need a wash-up, and that can live in a pantry until the sheet is opened.

The mark is the word STAMP in capitals. There is no symbol beside it. On the logo the field is light purple and the letters are dark purple. Flavour is set in type. It does not get a second colour.

:::figure
src: brand/logo.png
width: 340
caption: The mark is the word STAMP and nothing else. There is no symbol to learn.
:::

The pack shot in this plan is the Salted Butter sheet. The front carries the flavour name, the word spread underneath, and a line drawing. The word spread is doing a job. It stops the sheet being read as a fridge pat of butter. The line along the bottom is the same line as the advertising.

The social still is the light purple field, the same wordmark, and one line of copy: “Peel. Press. Toast.” It does not make a health claim, and it does not show a certification mark. A person who already eats toast can read the ad without a paragraph of explanation. The pack and the ad below are the two fronts a buyer actually sees.

:::row
src: brand/explorations/flavours/butter.png
caption: The Salted Butter front puts the word spread under the flavour name, so it is not a fridge pat.
src: brand/ad.png
caption: The social ad has one line of instruction: Peel. Press. Toast.
:::

## Marketing

The channel is Instagram and short video. The still is the ad already drawn: the word STAMP, the line Peel. Press. Toast., and no second message fighting it. A short video has one job, which is to show the gesture a still cannot prove. A hand peels a disc, presses it onto hot toast, and the heat softens the spread into a layer. The flavours can be named on screen. Salted Butter is shown as a spread, not as a pat cut from a fridge block. The video does not say the product treats anything, and it does not say it is better for you, low-sugar, organic, or gluten-free. Yeast extract is named as yeast extract. Peanut is named as peanut, so the allergen is not a surprise in the caption.
